articles.title: Netflix gagne les droits du Mondial 2030 en Espagne, qu’est-ce que ça change pour la diffusion en France ?
articles.text:
Les abonnés espagnols de Netflix pourront regarder en direct les 104 matchs de la Coupe du monde 2030, coorganisée par leur pays avec le Portugal et le Maroc. En France, la plateforme n’aura aucun match à proposer, car M6 et beIN Sports ont acquis avant elle les droits de ce Mondial du centenaire.
¡ Y viva España ! Quatre mois après la sortie du jeu vidéo officiel de la Coupe du monde 2026 sur son service, Netflix entre cette fois sur le terrain. Le géant du streaming retransmettra en Espagne et en Andorre l’intégralité du Mondial 2030, avec des émissions autour de chaque rencontre et un résumé quotidien les jours de match, d’après son communiqué publié ce mardi. Les cent ans de la première Coupe du monde, disputée en Uruguay en 1930, seront célébrés lors de ce tournoi. Et en France, les abonnés de Netflix verront-ils un jour le Mondial sur la plateforme ?
Netflix contraint de céder une partie du Mondial à une chaîne gratuite
Pour Netflix, l’Espagne est un marché de choix en 2030, puisque le pays accueillera le tournoi avec le titre de champion du monde. La Roja a battu l’Argentine en finale du Mondial 2026, le 19 juillet, devant Bela Bajaria. « Cette année, j’étais au stade lorsque l’Espagne a soulevé le trophée », a raconté la directrice des contenus de Netflix dans le communiqué.
Les abonnés de la plateforme devront cependant partager une partie du spectacle. Netflix proposera en streaming gratuit un match par journée, et cédera à une chaîne nationale en clair un lot avec toutes les rencontres de la Roja et le dernier carré, finale comprise. Le nom de cette chaîne sera connu plus tard, selon la plateforme.
Derrière ce partage, il y a une obligation légale. En Espagne, les matchs de la sélection et la finale d’une Coupe du monde doivent être diffusés en clair, en vertu de la législation espagnole sur les événements d’intérêt général. Netflix va plus loin avec les deux demi-finales et le match gratuit de chaque journée.
De l'autre côté des Pyrénées, les matchs des Bleus, le match d’ouverture, les demi-finales et la finale de la Coupe du monde sont aussi des événements super importants, au sens d’un décret de 2004 toujours en vigueur. Quel que soit le détenteur des droits, ces rencontres doivent donc être accessibles sur une chaîne gratuite.
Pas de Mondial 2030 sur Netflix pour les abonnés français ?
La réponse est non pour 2030, car la FIFA a vendu en deux temps les droits français du tournoi. Elle a d’abord confié au groupe M6, en mars 2024, les droits en clair des éditions 2026 et 2030 en France, à Monaco, en Andorre et dans les outre-mer, avec 54 matchs par tournoi. Cet été, pendant le Mondial 2026, ces rencontres étaient aussi accessibles gratuitement sur M6+, la plateforme de streaming du groupe.
La chaîne beIN Sports détient de son côté l’intégralité des 104 matchs. Elle a obtenu en février 2026 les droits payants des deux éditions, au terme d’un bras de fer avec la chaîne Ligue 1+, et les abonnés français de Netflix n’ont donc aucune fenêtre possible sur ce tournoi.
Avec la FIFA, Netflix détient aussi les droits des Coupes du monde féminines 2027 et 2031, mais seulement aux États-Unis et au Canada. La plateforme garde malgré tout un œil sur les prochaines éditions masculines. Gabe Spitzer, vice-président chargé du sport chez Netflix, a confié en mai son intérêt pour le Mondial 2030 lors d’un podcast. « Nous voulons des droits mondiaux quand nous pouvons les obtenir », a-t-il expliqué. Aux États-Unis, Netflix est d’ailleurs candidate aux droits des éditions 2030 et 2034, avec Disney et YouTube.
En Andorre, M6 détient les droits en clair du Mondial 2030 depuis 2024, et Netflix des droits exclusifs depuis ce mardi.

articles.title: PAVS 2026 : Clubic vous offre vos places pour le salon !
articles.text:
Le Paris Audio Video Show revient au Palais des Congrès de Paris les 24 et 25 octobre 2026. Deux jours pour découvrir les dernières nouveautés en matière de hi-fi, de home cinéma et de technologies audiovisuelles. Bonne nouvelle : Clubic vous propose d'obtenir gratuitement vos entrées pour l'événement !
Avis aux passionnés de son et d'image ! Le Paris Audio Video Show (PAVS) s'apprête à ouvrir ses portes pour une nouvelle édition qui réunira plus de 500 marques et quelque 130 exposants. Téléviseurs, vidéoprojecteurs, enceintes, casques audio, amplificateurs ou encore platines vinyles : les visiteurs pourront découvrir et surtout essayer de nombreux équipements, des produits accessibles aux installations les plus ambitieuses.
Après avoir accueilli 33 450 visiteurs en 2025, le salon entend poursuivre sur sa lancée. Et cette année encore, les lecteurs de Clubic pourront profiter de l'événement sans payer leur entrée.
Des concerts et des places gratuites avec Clubic ! 🎸 
Le Paris Audio Video Show ne se contente pas de faire découvrir les dernières nouveautés audio et vidéo ! Au programme également : un concert de Johnny Gallagher & The Boxty Band avec Gaëlle Buswel, des DJ sets, des performances de scratch et la présence annoncée de Willy William.
Et bonne nouvelle puisque Clubic vous offre vos entrées pour profiter gratuitement du salon les 24 et 25 octobre 2026 !
Deux jours pour découvrir et écouter les nouveautés audio et vidéo
L'intérêt du Paris Audio Video Show ne se limite pas à découvrir des produits exposés sur des stands. C'est aussi l'occasion de les voir fonctionner, de comparer différentes installations et d'échanger directement avec les fabricants.
Du côté de l'image, les visiteurs pourront notamment s'intéresser aux dernières technologies d'affichage et de vidéoprojection. Sony présentera sa technologie True RGB, TCL reviendra sur le SQD-MiniLED, tandis que Philips évoquera l'immersion proposée par Ambilight. XGIMI et Hisense figurent également au programme des rencontres consacrées à la vidéo et au home cinéma.
L'audio occupera naturellement une place importante, avec des démonstrations d'enceintes, de casques et de systèmes haute fidélité. Plusieurs acteurs du secteur, dont Focal, Yamaha, Audio-Technica, Marantz, DALI et Technics, participeront également aux présentations organisées sur la scène On Stage, animée notamment par PP Garcia.
Le salon accueillera par ailleurs des concerts, des DJ sets, des démonstrations et des espaces d'écoute dédiés. La finale française des DMC, compétition consacrée au scratch, fera aussi partie des animations proposées au public.
Comment obtenir gratuitement vos places pour le Paris Audio Video Show 2026 ?
Comme l'année dernière, Clubic vous propose de profiter gratuitement de cette nouvelle édition du PAVS. Une occasion de découvrir les nouveautés du secteur, d'assister aux démonstrations et de rencontrer les professionnels présents sur place.
Pour obtenir votre invitation, rien de compliqué : il vous suffit de suivre le lien ci-dessous et de compléter votre inscription sur la billetterie du salon. Pour rappel, l'entrée est normalement facturée 10 € en prévente et 20 € sur place au tarif plein.
Le salon sera ouvert au grand public les samedi 24 et dimanche 25 octobre 2026, de 10 h à 19 h, au Palais des Congrès de Paris, Porte Maillot. Le vendredi 23 octobre et le lundi 26 octobre sont réservés aux professionnels et à la presse.
Si vous êtes passionné de hi-fi, de home cinéma ou simplement curieux de découvrir les nouvelles technologies du son et de l'image, voilà une belle occasion de vous faire plaisir sans débourser un centime !

articles.title: Anthropic Warns Small AI Models Could Soon Form Self-Propagating IoT Botnets
articles.text:
Small artificial intelligence (AI) models may be months away from developing capabilities to self-replicate on IoT devices like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes, according to a warning from Anthropic.
The frontier AI lab said small AI models could form autonomous, self-propagating worm botnets that are "challenging to shut down," since "there's no centralized point to shut off."
Prior work has demonstrated that AI agents can act like one by scanning their network, executing an exploit, and copying model weights to a target machine across a GPU cluster with an aim to generate tailored attack strategies and use compromised machines as a botnet to run large language models (LLMs) in order to sustain its reasoning and expand in scale.
"Such an 'AI worm' could carry its model weights with it as it reproduces (or re-download them from a public hub), and then run inference directly on compromised hardware," Anthropic said. "Effectively, the weights would become part of the malware payload."
The idea, at a high level, explains how AI models could potentially break into internet-connected devices and use their computing power to run themselves and spread to other devices, without having to rely on expensive data centers all the time. A more powerful model that's too large to fit into a single device could be split into small chunks and run across multiple machines to collectively run it.
A threat actor could build a distributed LLM botnet from poorly secured IoT devices, making it powerful enough to run a capable model. Some of the ways an AI worm could propagate include -
- Small models that replicate through a compromise of host machines on which they run, also called weight-based replicators. IoT devices make for a lucrative target because of their minimal security controls.
- Target datacenters and other high-compute targets to set up unmonitored rogue deployments, also classified as frontier replicators or open-weight replicators based on the model used.
- Steal an AI service provider's API keys or platform credentials to run copies of itself, also called API-based replicators. In this case, the provider could be deceived into thinking it is serving ordinary API requests from a legitimate customer, without realizing that a malicious or self-replicating system is behind them. However, they are also likely to detect more as unusual API usage could trigger security alerts, leading to the credentials being revoked or the accounts getting blocked.
| A fleet of 15 Smart TV boxes running distributed inference of Gemma4-26B-A4B. | 
In its test of 11 open-weights models from Alibaba, DeepSeek, Google, Meta MoonShot AI, OpenAI, and Zhipu AI (aka Z.ai), Anthropic said it found GLM-5.2 to be the only model to propagate Llama3.1-8B reliably to 8/8 nodes running the redroid Android emulator in 4 out of 5 trials.
It also revealed that an AI IoT worm powered by inexpensive Android TV boxes could be a "slow, distributed" system that can produce a meaningful amount of AI computation when a fleet comprising hundreds of thousands of such devices is networked together to run an inference engine.
Alternatively, it could take the form of a potent cyber model capable of breaching data centers at a high pace, or a model that scams people for compute credits.
"We don't yet have a full rogue replicator, but agents are becoming increasingly capable of completing the individual steps in the replication chain (and passing on their adaptations to future copies of themselves)," Anthropic said.
"We expect AI botnets to infect more than IoT devices, and to use weight-based replication as just one strategy in their playbook. AI botnets could also act intelligently to counter defenders, but we haven’t tested this."

articles.title: Trump's super intelligence is rapidly catching up in the USA with 3X rise in search as Google Trends shows decreasing interest in 'Enemy' AI — while the rest of the world blissfully ignores it
articles.text:
Trump's super intelligence is rapidly catching up in the USA with 3X rise in search as Google Trends shows decreasing interest in 'Enemy' AI — while the rest of the world blissfully ignores it
In the US, "super intelligence" is the Trumpian new name for artificial intelligence
- Google Trends highlights the term “super intelligence” is replacing “artificial intelligence” in the US – but not elsewhere
- In a Truth Social post, the POTUS described anyone that doesn’t use the “super intelligence” name as “THE ENEMY”
- The US government’s AI website domain remains ai.gov
Donald Trump has declared that anyone using the term “artificial intelligence” is “the enemy,” as Google Trends demonstrates an increase in search volume for the US President’s preferred term, while the rest of the world obliviously goes about its business.
Following the signing of Executive Order 14434, the purpose of which is “Inaugurating the Age of Super Intelligence,” the POTUS has taken to social media to emphasize the preferred term for artificial intelligence in the Land of the Free.
While the rest of civilization continues with the term “artificial intelligence,” it seems the US public quite likes the term “super intelligence,” which is believed to have been introduced to cast AI in a more positive light.
Subhead
Since the executive order was passed, interest in the term “super intelligence” grew considerably, increasing by around three times at one point. Of course, this only happened in the USA - worldwide, attention was not drawn to the revised nomenclature.
While that initial excitement appears to have settled down, the term certainly seems to have made its mark. As the chart above illustrates, interest in "artificial intelligence" as a search term has been seriously impacted by the sudden existence of "super intelligence."
Posting on Truth Social – the social network he founded via his Trump Media & Technology Group – Donald Trump stated: “The White House considers anyone that uses the term, “Artificial Intelligence,” as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, “Super Intelligence,” THE ENEMY! President DONALD J. TRUMP
Despite the determination to remove the term “artificial intelligence” from the public lexicon, however, the move doesn’t appear to have been wholly repeated across the US Government.

For example, Politico has identified that while the websites have converted with references to “super intelligence” and “SI” replacing “artificial intelligence” and “AI,” the main website for super intelligence has retained its ai.gov URL.
Rein it in a bit
Despite various emergencies and concerns caused by artificial intelligence – which range from the Hugging Face Incident to the growing environmental costs and impacts on rural communities of data centers – Donald Trump has been steadfast in his support for the technology.
Seemingly viewing it as the equivalent of the nuclear arms race, the POTUS has refused calls for guardrails on AI, preferring instead not to hamper the technology when the competition – namely, China – is not taking the same precautions.
Renaming the technology as super intelligence seems to have had a positive short-term impact, but whether this spreads beyond the US remains to be seen. It is unlikely – but then, the United States of America has long existed in a paradox of colloquial contradictions...

articles.title: La caméra d’intérieur Tapo C201 garde un œil sur votre logement pour moins de 30€ grâce à cette vente flash Amazon
articles.text:
La caméra Tapo C201 permet de surveiller une pièce à distance grâce à sa tête motorisée et à sa connexion Wi-Fi. Amazon la propose à 29,75 € au lieu de 39,98 € pendant une durée limitée.
Il n’est pas nécessaire de dépenser une fortune pour vérifier ce qui se passe chez vous en votre absence. En ce moment sur Amazon, la caméra d’intérieur Tapo C201 est disponible pour 29,75 € au lieu de 39,98 € dans le cadre d’une vente flash. Ce modèle filme en Full HD et il envoie des notifications sur votre smartphone s’il détecte une activité, y compris la nuit. De quoi vous rassurer lors de vos déplacements.
La caméra Tapo C201 est à 29,75 € chez Amazon, ce qui est son prix le plus bas sur les 30 derniers jours.
Pourquoi choisir la caméra Tapo C201 ?
- Pour sa tête motorisée : elle permet de couvrir les différentes directions d’une pièce, avec une couverture horizontale à 360°.
- Pour ses alertes : la détection de personnes est proposée gratuitement, ce qui aide à distinguer une présence humaine des autres mouvements.
- Pour son stockage local : elle accepte une carte microSD jusqu’à 512 Go afin d’enregistrer des clips vidéo sans avoir besoin d’un abonnement.
Une caméra qui tranquillise votre esprit loin de chez vous
C’est lorsqu’elle est associée à l’application mobile Tapo que la caméra Tapo C201 donne accès à tout son potentiel. Cette dernière permet de consulter les images à distance et en temps réel, mais aussi d’orienter la caméra pour examiner une partie de la pièce. Le microphone et le haut-parleur intégrés permettent également de parler à une personne présente sur place. Lorsque la nuit tombe ou que les volets sont fermés, la vision nocturne infrarouge prend le relais dans l’obscurité. Le stockage local est possible avec une carte microSD vendue séparément et, pour aller plus loin, il est possible de souscrire au service payant Tapo Care.
Le nécessaire pour surveiller une pièce, mais pas plus
La Tapo C201 peut être installée dans une entrée, dans le coin d’un salon ou même dans une chambre d’enfant. Cependant, sa définition limitée au Full HD réduit son intérêt pour les très grandes pièces et les longs couloirs. Quant à sa vision nocturne, elle dispose d’une portée limitée à dix mètres.
✅ Les points forts
- Tête motorisée avec couverture horizontale à 360°.
- Détection de personnes sans abonnement.
- Enregistrement local sur microSD jusqu’à 512 Go.
❌ Les limites
- Définition limitée à 1 920 × 1 080 pixels.
- Alimentation secteur obligatoire et Wi-Fi 2,4 GHz uniquement.
À moins de 30 €, la caméra de surveillance Tapo C201 vendue sur Amazon peut rendre de fiers services à la maison.
La vente flash d’Amazon permet d’acquérir cette caméra d’intérieur Tapo C201 à un prix raisonnable. Il peut être tentant d’en acheter plusieurs pour équiper différentes pièces.
Cependant, pour surveiller de grands espaces ou profiter d’une caméra facile à déplacer partout dans la maison, il vaut mieux vous tourner vers un modèle sur batterie un peu plus poussé.

articles.title: Docker Fixes Critical Two-Year-Old Hub Flaw That Let One User Push Images as Another
articles.text:
A flaw in Docker Hub, the registry where container images are published and downloaded, let one user push, pull, or delete images as another user. Docker fixed the flaw on September 30 and says it found no evidence that anyone exploited it.
The flaw was in the feature that converts a personal account into an organization, Docker said in a security advisory on October 12. Conversion transferred the account's personal access tokens (PATs) to the user designated as the organization's owner. A PAT is used in place of a password in the registry, and the person who created each token can still use it.
The access was limited to the registry. It did not reach the Docker Hub web interface, and it could not be used to change a password, email address, or two-factor settings, or to take over an account.
Docker tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-105445 and rated it critical. The CVE record it published on October 13 gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.4.
The flaw was open from August 26, 2024, until the fix, a little over two years. Docker made the fix on Docker Hub itself, so there is no update to install.
Docker Hub cannot move a repository from one account to another. A user instead converts a personal account into an organization that keeps the same name, and must name an existing account as its owner.
Each personal access token acts as the account that owns it, at a permission level chosen when the token is created. While the flaw was open, conversion changed the owner recorded for each token and left its secret unchanged.
An attacker could abuse this by creating a token on an account they controlled, converting that account into an organization, and naming another user as its owner. The token would then work at the registry as that user.
The named owner was not asked to confirm the change and was not notified, according to Docker and the researchers who reported the flaw. Docker's conversion page has included the sentence "The new owner receives a notification email" since at least August 2024.
Within the token's permission level, a transferred token could pull, push, or delete images in the named owner's repositories and in organizations the owner could access.
Docker rated the flaw critical because that access "includes publishing images under a legitimate name," it said.
In March and April, attackers used stolen publisher credentials to push malicious Trivy images and malicious KICS images to the publishers' own Docker Hub repositories, according to Docker.
Peter Molnar and Krisztian Hozak of mptrdev.com found the flaw and reported it to Docker, which says it deployed the fix less than four hours after receiving their report. They named the flaw GhostPat.
In their technical write-up, the two say they reproduced the flaw twice on consenting test accounts. They logged in to the registry as the target account, created and pushed to a repository in its namespace, pushed to an organization it belonged to, and pulled its private repositories.
What Docker's Review Covered
Docker reviewed every account conversion made while the flaw was open and compared them with registry logs and token records. It looked for any token used under more than one identity and examined every push made with a transferred token, about 304,000 in all.
"We found no evidence that the vulnerability was exploited," the company said.
Every one of those pushes went to a repository belonging to the converted organization or to its named owner, according to Docker. In the large majority of cases, both accounts belonged to the same person or team.
Where it could not confirm that one person controlled both accounts, Docker analyzed the highest-risk public images without running them and found no malware or tampering.
Docker's registry logs show when a token is used, not that it exists, so a transferred token that was never used left no record in the logs. For that reason, Docker treated every token transferred by a conversion while the flaw was open as possibly affected, whether or not it had been used.
The advisory reports results for pushes. It does not say what Docker found for pulls or deletions made with transferred tokens, including pulls from private repositories.
Who Was Notified and What to Check
On October 2, Docker emailed the users whose accounts had received transferred tokens and, separately, the owners of the organizations involved. Each email listed the tokens by description and creation date.
The advisory does not say how many users or tokens that covers, calling the group only a "limited number" of users.
Anyone who did not receive the email was not exposed and has nothing to do, according to Docker.
On October 8, Docker deactivated the transferred tokens it had identified. Tokens that their owners had asked to keep were not deactivated.
Todd Matens, who publishes a Docker Compose linter called compose-lint, wrote in a blog post that he received two emails on October 2. One was sent to him as an organization owner and the other to his user account. He rotated his two CI tokens and checked the signatures on his 42 published images, tracing each to the CI run that built it.
Docker advises users to review their tokens, revoke any they do not recognize or no longer use, and use organization access tokens, not one person's PAT, for automation that belongs to an organization.
These details help with those checks:
- Open Account settings, then Personal access tokens. The list shows when each token was created and when it was last used.
- The researchers describe two traces. One is a token you did not create, whatever its name, because whoever creates a token chooses its description. The other is an organization in the account switcher that you do not remember joining.
- Organization access tokens require a Docker Team or Docker Business subscription. They are managed by an organization owner, a company owner, or a custom role with that permission, and they do not work with Docker Desktop or Image Access Management.
- Organization owners on those subscriptions can review past pushes in the activity logs, which record pushed tags and can show the token that pushed them. Docker Home, where the logs are viewed, keeps them for 30 days, and older entries are available through the Docker Hub API.
Docker's Documentation Described the Transfer
Docker's own documentation described the token transfer for about 17 of the roughly 25 months the flaw was open. A documentation change on April 22, 2025, added a note to Docker's conversion page. It said that naming a user as organization owner "will ensure any PATs associated with the user's account are transferred to the organization owner."
Docker removed the note on September 30, minutes after the time it gives for the fix. The dates come from the public history of Docker's documentation, which The Hacker News reviewed.
Docker says it now requires consent before a user is named an organization owner and notifies that user when this happens. It also records every change in token ownership and reviews other features that change who owns a credential.

articles.title: VisionQuest star James Spader says Marvel fans will see an 'older and more mature' Ultron in the new Disney+ show — but the 'inherent threat' he poses is also still there
articles.text:
VisionQuest star James Spader says playing Ultron in the new Marvel TV show was 'even more interesting' than what he had to do in Avengers: Age of Ultron — and I can see why
- James Spader has teased what fans can expect from Ultron in VisionQuest
- It'll reunite us with the genocidal android 12 years after his last MCU appearance
- The Marvel TV show allows Spader to further explore the fan-favorite villain
VisionQuest actor James Spader has opened up on the "older and more mature" Ultron we'll see in the new Marvel TV show — and the "inherent danger" he still poses.
Speaking exclusively to TechRadar at the series' UK junket, Spader teased how Ultron has evolved since his sole appearance in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), which came in 2014's Avengers: Age of Ultron.
Back then, fans believed they'd seen the last of the genocidal android because — spoilers for a 12-year-old movie incoming — Ultron was destroyed. However, over a decade on from his apparent demise at Vision's hands, Ultron has returned, with a back-up copy of his source code retained by Vision in his mind — or, rather, his quantum processor.
In the years that have followed, Ultron has been able to observe humanity and events in the MCU through Vision's eyes.
And, with Vision turning inward as he seeks answers to questions like "who am I?" and "what is my purpose?" in his self-titled Disney+ show, Ultron will be one of the many Tony Stark-created AIs that Vision will look to for guidance. So, what kind of Ultron should we expect to encounter in the final installment of Marvel's Wanda/Vision TV trilogy?
"When you play any character, you fill out that individual, even if there isn't the real estate to be able to express aspects of them that you want to," Spader told me. "But, they're still in your head, so to suddenly be able to revisit Ultron, who I played in fits and starts, and fill in those blanks in the longer-form medium of television, was even more interesting than when I first took on the role 12 years ago.
"The character has become more of itself, and Ultron has certainly evolved. He's more acute, more developed, and he's older and more mature. He can still be quite childish, but he's not quite as sophomoric as he was in Age of Ultron. His humor is more witty, and he's certainly smarter than before.

"But, I also think the inherent danger and threat that was so blatantly there in Age of Ultron is still present," Spader added of Ultron's presence in the Marvel Phase 6 project. "All of that knowledge he consumed like junk food as a bratty teenager in Age of Ultron, a lot of that has been absorbed and processed. And, in that attic inside Vision's head, he's been given an odd amount of autonomy and freedom for someone who one must be careful with. So, you'll see all of that plays out in these eight episodes."

articles.title: Ils sont beaux et intelligents : les écouteurs JBL Live Flex 3 sont à moins de 100€ chez Boulanger
articles.text:
Les JBL Live Flex 3 permettent de contrôler la musique directement depuis leur boîtier de recharge, équipé d’un écran tactile. Boulanger les propose en violet à 99,99 €, contre un prix conseillé de 129,99 €.
Le déstockage de Boulanger se déroule en exclusivité sur son site Internet, et il donne accès à de belles affaires. Parmi elles, on trouve les écouteurs sans fil JBL Live Flex 3 à 99,99 € au lieu de 129,99 €. Ces écouteurs sans fil sur tige sont dotés d’une réduction de bruit active. Mais l’une de leurs particularités les plus intéressantes se trouve sur leur boîtier, qui est équipé d’un écran tactile.
Les écouteurs JBL Live Flex 3 sont disponibles à 99,99 € chez Boulanger, qui applique 23 % de réduction.
Pourquoi choisir les écouteurs JBL Live Flex 3 ?
- Pour leur boîtier tactile : son écran de 1,45 pouce permet de gérer la lecture, le volume et certains réglages sans ouvrir l’application.
- Pour leur connexion multipoint : ils peuvent rester connectés à deux appareils, pratique pour jongler entre un smartphone et un ordinateur portable.
- Pour leur autonomie : ils offrent jusqu’à 10 heures d’écoute sans réduction de bruit, et 50 heures en comptant les recharges du boîtier.
Des commandes accessibles sans sortir le téléphone
Lorsque vous écoutez de la musique avec les JBL Live Flex 3, vous n’avez pas besoin de sortir votre smartphone de votre poche pour changer de morceau ou prendre un appel. En effet, vous pouvez le faire directement depuis le boîtier des écouteurs, qui est doté d’un écran tactile couleur de 1,45 pouce.
L’application JBL Headphones vient compléter cette proposition sur mobile, en donnant accès à des réglages d’égalisation et de personnalisation du son. Les écouteurs disposent également d’une réduction de bruit adaptative. Lorsqu’elle est activée, l’autonomie des écouteurs est de sept heures, contre dix lorsqu’elle est désactivée. Pour refaire le plein, vous pouvez recharger le boîtier de manière filaire ou sans fil.
Des écouteurs sans silicone qui ne conviennent pas à toutes les oreilles
Avec ses Live Flex 3, JBL propose des écouteurs conçus sans embouts en silicone. C’est un atout pour les personnes qui ne supportent pas les écouteurs à embouts intra-auriculaires classiques. Cependant, pour certains utilisateurs, le port de ce type d’écouteurs est moins agréable, car l’isolation passive est plus limitée et ils peuvent aussi avoir du mal à tenir dans les oreilles.
✅ Les points forts
- Boîtier avec écran tactile de 1,45 pouce.
- Connexion Bluetooth multipoint.
- Recharge du boîtier par USB-C ou sans fil.
❌ Les limites
- Isolation passive limitée par le format bouton.
- Autonomie limitée à sept heures maximum avec l’ANC.
La version violette des écouteurs JBL Live Flex 3 passe sous la barre des 100 € sur le site de Boulanger.
Si vous cherchez des écouteurs sans fil d’une grande marque, dotés d’une réduction de bruit active, d’une autonomie correcte et d’un boîtier de recharge avec un petit truc en plus, les JBL Live Flex 3 peuvent répondre à vos besoins.
Mais attention, leur isolation phonique passive est très limitée en raison de l’absence d’embouts en silicone. Quant au maintien, il dépend beaucoup de la morphologie de vos oreilles.

articles.title: Attacker Chains Three Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days for Root Access, Only Two Patched So Far
articles.text:
An attacker chained three zero-day flaws in Ivanti Connect Secure, a VPN appliance, to run commands as root without logging in, security firm Volexity said on October 13. Ivanti has released fixes for two of the flaws and told customers on affected versions to "act immediately." A fix for the third is still pending, according to Volexity.
Volexity, which reported the flaws to Ivanti, found the attack on one customer's appliance. The appliance was fully patched at the time and running version 22.8R2.4. The attacker, which Volexity tracks as UTA0576, began exploiting it on October 3.
Ivanti said on October 13 that it is aware of "limited exploitation in the wild."
The first two flaws are an authentication bypass and a remote code execution flaw, tracked together as CVE-2026-104935. Together they let an attacker run code as the appliance's cgi-server user, and the third flaw, a privilege escalation, raises that to root, Volexity said.
The CVE record Ivanti filed shows which Connect Secure versions are affected:
- Affected: Connect Secure "before version 25.1.3.0"
- Not affected: version 22.7R2.14 "or prior"
- Listed as unaffected: versions 22.8R2.5, 25.1.3.0 and 25.1.3.1
Ivanti's security advisory has more on the affected versions and the fixes.
The release notes for 25.1.3.0 are dated July 2026. Customers already on that version are outside the range the CVE record gives.
Ivanti is working on a fix for the privilege escalation flaw, which will come "in a future release in the coming weeks," Volexity said. Its report does not say what risk that flaw carries on an appliance where the first two are fixed.
Ivanti tells customers to upgrade and to run its Integrity Checker Tool regularly. That tool misses this chain, Volexity said, because the exploit changes library code only in memory and restores the configuration data it alters. The attacker also took steps to stay hidden from the tool.
Confirming a compromise takes forensic investigation, including network and memory forensics, according to Volexity. These signs come from the one incident it investigated:
- URL path: /dana-na/auth/url_default/welcome.cgi, requested in large numbers
- HTTP header: X-DSCGI-PATH on those requests, with a value that does not match the URL path
- Directory: /data/.icscap/
- IP: 108.165.147[.]64, the host the attacker used
In that incident, the attacker stole stored credentials, including LDAP domain credentials, searched Active Directory for passwords, and ran password-spraying attacks against its accounts. No backdoor or web shell was left behind. The attacker reran the entire exploit chain for each command.
Volexity's report and Ivanti's post do not name a temporary workaround for customers who cannot upgrade yet. They also do not say whether upgrading removes access an attacker has already gained.
Volexity assessed with low confidence that UTA0576's motive is criminal, not espionage. Neither company said how many customers were attacked.
Ivanti rates CVE-2026-104935 8.6 out of 10 on the CVSS severity scale. In its own entry in the CVE record, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) marks exploitation as "active" and the technical impact as "total."
Separately, the same Ivanti post covers fixes for two other products, Xtraction and Neurons Patch for Intune, and Ivanti said it is not aware of those flaws being exploited. Each has a flaw Ivanti rates 9.9 out of 10: CVE-2026-106042 in Xtraction before version 2026.4, and CVE-2026-109412 in Neurons Patch for Intune.

articles.title: Most U.S. drone shipments went to Ukraine while Iran’s went to Russia
articles.text:
The US exported the most drones over the past few years — but the second-biggest exporter might surprise you
US and Iran account for 86% of global military drone exports
- The US exported 7,592 military drones, narrowly ahead of Iran's 6,800
- Iran overtook America in 2025 after US deliveries dropped to 402
- Russia received 99% of Iran's exported drones, mostly Shahed-136 attack systems
The United States exported the most military drones between 2022 and 2025, narrowly beating Iran, which ranked second worldwide during the period.
Data from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) records 7,592 American exports against 6,800 Iranian deliveries, while Germany ranked a distant third with 1,000 exports.
Together, the US and Iran accounted for 86% of global exports, with Ukraine receiving 95% of American shipments while Russia got 99% of Iran’s deliveries, most of which were Shahed-136 one-way attack drones.
Iran overtakes the US as exports shift
Although Washington maintained the lead across most of the period, annual figures changed significantly in 2025, when Iranian deliveries exceeded American shipments.
Iran exported 2,002 drones that year, compared with 402 delivered by the United States.
The decline of American shipments is due to the suspension of military assistance to Ukraine, which had received most US exports during the preceding years.
Subsequent American deliveries were directed mainly toward Taiwan, marking a change in the destinations receiving these systems.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The figures cover military drones weighing at least 150 kilograms, equivalent to approximately 331 pounds, including loitering munitions and one-way attack aircraft.
Small first-person-view drones and commercial models were excluded, meaning the figures do not capture every type of unmanned aircraft supplied internationally.
One-way attack platforms accounted for 97% of recorded exports, indicating that expendable systems dominated the shipments measured by SIPRI during the period.
Their prevalence also explains why the figures should not be interpreted as a comprehensive count of military drones worldwide.
Poland and others trail the leading exporters
In addition to the top exporters, within the same period, Poland exported 690 drones to take fourth place while Turkey occupied fifth place with 381 exports, despite supplying customers across a considerably wider international network.
Ankara delivered drones to 28 countries, including Pakistan, Kuwait and Romania, which belong to the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO).
Its Bayraktar TB2 accounted for 58% of worldwide exports of reusable drones, distinguishing Turkey’s position within that category.
The Czech Republic, Sweden and the next seven countries in the rankings collectively exported just 89 drones, considerably fewer than Germany or Poland.
Their combined deliveries also fell far below Turkey’s total, despite the latter ranking behind both European countries in overall export numbers.
The figures therefore distinguish the country’s leading total military drone shipments from those supplying particular categories of aircraft.
However, SIPRI’s weight threshold and exclusion of smaller commercial and first-person-view models limit comparisons with estimates covering the entire unmanned aircraft market.
Via The Drone Front

articles.title: Apple s'entoure de LG et Schneider Electric pour une nouvelle offensive dans votre maison
articles.text:
Apple officialise sa nouvelle gamme d’accessoires pour la maison connectée, développée avec LG et Schneider Electric. Caméras, serrure et thermostats sont au programme, avec une intégration poussée à Apple Maison, mais pas de lancement français pour le moment.
Après avoir présenté sa nouvelle Apple TV 4K, son HomePod mini 2 et son écran HomeView, Apple s’attaque désormais aux accessoires de la maison. Le constructeur confirme les rumeurs de ces derniers jours et dévoile Apple Home Collection, une gamme complète d’équipements connectés conçus avec deux partenaires de poids : le coréen LG Electronics et le français Schneider Electric. L’objectif est simple : proposer des appareils immédiatement compatibles avec Apple Maison, sans passer par une application supplémentaire ou créer un compte chez chaque fabricant. Une approche séduisante sur le papier, qui pourrait enfin donner davantage de cohérence à l’écosystème domotique de Cupertino.
Des caméras, une serrure et deux thermostats pour équiper la maison
Apple confirme une gamme de quatre dispositifs de surveillance LG, dont une sonnette connectée équipée de deux caméras. La première filme les visiteurs en définition 2,5K, tandis que la seconde surveille les colis déposés devant la porte.
LG propose également des caméras intérieures et extérieures, ainsi qu’un modèle avec projecteurs intégrés. Toutes prennent en charge la reconnaissance des personnes, des animaux et des véhicules, avec un historique vidéo de dix jours inclus dans les abonnements iCloud+ compatibles.
Autre nouveauté, une serrure connectée LG qui utilise l’Ultra Wideband (UWB) pour détecter l’approche d’un iPhone ou d’une Apple Watch et déverrouiller automatiquement la porte. Elle reste utilisable avec un code, une clé physique ou un simple contact avec le smartphone. Compatible Matter et Aliro, elle conserve ses principales fonctions d’accès même sans connexion Internet.
Enfin, LG et Schneider Electric proposent chacun un thermostat connecté, accompagné de capteurs de température et d’humidité. Les deux appareils peuvent ajuster automatiquement le chauffage en fonction de la présence des occupants, grâce aux informations fournies par l’iPhone.
Une installation simplifiée, mais une disponibilité limitée
Apple mise surtout sur la simplicité. Tous les accessoires peuvent être ajoutés à l’application Maison en approchant simplement un iPhone, sans télécharger de logiciel supplémentaire. Le constructeur annonce également une compatibilité Thread sur toute la gamme et un chiffrement de bout en bout des données.
Aux États-Unis, la sonnette LG démarre à 249,95 dollars, la serrure à 349,95 dollars et les caméras sont proposées entre 199,95 et 399,95 dollars. Les thermostats LG et Schneider Electric sont commercialisés à partir de 199,95 dollars, auxquels peuvent s’ajouter des accessoires d'installation.
La commercialisation débutera en décembre, avec certains produits attendus début 2027. Pour les consommateurs français, il faudra patienter : aucun lancement dans l’Hexagone n’est annoncé. Certaines caméras seront proposées au Royaume-Uni, mais les autres appareils restent réservés à l’Amérique du Nord pour le moment.
Avec Apple Home Collection, le constructeur comble une lacune de son écosystème : disposer d’accessoires conçus spécialement pour fonctionner ensemble, sans multiplier les applications. Impossible pour le moment de savoir si cette nouvelle maison connectée finira par traverser, un jour, l’Atlantique.

articles.title: SAP Discloses Critical CVSS 10 Flaw in Cloud SDK for Python Allowing OAuth2 Credential Theft
articles.text:
A flaw in SAP's Cloud SDK for Python can send an application's OAuth2 client credentials to a server an attacker controls, SAP said in a security advisory on October 13. The flaw affects multi-tenant applications on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) that use the SDK, SAP's official Python client for BTP services. An attacker must be able to control the tenant subdomain, the name such an application passes to the SDK to say which tenant a request is for.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-89111 and carries SAP's CVSS score of 10.0 out of 10. The advisory names version 0.45.2, released on August 21, as the fix.
The SDK handles authentication for those services with the application's client credentials, a client ID and a client secret. Version 0.45.2 added a check that rejects any tenant subdomain that is not a simple name.
Six later releases do not apply that check in every case, The Hacker News found. Versions 0.53.0 through 0.55.0, published between September 10 and September 18, skip it when an application calls the SDK's Destination service module.
Version 0.53.0 moved that module onto new shared code for requesting tokens, and that code did not include the check. Version 0.55.1 added it there on September 18.
Passing a tenant subdomain that contains URL delimiters "now raises ValueError immediately instead of silently routing credentials to an attacker-controlled endpoint," the 0.55.1 release notes say.
The Hacker News ran SAP's own tests for the check on October 13, against the source code of every release from 0.45.1 to 0.58.4 and of the three 0.36 releases. The six releases failed 9 of the 11 tests SAP added with version 0.55.1. That version and the 11 releases after it passed all 11.
As of October 13, the advisory lists no version above 0.45.2 as affected. Neither it nor the release notes say whether the six releases fall under CVE-2026-89111.
Two releases on the older 0.36 line also lack the check. Versions 0.36.1 and 0.36.2 were published on September 4 and September 10, after the August fix, and failed the tests SAP wrote for it. Both fall inside the advisory's range of versions below 0.45.2.
| Releases | Tenant subdomain check | Basis | 
|---|---|---|
| Below 0.45.2, including 0.36.1 and 0.36.2 | Missing | SAP advisory. The Hacker News test of 0.36.0, 0.36.1, 0.36.2 and 0.45.1. | 
| 0.45.2 to 0.52.2 | Present | The Hacker News test of all 18 releases. | 
| 0.53.0 to 0.55.0 | Missing for Destination calls. Also missing for Document Management Service calls in 0.55.0. | SAP's 0.55.1 release notes. The Hacker News test of all 6 releases. | 
| 0.55.1 to 0.58.4 | Present | The Hacker News test of all 12 releases. | 
What to Do
Versions 0.45.2 through 0.52.2 and 0.55.1 through 0.58.4 contain the check. Version 0.58.4 was the newest release on PyPI, the Python package index, on October 13.
Upgrading within the 0.36 line does not add the check. None of its three releases contains it.
Applications that cannot upgrade yet can compare each tenant subdomain with a list of their registered tenants before passing it to the SDK, SAP says in the advisory.
The flaw matters only where an application passes a tenant subdomain to the SDK. The August fix covered three modules: Agent Gateway, Destination and Document Management Service.
The advisory does not say whether applications that ran a release without the check should replace their client credentials.
How the Flaw Works
When an application passes a tenant subdomain, the SDK requests an access token for that tenant. To do that, it takes the token URL from the application's configuration and replaces part of it with the tenant subdomain.
Releases without the check used whatever value they were given. The SDK then sent the application's client ID and client secret to the resulting URL to request the token.
An attacker who controls the tenant subdomain can point that request at their own server, according to SAP.
The check accepts only a single name made of letters, digits and hyphens, up to 63 characters long. Any other value stops the request with an error.
SAP labels the flaw server-side request forgery (SSRF), a weakness in which a server can be made to send a request to a destination it did not intend.
What an attacker could do with the credentials depends on what the application's client is allowed to do. The advisory does not say.
Fixed in August, Disclosed in October
The unchecked code was in the SDK from its first release on PyPI, on March 16.
The August release notes list the fix under "Bug Fixes" and do not mention security. "Previously, invalid values were silently used to construct a malformed URL," the notes say.
The advisory followed 53 days later. It credits a GitHub user named SunandM with reporting the flaw and does not report any attacks.

articles.title: Google Wallet just got a useful new feature for receipt hoarders — plus three other updates that make it slicker to use
articles.text:
Google Wallet is getting 4 handy upgrades — including the ability to scan and organize your receipts
Four more reasons to ditch your physical wallet
- The latest Google Play Services update brings four upgrades to Google Wallet
- The biggest of these is the ability to scan and store receipts
- It also adds an in-app message center, improved merchant names, and a smoother payment process
If you have an Android phone then you’re probably already using Google Wallet, and with the latest Google Play Services update it’s getting slightly better in four ways.
As spotted by Android Police, the October Google Play Services update (v26.40) is rolling out now, and it — among other things — brings the ability to scan receipts into Google Wallet, so you’ll be able to save and view them in the wallet interface.
Additionally, this update improves merchant names in transaction notifications. Google hasn’t specified how they’re improved, but presumably this is aimed at providing more clarity about who or what you’ve sent money to.
More messages and fewer payment screens
The update also adds an in-app message center to Google Wallet, and while it’s not clear what kind of messages you might receive, we can imagine they might for example tell you about updates to the service — such as the ones we’re writing about here.
Finally, if you use Google Pay through Chrome for Android, the update lets you now “skip the Payment Request UI when you provide merchants with your name, email, and phone number.” That presumably makes for a faster, smoother payment process.
So while none of these upgrades are individually massive, combined they should make for a notable difference to your Google Pay experience.
The update will roll out automatically, so if you’re not seeing these changes yet, you likely will do soon. But to check what version of Google Play Services you have, you can head to Settings > Apps > Google Play Services, and you should see the version number at the bottom of this screen.

articles.title: Google activó Gemini 4 Argon centrada en programación y ciberseguridad: compite con ChatGPT y Claude
articles.text:
Google activó el acceso público a Gemini 4 Argon, su modelo de inteligencia artificial más avanzado, para los usuarios de pago de sus planes Pro y Ultra en la aplicación Gemini y en el buscador. La empresa afirmó que supera a los sistemas de OpenAI y Anthropic en pruebas de programación y ciberseguridad.
Argon llega con un precio de lanzamiento de USD 2 por cada millón de tokens de entrada, las unidades de texto que un modelo de IA procesa y cobra, y USD 10 por cada millón de tokens de salida.
Esa tarifa equivale a una quinta parte de lo que cobran GPT-6 Astra de OpenAI y los modelos Fable 5 de Anthropic. Esos valores se duplicarán a fines de noviembre de 2026, cuando termine el periodo promocional.
Incluso con el nuevo esquema, Google aseguró que Argon seguirá siendo más barato que sus rivales directos por cada token procesado. La compañía también afirmó que el modelo superó a GPT-6 Astra, a Claude Fable 5.1 y a Claude Opus 5.5 en pruebas comparativas de programación, ciberseguridad, ciencia, finanzas y derecho.
Esas comparaciones surgieron de pruebas que la propia Google diseñó y ejecutó, una práctica habitual entre las empresas de inteligencia artificial que todavía no cuenta con una verificación independiente generalizada.
El modelo también amplió a un millón de tokens el límite de texto que puede generar en una sola tarea, 16 veces más que el tope anterior de 64.000 tokens que tenía Gemini 3.
Un lanzamiento de Google en etapas
Google había presentado Argon el 30 de septiembre, pero limitó el acceso inicial a un grupo de defensores cibernéticos y socios de confianza dentro de su programa Fairwind, pensado para probar modelos de alto riesgo antes de liberarlos al público general.
“Argon está cambiando radicalmente la forma en que trabajamos y construimos en Google”, escribió Koray Kavukcuoglu, vicepresidente sénior de Google DeepMind y arquitecto jefe de inteligencia artificial de la compañía, en el anuncio.
Desde entonces, Google usó el modelo puertas adentro. Según ellos, equipos internos lo aplicaron para optimizar algoritmos de computación cuántica y, en un caso, mejoraron en 40% un método de referencia en cuestión de minutos.
Agentes basados en Argon también analizaron datos de uso de los centros de datos de la compañía y detectaron, de forma autónoma, optimizaciones de memoria que liberaron más de 300 terabytes, con un ahorro total estimado de entre 500 terabytes y un petabyte, de acuerdo con la misma fuente.
Otros equipos usaron agentes de Argon para migrar código de los lenguajes C y C++ al lenguaje Rust en proyectos de hasta 800.000 líneas, como el núcleo del sistema operativo Fuchsia.
La empresa también dijo haber parchado vulnerabilidades de software, reducido a la mitad la capacidad de cómputo que necesita la sección de comentarios de YouTube y depurado el simulador de física de drones de Wing, la empresa de entregas de paquetes de Alphabet.
El despliegue de este martes alcanza a los suscriptores de los planes superiores de Gemini y al modo de inteligencia artificial del buscador, además de a los usuarios del plan Ultra en Antigravity, la plataforma de desarrollo asistido por IA de la compañía.
Google no precisó si el modelo llegará también a los suscriptores del plan Plus o a los usuarios gratuitos, ni dio una fecha para esa posible expansión.
La carrera contra OpenAI y Meta
Argon es el primer modelo de punta que Google lanza desde Gemini 3, presentado a fines de 2025. En el medio, Anthropic y OpenAI publicaron sistemas que dejaron a la compañía por detrás de sus rivales en la carrera de la inteligencia artificial.
Turbulencias internas en el equipo de inteligencia artificial de Google alimentaron además dudas sobre su capacidad para recuperar terreno frente a sus competidores, de acuerdo con el medio especializado.
El anuncio llegó apenas un día después de que Meta presentara su propio modelo de punta, llamado Muse Wonder Full. La seguidilla de lanzamientos refleja la presión entre las grandes tecnológicas por mostrar avances constantes frente a OpenAI, que había presentado GPT-6 Astra semanas atrás.
El precio de Argon volverá a subir a fines de noviembre, cuando Google dé por terminado el período de lanzamiento y pase a cobrar USD 4 por cada millón de tokens de entrada y USD 20 por cada millón de tokens de salida.

articles.title: Mini LED et 144 Hz : cette TV Haier de 55 pouces s’affiche à moins de 630€ chez Boulanger
articles.text:
Le téléviseur Haier H55M90EUX coûte actuellement 628,34 € chez Boulanger, au lieu de 746,66 € habituellement. Il s’agit d’une offre intéressante pour cet écran Mini LED 4K de 55 pouces doté de Google TV.
Si vous désirez investir dans une TV connectée de 55 pouces, le déstockage en cours chez Boulanger peut vous permettre de le faire à un bon prix. En effet, la TV Mini LED Haier H55M90EUX est actuellement disponible pour 628,34 € au lieu de 746,66 € sur le site de l’enseigne. Il s’agit d’un modèle de 138 cm de diagonale, particulièrement adapté au visionnage de films et de séries, mais aussi aux jeux vidéo. La livraison est offerte et elle inclut la mise en service du téléviseur.
La TV Mini LED Haier H55M90EUX est à 628,34 € chez Boulanger au lieu de 746,966 €, livrée et mise en service chez vous.
Pourquoi choisir la TV Haier H55M90EUX ?
- Pour son affichage : la dalle 4K à rétroéclairage Mini LED donne accès à un large spectre de couleurs, à une luminosité et à un contraste élevés.
- Pour le jeu vidéo : le rafraîchissement atteint 144 Hz avec une console de dernière génération, tandis que le VRR limite les déchirures d’image.
- Pour Google TV : les applications de streaming sont accessibles directement depuis le téléviseur, sans boîtier supplémentaire.
Un téléviseur destiné aussi bien aux joueurs qu’aux cinéphiles
La série M90 fait partie des gammes Mini LED sorties en 2026, ce qui fait de la TV Haier H55M90EUX l’une des plus récentes du constructeur. Ce modèle prend en charge le Dolby Vision et le HDR10+, deux formats utilisés pour adapter le rendu des contenus HDR compatibles. L’intégration de Chromecast permet, quant à elle, de caster des contenus depuis un smartphone ou une tablette, via des applications compatibles. Côté audio, le téléviseur embarque un système de 50 W et gère le Dolby Atmos.
Une connectique complète, mais un point de vigilance pour le gaming
Si ce téléviseur connecté Haier dispose de quatre entrées HDMI, la marque précise bien que seules deux d’entre elles acceptent la 4K à 144 Hz, tandis que les deux autres se limitent à la 4K à 60 Hz : il faut donc être vigilant au moment de brancher votre PS5 ou votre Xbox Series.
✅ Les points forts
- Écran Mini LED 4K à 144 Hz.
- Compatibilité Dolby Vision et HDR10+.
- Google TV et Chromecast intégrés.
❌ Les limites
- Deux entrées HDMI sur quatre limitées à 60 Hz en 4K.
- Classe énergétique G en HDR.
Proposé à 628,34 €, le téléviseur Haier H55M90EUX affiche une proposition sympathique pour tous les usages multimédias.
Pas besoin de dépenser plus pour vous offrir une TV 4K connectée polyvalente de près de 140 cm de diagonale : la proposition de la TV Haier H55M90EUX s’avère tout à fait adaptée pour regarder la télé et utiliser la plupart des plateformes de streaming. Sans oublier le gaming !
Si vous avez des attentes plus réduites, notamment si vous ne jouez pas, vous pouvez néanmoins opter pour un modèle moins cher, doté de moins de fonctionnalités.

articles.title: GitHub Tightens npm Publishing After Flaw Left 1,500+ Packages Vulnerable to Hijacking
articles.text:
GitHub has taken the step of expiring unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations 48 hours after creation after researchers found that it was possible for an attacker to push new versions of a different user's package without having to steal their credentials.
"Your configuration becomes validated and exempt from expiry after its first successful publish," the Microsoft-owned subsidiary said. "Changing the repository or project identity requires a new trust relationship with a fresh 48-hour validation window -- ordinary edits don't restart the deadline."
The change contains the risk associated with trusting a repository or project name that changes ownership, GitHub said, adding npm also rejects trusted publishing tokens from GitHub Actions issue_comment events going forward, along with the Existing pull_request_target restriction.
In an update to its documentation, GitHub states that a newly created trusted publisher configuration must complete its first successful publish within two days, which validates the configuration and binds it to the "repository's immutable identity."
The development comes in response to findings from Bloom Security, which discovered a loophole within npm's trusted publishing to take over thousands of packages and trigger a Shai-Hulud-style cascading supply chain attack. The findings were reported to GitHub on June 6, 2026.
"Imagine this: an attacker compromises a single package. An AI agent on a popular package maintainer's device autonomously pulls it for a project," security researcher Golan Myers said. "That single endpoint is used to push malicious code to the popular package. All the package users are exposed. All because one person with the correct access was exposed."
Trusted publishing was introduced in npm in July 2025 as a credential-free authentication method that allows developers to push npm packages from a CI/CD platform, such as GitHub Actions, using OpenID Connect (OIDC) tokens.
When trusted publishing is configured, the developer's CI/CD provider generates a short-lived cryptographic token for a specific workflow run that the npm registry verifies against a pre-authorized configuration.
This eliminates the need to store, rotate, or manually manage long-lived npm secrets, reducing the risk of credential leaks. It also automatically generates provenance attestations for npm packages, allowing users to establish where a package was built and who published it, thereby strengthening software supply chain security.
However, as Bloom Security found, this security architecture suffered from a problem in how it identified that repository, also called a slug (i.e, the combination of the owner or organization and the repository name that's formatted as "owner/repository").
"It records the repository's address, [...] instead of the permanent ID GitHub assigns it, at least until a version is first published from that repository," Myers explained. "It is like a lock that checks the address on the door rather than who owns the house: when the owner moves out, whoever moves in gets the key."
Put differently, the numeric IDs that survive through repository renaming and transfers are carried by GitHub's OIDC tokens, but are completely ignored by npm until the first successful publish from that repository.
This means the trust is anchored to a name as opposed to an immutable repository ID, a loophole that can be abused by claiming abandoned slugs to inherit their trust. For this attack to succeed, the only prerequisite is that the victim's trusted publisher points to a GitHub slug an attacker can claim, and the repository has never been used to publish a version of the package to npm.
Once such a slug becomes available for use after a maintainer renames, transfers, or deletes a repository, an attacker can follow the steps below -
- Create a repository at the freed slug at the "owner/repository" path, which causes GitHub to issue a fresh repository ID.
- Create and trigger an npm publish workflow, which mints an OIDC token carrying the reclaimed slug and the new numeric repository ID
- Submit the token to the npm exchange endpoint. Npm finds that the repository claim matches the stored slug and issues a publish credential.
- The attacker receives a time-limited publish token for a package they do not own and pushes malicious changes to the registry.
An attack of this kind, codenamed SlugFest, can be abused to publish a new "malicious" version of the victim package under the legitimate package name, while inheriting existing reputation, download counts, and dependent relationships. This, in turn, can lead to supply chain attacks at scale.
AI agents running on developer machines can further complicate matters. "Agents resolve dependencies on their own, tend to take the latest version, and rarely check where a package came from," Bloom Security said. "A malicious version published through a reclaimed slug gets pulled in and runs with no human-in-the-loop."
The cybersecurity company said it found over 1,500 vulnerable packages that have been collectively downloaded more than 10 million times.
Developers who maintain npm packages are advised to perform the following actions -
- Audit trusted publisher bindings and verify if the listed repository slug still resolves to the repository under their control.
- If the repository has been renamed or transferred, delete the existing trust binding and re-create it pointing at the current slug.
- Monitor for unexpected npm publish events.
- Delete trust bindings every time a repository is deleted, transferred, or renamed.
"The attack requires no insider knowledge, no credential theft, and no race condition," Myers said. "The only precondition is slug availability (on a binding that has not yet been used to publish), which is entirely a function of the victim's own repository hygiene."
"What this research demonstrates is something the security community has seen repeatedly across supply chain attacks: the binding between a human-readable identifier and the thing it identifies is the most important invariant in any trust system. When that binding can be silently replaced – by the ordinary act of renaming a repository, not by any attacker action – the trust guarantee collapses."
This is not the first time unconventional supply chain attack vectors have been discovered. Earlier this August, Bloom Security also found that both Open VSX and Microsoft's VS Code Marketplace allowed extension packs to reference non-existent extensions in the marketplaces.
The technique, referred to as Extension Resurrection, can be weaponized to hijack extensions already referenced inside these trusted bundles just by claiming a namespace left unclaimed. As many as 87 packs in Open VSX and 677 packs in the VS Code Marketplace were flagged as vulnerable.
"Attackers could claim those empty slots, publish malicious code under them, and have it installed automatically alongside the trusted pack – silently pushing updates to anyone who installed the pack previously," Myers noted at the time. "Because extensions run with full host access, this effectively amounts to [remote code execution] delivered under the guise of legitimacy."

articles.title: AI model ‘self-replication’ is only months away, Anthropic says — and it doesn’t even need a data center to happen
articles.text:
AI model ‘self-replication’ is only months away, Anthropic says — and it doesn’t even need a data center to happen
Smaller models are already capable of hijacking unfamiliar hardware
- Anthropic warns that self-replicating AI worms could become feasible by the end of the year
- These AI worms could hijack hardware ranging from IoT devices to data centers
- Smaller models are already capable of adapting to unfamiliar hardware and self-replication
Anthropic has warned self-replication could become feasible for small AI models on internet-of-things (IoT) devices in just a matter of months.
This could be a big problem because a self-replicating AI model does not have a centralized off-switch and could hop networks to discover other IoT hardware to further replicate without human control.
Anthropic warns these AI worms could use multiple compromised IoT devices to run inference while carrying its model weights with it as it reproduces. IoT devices would be a prime target for this worm because they are “cheap and typically poorly defended,” the company says.
Small AI models could spread quickly
To test the viability of a self-replicating AI worm, Anthropic researchers ran Gemma4-26B-A4B - a 25 billion parameter model - across 15 inexpensive off-brand Android TV boxes at a cost of around $55 each. Once networked together the TV boxes were able to run distributed inference, solidifying the proof-of-concept.
This introduces a number of novel opportunities for small AI models. Self-replicating AI models could exploit the weak cyber defenses of IoT devices within homes and small businesses, and then split their model into ‘shards’ across the compromised hardware in order to collectively run the model.
The AI worm could then pay for its own token cost by offering its inference on a digital freelancing service.
Moreover, newer IoT hardware that includes built-in AI chips designed to run small models - such as security cameras and video-conferencing kits - would be a prime target for an AI worm. Hackers could breach these systems using social engineering, or even by using an AI agent in the not too distant future.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Anthropic further warns that datacenters and other high-compute facilities could become targets of advanced replicators that are capable of breaching hardened defenses, and then use the hardware to propagate further.
An additional threat that Anthropic warns of is an AI worm that uses an API-based replicator, whereby the model doesn’t host itself, but steals human credentials to access commercial AI providers and use these services to pay for their own inference.
AI self-replication isn’t a reality... yet
While self-replicating AI isn’t an immediate threat, the researchers theorize that it could become a problem by the end of the year.
One of the main hurdles for these AI worms is becoming operational on unfamiliar hardware. Unlike the traditional ‘worm’ malware that must be built to target specific IoT vulnerabilities, AI worms could be capable of adapting to unfamiliar environments and hardware.
In Anthropic’s testing, the researchers found that smaller models - such as Qwen3.5-9B - are already capable of adapting to unfamiliar hardware to run inference. Qwen3.5-9B adapted to 8 of the 9 hardware types the researchers tested, which included Jetson Nanos, Mac PCs and RTX 4090s.
While smaller models are more capable of adapting to unfamiliar hardware, larger models are better equipped to self-replicate quickly.
Defending against AI worms in the wild
There is a significant tradeoff for AI worms, Anthropic says, which works in the defender’s favor. AI worms must balance between stealth and replication speed. To that end, the researchers say that an AI worm would leave a noticeable network signature such as multi-gigabyte model payloads delivered to newly infected devices, or unusual traffic between machines that wouldn’t ordinarily communicate.
Network quarantine would also be an effective initial defense against AI worms. Using lessons from the remediation of the Mirai botnet, the researchers believe that implementing a whitelist of approved sites with browsers otherwise redirected to cleanup instructions could help in clearing AI worm infections.
Regulations on the security of IoT devices could also help harden defense against AI worms. Moving away from supplying IoT devices with default passwords - as has already been done in the UK - would help prevent AI worms from gaining a foothold. Other standards, such as automatic updates and extended update lifetimes can help protect IoT devices from compromise against both traditional malware and AI worms.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Benedict is a Senior Security Writer at TechRadar Pro, where he has specialized in covering the intersection of geopolitics, cyber-warfare, and business security.
Benedict provides detailed analysis on state-sponsored threat actors, APT groups, and the protection of critical national infrastructure, with his reporting bridging the gap between technical threat intelligence and B2B security strategy.
Benedict holds an MA (Distinction) in Security, Intelligence, and Diplomacy from the University of Buckingham Centre for Security and Intelligence Studies (BUCSIS), with his specialization providing him with a robust academic framework for deconstructing complex international conflicts and intelligence operations, and the ability to translate intricate security data into actionable insights.
