articles.title: Este es HomeView de Apple, la nueva pantalla que controla el hogar con Siri AI
articles.text:
Apple presentó HomeView, una pantalla inteligente diseñada para reunir en un solo dispositivo el control del hogar conectado, el entretenimiento y algunas funciones de comunicación. La compañía apuesta por Siri AI, su asistente de inteligencia artificial, para que los usuarios puedan buscar contenido, controlar accesorios y consultar información mediante la voz.
El equipo tiene una pantalla Liquid Retina de siete pulgadas y puede colocarse sobre una mesa o instalarse en la pared. También permite hacer videollamadas con FaceTime, reproducir música y acceder a funciones de vigilancia del hogar. Apple indicó que HomeView reconoce a las personas por su rostro y adapta el contenido para cada usuario, como mensajes, calendario y recordatorios.
Las reservas comenzaron el martes 13 de octubre y la disponibilidad en tiendas de Estados Unidos está prevista para el 13 de noviembre. HomeView no estará a la venta en la Unión Europea, porque Siri AI todavía no está disponible en iOS en esa región.
Siri AI lleva la conversación al hogar
Apple describe Siri AI como una versión más conversacional del asistente, con conocimiento general y capacidad para comprender mejor las solicitudes. En HomeView, permitirá descubrir música y controlar dispositivos inteligentes mediante comandos de voz. También podrá responder preguntas y mostrar información en pantalla.
Cuando se empareja con un dispositivo compatible con Apple Intelligence, como un iPhone, HomeView puede utilizar ciertos datos personales para dar respuestas más relevantes. Por ejemplo, Siri AI puede consultar información de aplicaciones como Calendario o Mensajes para responder a solicitudes relacionadas con la rutina de cada usuario.
El reconocimiento facial también permite que la pantalla compartida cambie de perfil según quién la esté utilizando. Así, cada persona puede acceder a su contenido sin que el dispositivo se limite a mostrar una experiencia común para toda la casa. Apple afirma que la privacidad y la seguridad son parte central del diseño.
Un centro para los dispositivos inteligentes
HomeView está pensado para controlar luces, cámaras, persianas, cerraduras y otros accesorios compatibles con Apple Home. El dispositivo puede ejecutar automatizaciones y permitir que los usuarios manejen escenas del hogar por voz.
Si se conecta un timbre compatible, las notificaciones pueden aparecer en la pantalla. Desde allí, el usuario podrá ver quién está en la puerta y comunicarse con esa persona. La pantalla también puede servir para vigilar cámaras del hogar y consultar información sobre la actividad detectada.
El producto busca ofrecer una alternativa a controlar la casa desde un iPhone o una tableta. Apple ya permite gestionar accesorios desde esos dispositivos y mediante sus altavoces HomePod, pero HomeView incorpora una pantalla dedicada a permanecer en espacios comunes de la vivienda.
Precio y disponibilidad en Europa
Apple todavía no ha publicado el precio de HomeView ni todos los detalles sobre su disponibilidad en cada mercado. La falta de una fecha para Europa está relacionada con la disponibilidad de Siri AI en la Unión Europea: según la compañía, el dispositivo no se venderá en la región mientras el asistente no esté disponible allí.
La restricción deja pendiente el lanzamiento europeo de la nueva pantalla. Apple señaló que está trabajando con las autoridades de la Unión Europea para encontrar un camino que permita llevar Siri AI a iOS en ese mercado. Hasta que haya un acuerdo o un cambio en la disponibilidad del asistente, los usuarios de la UE no tienen una fecha anunciada para comprar HomeView.

articles.title: Alerte maximale chez SAP : quatre failles critiques permettent de voler des identifiants et de prendre le contrôle de serveurs
articles.text:
SAP vient de corriger quatre vulnérabilités critiques dans ses logiciels professionnels. La plus grave permet de détourner les demandes d’authentification d’applications pour récupérer leurs identifiants et accéder à des informations sensibles.
Une application qui transmet ses propres identifiants à un serveur contrôlé par des pirates, leur permettant ensuite d’accéder à des données confidentielles : voilà ce que peut provoquer une faille que SAP vient de corriger, et dont la gravité a été évaluée à 10/10. Ce mardi 13 octobre, l’éditeur allemand a également publié des correctifs pour trois autres vulnérabilités critiques, dont deux pourraient conduire à une prise de contrôle complète des systèmes concernés.
La solution tout-en-un pour protéger votre entreprise
Votre petite entreprise a de grandes ambitions. Protégez-là contre les pirates. Et développez sereinement votre activité !
Des identifiants envoyés directement au mauvais serveur
Référencée CVE-2026-89111, la vulnérabilité la plus grave concerne SAP Cloud SDK for Python, une bibliothèque utilisée par les développeurs pour connecter leurs applications aux services cloud de SAP. Elle touche plus particulièrement les applications capables de gérer plusieurs clients à partir d’une même infrastructure.
Pour accéder aux services auxquels elles sont autorisées, ces applications doivent s’identifier auprès d’un serveur d’authentification, auquel elles transmettent leurs propres identifiants afin d’obtenir un jeton d’accès. Or, le SDK ne vérifie pas correctement un paramètre utilisé pour déterminer l’adresse de ce serveur. Si un attaquant parvient à le manipuler, il peut rediriger la demande d’authentification vers un serveur frauduleux et récupérer les identifiants transmis par l’application.
Une fois ces informations récupérées, le pirate peut se faire passer pour l’application et accéder aux ressources pour lesquelles elle dispose d’autorisations. Selon les droits accordés, il pourrait ainsi consulter des données financières, des informations relatives aux salariés ou d’autres données professionnelles sensibles, voire les modifier.
Le risque est d’autant plus sérieux que la vulnérabilité peut être exploitée à distance, sans compte préalable ni intervention d'un utilisateur, dès lors que l’attaquant parvient à contrôler le paramètre concerné. SAP a publié un correctif dans la version 0.45.2 de son SDK, qui vérifie désormais ce paramètre avant de l’utiliser pour construire l'adresse du serveur d’authentification.
Trois autres failles critiques qui menacent les systèmes SAP
Le bulletin de sécurité d’octobre comprend trois autres vulnérabilités critiques, dont deux évaluées à 9,9/10. La première, CVE-2026-89110, affecte SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer. Elle permet à un utilisateur disposant de droits limités de contourner les contrôles d’accès et, selon la configuration, de prendre entièrement le contrôle d’un système distant.
La deuxième, CVE-2026-89107, concerne SAP S/4HANA, le logiciel de gestion intégré de l’éditeur. Un utilisateur authentifié et disposant des autorisations nécessaires pourrait y injecter du code malveillant et compromettre le système. Enfin, CVE-2026-89108, notée 9,1/10, touche SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence, utilisé dans les environnements industriels. Elle permet à un administrateur de l’application d’obtenir des privilèges étendus sur le serveur Java qui l’héberge.
SAP n’a signalé aucune exploitation active de ces vulnérabilités pour le moment, et les correctifs sont désormais disponibles. À installer sans attendre, évidemment.

articles.title: I escaped from Nemesis on the Nintendo Switch 2 edition of Resident Evil 3, and it’s a highly capable port with smooth performance and solid visuals
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Resident Evil 3 looks and feels great on Nintendo Switch 2, with consistent frame rates, faithful visuals, and smooth controls. It would’ve been nice to see this port take advantage of the Switch 2’s gyro aiming or mouse controls, but this won’t be a dealbreaker for most players. Meanwhile, the core game is one of the most high-octane entries in the series, and conjures up an immensely tense atmosphere — even if it lacks the depth and strong narrative of its predecessor.
Reasons to buy
- + Smooth performance
- + Good visual fidelity in handheld and docked mode
- + Still an extremely tense, atmospheric survival horror experience
Reasons to avoid
- - Doesn’t take advantage of Switch 2’s motion or mouse modes
- - Core game held back by short runtime and average narrative
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
While a lot of fans have been mixed on Capcom’s remake of Resident Evil 3 since its initial release in 2020, there’s no denying that it's an incredibly tense survival horror experience that’s filled to the brim with high-octane action. And now, you can experience Jill Valentine and Carlos Oliveira’s terrifying journey on the go, thanks to a new Nintendo Switch 2 port.
Platform reviewed: Nintendo Switch 2
Available on: PS4, PS5, Nintendo Switch (cloud only), Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox One, Xbox Series X and Series S, PC, iOS
Release date: October 16, 2026 (Switch 2 edition)
I’ve spent more than 10 hours playing Resident Evil 3 on Nintendo Switch 2, experiencing the main story in full. So, is it a port that’s worth your time and money? Here’s my take.
For the most part, I want to focus on the quality of this port on Nintendo’s latest hybrid system, but before we delve into that, I’d like to share a few thoughts on the remake of Resident Evil 3 in itself.
Nemesis is coming for you...
I played through the Resident Evil 2 remake right before this entry, and while there are a lot of similarities in terms of the combat, resource management, environments, and visuals, they have a few striking differences.
Above all, Resident Evil 3 feels far more focused on the action — it feels like you’re constantly on the run, blasting through zombies, and rushing to save the people of Raccoon City. In some ways, this works to the game’s advantage: the horrifying Nemesis is a truly daunting foe, the high-paced gameplay is engaging from start to finish, and the explosive set pieces make this entry feel truly cinematic.
However, the fast pace and distinct action focus come with its drawbacks. The game’s runtime is very short — you’ll easily finish this one in about six hours. On top of that, the overall narrative feels a bit thin, and there are very few puzzles. Ultimately, Resident Evil 3 is still a blast, and its likeable cast and engrossing gameplay make it worth playing alone — it just doesn’t quite have the depth of some of the best entries in the series.
OK, I thought Mr. X was frightening in Resident Evil 2, but Nemesis is on a whole other level. He’s far more deadly and imposing, and when he whipped out a flamethrower on the rooftop, I was bricking it. All of the battles against him feel so incredibly tense yet enjoyable, and ended up being my favorite parts of this adventure.
Anyway, let’s talk about how this title plays on Switch 2 specifically. And good news — the Resident Evil 3 remake runs very well on this system. The Switch 2 edition targets 60 frames per second (fps), and I enjoyed smooth frame rates in both docked and handheld mode with barely any noticeable drops. Yes, the movement of some distant enemies could appear a little shaky — something I also saw in the Resident Evil 2 remake on Switch 2 — but even the most action-packed segments of the game were silky smooth.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While you could probably get a more premium visual presentation from a gaming PC or PS5 Pro, the game’s graphics also translate well onto Nintendo Switch 2 after calibrating HDR. The dark, moody environments look sharp and intricate in docked mode, with character models looking pleasantly detailed. Contrast is solid too, with colors popping against the dismal city streets, though it’s worth noting that in handheld mode there’s a noticeable (yet understandable) hit to graphical fidelity — though the game still looks very decent overall.
The game also controls nicely, and you can switch between a few different schemes in the options menu, although it would’ve been neat to see gyro aiming, which worked well on the Switch 2 edition of Resident Evil Requiem. There’s also no mouse mode integration, and more generally, it would’ve been nice to see this version play to the Switch 2’s strengths a bit more. One thing that I did like, though, was the Switch 2’s virtual spatial sound, which provides an expansive, almost three-dimensional soundscape when you’re battling through hordes of zombies.
In the end, then, it’s easy for me to recommend the Resident Evil 3 remake on Switch 2. While the graphics won’t wow you in handheld mode and the core game isn’t without its flaws, it consistently runs at a stable frame rate, visuals are strong in docked mode (and still more than adequate in handheld), and the action-packed gameplay is sure to keep you absorbed in the game from start to finish.
Should you play Resident Evil 3 for Nintendo Switch 2?
Play it if…
You want to experience Resident Evil 3 on the go with little compromise
I was very pleased with this Switch 2 port’s performance. It looks very solid overall, especially in docked mode, and you’ll get smooth frame rates for satisfying and seamless gameplay, both at home and on the go.
You’re looking for a brief survival horror game to blast through
The remake of Resident Evil 3 has a very brief runtime. I finished it up in about six hours, and while I feel that it could’ve offered more, some may appreciate its brevity. Sometimes, it’s fun to just fly through a brief, action-packed experience, and Resident Evil 3 offers exactly that.
Don’t play it if…
You want the best performance possible
For those of you looking for peak performance, then the PS5 Pro or PC might be the better destination for playing this title. That being said, the visuals and performance of the Switch 2 version are commendable, and the benefit of getting to play the game on the move is massive.
You’ve never played a Resident Evil game before
Resident Evil 3 isn’t the best starting point for series newcomers. The events that play out are deeply connected to those of Resident Evil 2, which I’d suggest as an entry point for anyone looking to get into the franchise.
Accessibility features
The options menu allows you to make a few changes to your experience, with a range of camera options, three separate control schemes, toggle or hold run modes, and a range of voice and text languages available. What’s more, you can change the color of the reticle, laser dot sight, and dot display, alter HUD opacity, and tone down damage display if you’d prefer.
How I reviewed Resident Evil 3 for Nintendo Switch 2
I sunk just over 10 hours into the Resident Evil 3 remake on Nintendo Switch 2, during which time I finished the main story and tried playing in both docked and handheld mode.
Most of the time, I played the game docked, with my Switch 2 connected to the Sky Glass Gen 2 TV and Marshall Heston 120 soundbar. I did try out handheld mode from time to time, though, and used my JBL Live Beam 4 earbuds to experience the game’s virtual spatial sound.
More generally, I’m an experienced gaming hardware and software reviewer, and have been testing all kinds of games and accessories at TechRadar for years now, where I serve as a Senior Reviews Writer. I’ve reviewed all sorts of Nintendo Switch 2 titles, from major first-party releases like Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave to ports like Yakuza Kiwami. I’ve also played a number of Resident Evil games, including the Switch 2 port of the Resident Evil 2 remake.
First reviewed October 2026
Harry is a Senior Reviews Writer for TechRadar. He reviews everything from party speakers to wall chargers and has a particular interest in the worlds of audio and gaming. Harry has a background in business tech journalism, particularly around the telecoms industry.

articles.title: Xandr Fined a Record €8.6 Million for Relaying Grindr Data Revealing Sexual Orientation
articles.text:
The Norwegian Data Protection Authority (DPA) has fined Xandr, an advertising unit owned by Microsoft, €8.6 million ($9.62 million) for illegally relaying Grindr users' sensitive data to advertisers.
The administrative penalty is the largest issued by the data protection watchdog, arguing the case merited a high fine because of the "very serious" nature of the breach. The infringements occurred between July 2018 and April 2020.
"Xandr acted as an intermediary that relayed the personal data of Grindr users in Norway, including data revealing sexual orientation, to potentially thousands of other companies," the Data Protection Authority said in a statement.
The data protection authority said its investigation found that Xandr was a joint controller with Grindr, which meant it was responsible for obtaining users' consent before processing their data.
Instead of ensuring they had the legal basis for their own processing of the data, Xandr pointed fingers at Grindr, stating it assumed the online dating app had collected users' consent to do so," it added.
Xandr was formed by AT&T following its June 2018 acquisition of AppNexus. The name is a reference to Alexander Graham Bell, who founded AT&T in 1885. It was subsequently sold to Microsoft in late December 2021, following which the brand was retired and consolidated under the Microsoft Ads umbrella in June 2023.
The case dates back to 2020, when the country's consumer council, along with Austrian privacy non-profit None of Your Business (noyb), filed a complaint against Xandr, accusing it of unlawfully sharing users' personal data for commercial purposes without getting users' explicit consent. Thousands of users in Norway are said to have been subjected to unlawful sharing of their sensitive data as a result of this practice.
"The essence of the infringement was Xandr's participation in so-called real-time bidding, where they acted both on the buyer and seller side," the watchdog said. "When a person opened Grindr, their personal data was in many cases relayed through Xandr to potentially thousands of actors in the advertising ecosystem."
"Advertisers could thereby bid against each other to present targeted adverts, completely hidden from the individual user."
The DPA also said the fine was calculated taking into account Xandr's total annual turnover during the two-year time period, which predates Microsoft's acquisition. Xandr has three weeks to appeal the decision.
Responding to the DPA's decision, noyb described the fine as a "major blow for the online advertising and commercial surveillance industry" and said that "companies such as Xandr are eventually held accountable for their shady practices."
In a statement shared with Reuters, Microsoft said it's reviewing the decision and assessing its options.
Last month, Grindr opted to pay £26 million ($35.1 million) to settle a lawsuit in the U.K. over allegations that it shared users' personal information, including their HIV status, with third-parties.
The development comes as a Texas federal judge granted final approval of a $177 million AT&T settlement for classes of AT&T consumers whose personal information was exposed in two separate data breaches that took place in March and July 2024. The class-action lawsuit was settled in November 2025.
The March 2024 incident involved the publication of a dataset on the dark web containing Social Security numbers. It affected about 7.6 million current AT&T account holders and approximately 65.4 million former account holders, the telecom service provider noted at the time.
The second hack revolved around threat actors illegally downloading AT&T customer data from a third-party cloud platform hosted by Snowflake. The American company said that calls and text message records that occurred between May 1 and October 31, 2022 were compromised for "nearly all" cellular customers.

articles.title: Getty Images dejará de cotizar en la Bolsa de Nueva York: una pérdida de USD 206,1 millones en 2025
articles.text:
Getty Images se declaró en quiebra en Estados Unidos y dejará de cotizar en la Bolsa de Nueva York como parte de un acuerdo para reorganizar su deuda con los principales acreedores. La empresa anunció un plan preacordado que incluye una inversión de hasta USD 533 millones por parte de integrantes de la familia Getty y filiales de Koch Equity Development.
La decisión afecta a una de las compañías más conocidas del mercado global de fotografía, video y contenidos visuales. Getty Images asegura que mantendrá su actividad durante el proceso y que no prevé consecuencias para proveedores, clientes, socios comerciales ni empleados. La reorganización llega después de una pérdida de USD 206,1 millones en 2025 y una caída del 68% de sus acciones tras el anuncio.
Getty Images buscará reorganizar su deuda bajo el Capítulo 11
La compañía planea acogerse al Capítulo 11 de la ley de quiebras de Estados Unidos, un mecanismo que permite a las empresas reorganizar sus obligaciones financieras bajo supervisión judicial. Este procedimiento no implica necesariamente el cierre de la compañía, sino que ofrece un marco legal para renegociar compromisos, reducir deuda y asegurar recursos para continuar operando.
Getty Images informó que la reestructuración ya cuenta con el respaldo de la mayoría necesaria de sus acreedores. El objetivo es presentar ante el tribunal un acuerdo previamente negociado, lo que evita iniciar el proceso sin una propuesta financiera definida.
La empresa espera completar la reorganización antes de que termine el año. Durante ese periodo, continuará ofreciendo licencias de fotografías, videos, ilustraciones y otros contenidos para medios de comunicación, empresas, instituciones y usuarios de todo el mundo.
“No prevemos consecuencias para los proveedores de contenido, socios comerciales, clientes o empleados en todo el mundo”, señaló Getty Images al informar sobre el acuerdo.
La familia Getty y Koch aportarán hasta USD 533 millones
La operación contempla una inversión de hasta USD 533 millones para reducir el endeudamiento de la empresa. Los fondos procederán de miembros de la familia Getty y de filiales de Koch Equity Development, la división de inversiones del conglomerado estadounidense Koch.
Además de esa inyección de capital, Getty Images tendrá acceso a hasta USD 143 millones en financiación aportada por Koch. Estos recursos, junto a los ingresos procedentes de la actividad habitual de la empresa, servirán para sostener las operaciones durante el proceso judicial.
La compañía no detalló el reparto exacto de la inversión ni las condiciones finales de la nueva estructura accionarial. Sin embargo, la entrada de recursos forma parte de un plan para aliviar la presión financiera y mantener la continuidad del negocio mientras avanza la negociación con acreedores.
La salida de la Bolsa de Nueva York marca el cambio
La reestructuración también implica que Getty Images dejará de cotizar en la Bolsa de Nueva York. La empresa ya había advertido que podía perder su presencia en el mercado bursátil después de que el valor de sus acciones descendiera por debajo de un dólar.
Tras conocerse el acuerdo con los acreedores, los títulos registraron una caída del 68%. El descenso reflejó la reacción del mercado ante el anuncio de la quiebra preacordada y la futura salida de bolsa.
Dejar de cotizar permite a la empresa avanzar con la reorganización fuera de la presión diaria de los mercados financieros. A cambio, los accionistas actuales afrontan un escenario de incertidumbre sobre el valor de sus participaciones y sobre la estructura que tendrá la empresa una vez concluya el proceso.
Una empresa clave en el mercado de contenidos visuales
Getty Images opera en un sector que reúne fotografía editorial, material de archivo, imágenes comerciales, video e ilustraciones. Su catálogo abastece a medios de comunicación, agencias de publicidad, compañías tecnológicas, marcas y organizaciones de diferentes países.
La continuidad de su actividad resulta relevante para fotógrafos, agencias y creadores que distribuyen su trabajo a través de la plataforma. También lo es para empresas y redacciones que utilizan su material mediante licencias para publicaciones, campañas y producciones audiovisuales.
El anuncio sitúa a Getty Images ante una etapa de reorganización financiera. La compañía confía en reducir su deuda, mantener sus operaciones y cerrar el proceso antes de finalizar el año, mientras deja atrás su cotización pública en Nueva York.

articles.title: [Webinar] How to Stop AI-Driven Privilege Escalation With Runtime Identity Controls
articles.text:
The dangerous part of a stolen identity isn't always the initial login. It's what an attacker can do with that access next.
With AI accelerating reconnaissance, exploitation of vulnerabilities, and privilege escalation, attackers can move through systems faster than security teams can investigate. A compromised account that looks legitimate at first could become the starting point for a much larger attack.
And that's where traditional identity security faces a serious problem: Checking who gets access isn't enough if you can't control what happens after.
Why Traditional Identity Controls Are Falling Behind
Many identity security controls focus on authentication, permissions, and access policies. But what happens when a trusted identity is compromised, its behavior changes, or an attacker begins exploiting already granted privileges?
That gap becomes more dangerous as AI-powered attacks accelerate.
Attackers can automate parts of the attack chain while defenders are still collecting alerts, investigating activity, and deciding how to respond.
The answer isn't simply detecting attacks faster. It's the ability to evaluate and control access in real time while an identity is actively being used.
This is the idea behind runtime identity security.
In this upcoming expert-led webinar, you'll learn:
- Where attackers find identity gaps across cloud, on-premises, SaaS, and AI environments.
- Why AI-powered attacks challenge traditional defenses and reduce the time available to respond.
- How runtime identity security works to evaluate access continuously and enforce security decisions when they matter.
- How to prepare your defenses for AI-driven attacks that move at machine speed.
The Next Identity Attack May Not Give You Time to React
If attackers can compromise identities and escalate privileges in minutes, discovering suspicious activity after the fact may already be too late.
Security teams need to know not just who has access, but whether that access should still be trusted right now.
This session explores how to close that gap and build an identity security strategy designed to keep pace with the speed of modern attacks.

articles.title: Uplift 4-leg standing desk review: Possibly the only desk you'll ever need
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Uplift 4-leg standing desk is one of those office products that earns your respect without having to try too hard. It's got everything that you want in a desk without any of the nonsense, and it looks good doing it. It's elegant, it's well-built, it's customizable, and it's exactly what nearly everybody who is looking for a standing desk actually needs.
Reasons to buy
- + Very stable
- + Solid construction
- + Fantastic materials
- + Easy assembly
Reasons to avoid
- - Legs block grommet holes in places
- - Limited availability outside the US
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
I've tested many desks. I've used a lot of different companies. I've built many desks, and I currently have several in my active repertoire that my team and I use daily.
There are some desks I've learned I can rely on: I know testing will go smoothly, building will be a no-frills experience, and once it's built, I won't have to worry about it falling apart on me. Uplift has quickly become one of those companies that I can give my five-star label to without any hesitation.
Of course, as I am with this one, I thoroughly test every desk. I'm pleased to say the four-legged standing desk continues the trend I have seen over the last couple of years in Uplift's build quality, reliability, and user experience.
This is the kind of desk most people should probably get if they want the best standing desk - although limited availability outside North America might mean its misses out on a spot in my guide. Most people I know don't need a ton of add-ons or bells and whistles. Just a quality slab of wood that won't be a waste of money in a few years, but something they can keep building on and use for many, many, many years to come.
Yes, of course, some people just want a simple budget desk, and for them, this might not be the right option. For those who want something that lasts and want to invest in something worth it, the Uplift standing desk family, including this four-legged standing desk, is well worth the cost, in my book.
Uplift 4-leg standing desk: Price and Availability
The Uplift 4-leg standing desk is available direct from the manufacturer, and comes in a range of different styles to match the workspace.
The MSRP on this desk is about $960, but you'll likely be able to grab it on sale if you aren't in any rush. I would keep an eye on Uplift's website and other third-party retailers to see if you can find it.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Unless you'd rather go with a custom desk, I would suggest going straight to Uplift's website and customizing your desk there. During the customization process, you can choose everything, down to the wood type, exact specifications and sizing, leg color, accessories, grommet placement, fill, and more.
Keep in mind, of course, that if you choose a larger desk and some more premium accessories, the price will go up, but I believe my build with a 48-inch desk was just around $960.
Uplift 4-leg standing desk: Unboxing and First Impressions
Every company has its modifications, but Uplift's unboxing experience is super straightforward. Overall, unboxing and building took me about 20 minutes, which says a lot. I know it's only a 48-inch desk, so there wasn't much logistical physics involved in maneuvering around a large slab of wood. A 20-minute build time for a standing desk is pretty crazy, since some desks take people upwards of 2 hours due to their complexity (and I should probably say unnecessary complexity, since Uplift shows it doesn't have to be that hard).
Another thing I really appreciate about Uplift is that everything is pre-threaded. Unless you want to add things beyond what they send, even with their additional accessories, everything has a pre-threaded hole in the ideal location. Of course, since this is, at the end of the day, a hunk of wood, you can customize it however you want, adding that extra flexibility. If you want to build to their suggestions, there are plenty of mounting options, down to the controller.
I mentioned it briefly above, but as someone who has had plenty of power strips fall off due to failed adhesive or the frustration of having to undo a screw in a nice piece of wood (because the power strip placement was slightly off), I can attest to the value of this. Being able to mount the power strip directly to the desk frame in multiple locations is an unlock I didn't realize I wanted until I started using Uplift desks.
Once again, if you plan to add a power strip, I suggest getting one or several from them so you can use this system. You can connect the power strip, which will inevitably get heavy and warm, to the frame so it won't fall off in the future.
Uplift 4-leg standing desk: Design and Build Quality
Building on what I said in previous sections, Uplift standing desks have build quality that's probably second to none, especially on their higher-end models, like this solid walnut one I have here. The quality and materials are spectacular.
Sure, if you want, you can get a much cheaper desk with a fake wood top or a non-wood top all around. Having a solid hunk of walnut, or any quality wood, to base your entire workstation around is well worth it, in my book.
Before my years of reviewing desks, I've gone the route of:
- cheap built-ins in apartments
- cheap desks at university
- tables that I pulled from other areas because I didn't think it mattered
- not even having a desk at all and just running a laptop on my lap or at the kitchen table
While those are all viable options, maybe some people need a dedicated workspace they can be proud of. That makes all the difference if you choose the 48-inch desk route, as I do.
One thing to note: the frame that holds the legs to the desktop will slightly cover the grommet holes. If you plan to use one of the powered grommet holes to run power all the way up to the top of your desk, it may not fit properly.
For me, having the cable pass through, or even a little cubby, works just fine. For this size desk, it doesn't seem worth it to me to have a power grommet in the top, especially since I planned to use my Siteki power block on top, as you can see in the photos.
Uplift 4-leg standing desk: In use
I'm 6'1", 6'2" depending on who's asking, or, honestly, what shoes I'm wearing that day. I've noticed I'm at that cutoff point where some desks rise to the level I want, and some are just a little too short. Most of the time, I'm putting my desks on caster wheels, which helps significantly by adding a couple of inches, but for some desks, I don't, and that's really when I notice the cutoff in height.
So, this is for those who are around that same height or taller. I've done my homework over the last several years, and many sit-stand desks aren't built for people who are our height or taller. Uplift is not one of those companies.
It can rise to a height that is actually taller than I would want, which is very uncommon for me. This means that I can raise it up to where I actually am comfortable standing for long periods of time, not feeling like I have to hunch over at all or compromise by having my monitor on an arm that's abnormally high when I'm sitting (just so that it matches the height I want when I'm standing).
All right, back to everybody here. A standing desk that can get really high isn't just useful for taller people. Of course, that's one clear benefit, but it's also a huge benefit if you want to use your space a little more intentionally and slide your desk chair under your desk when you're not using it. If you're the kind of person who changes out parts on your desk even semi-regularly, being able to raise it lets you get under it much easier without crawling around on the floor, lying on your back, or feeling claustrophobic.
It's also helpful if you are on a call on your laptop that's open on your desk and you want a better height or angle during an interview (so your potential future boss isn't looking up your nose from your camera angle on your laptop). If you're like me and need to get it up and out of the way so your kids can't reach it when you're not around, the extra height can be a game changer and potentially a work saver.
I've really enjoyed doing this for the last several desks and products I've tested, and I've had this desk for about 100 days now, actually 106 if you're being very technical. It's been in my office space at my studio for about 100 days.
Over the last few years, I've started testing longer periods like this because I noticed a few products I tested early on didn't work great after a few months of heavy use. Uplift has absolutely knocked it out of the park and has even survived about six different desk setups in those 106 days so far.
Now, of course, I know not many people will rotate out their gear as quickly as I do. What is good to know is that this desk has gone up and down numerous times. Over the last 106 days, it has lifted almost no weight every single day. It has lifted an extremely heavy monitor, desk shelves, and multiple monitors. It's even lifted my kids a couple of times because, scarily enough, my kids now view my office as a jungle gym sometimes.
Through all those tests, desk setups, and children, this desk hasn't wavered at all. There's been absolutely no degradation in the materials or the electric motors. There are zero signs of wear and tear. The desk still lifts and lowers as quietly as before. Partly because of its smaller size, but mostly because of its quality build, this desk has zero wobble. Even at height, you won't notice it moving at all.
This desk probably isn't for those who need a super niche desk, but for everyone else looking for a quality workstation, it's a great place to start, or at least one to strongly consider.
Uplift 4-leg standing desk: Final verdict
If you're looking for a corner desk, this is not it. If you're looking for a very specific niche desk that matches your aesthetic perfectly, this might be it. If you want a quality desk you can build out into just about anything, you should absolutely check out Uplift's standing desks and consider them for your build.
A quality desk as the capstone and foundation for everything else you build around it makes all the difference. You can have the best chair, the best speakers, the best laptop, the best monitor arm, and the best gadgets on your desk, but if your desk itself is terrible, it'll make everything else feel lesser, like it's trying to cover up. It's going to feel like makeup on a pig.
If you start with a quality main piece and then slowly build around it, you know what you're building on is a firm foundation, and that's wise no matter how you look at it.
For more work essentials, we've tested and reviewed the best office chairs.
Former TechRadar Pro B2B Hardware Editor, Collin has been in journalism for years, with experience in small and large markets, including Gearadical, DailyBeast, FutureNet, and more.

articles.title: Shadow AI : faut-il interdire l'IA fantôme en entreprise ? Les experts de la cyber ne sont pas d'accord
articles.text:
ChatGPT ouvert en douce, des agents bricolés avec Copilot et d'autres : le Shadow AI, ou IA fantôme, s'installe dans les entreprises et crée la pagaille. Six experts nous ont expliqué comment le dompter, sans tous appeler à son interdiction.
Le Shadow AI, cette IA fantôme que les salariés utilisent en entreprise sans l'aval de leur service informatique, s'est imposé comme l'un des grands casse-têtes de la cybersécurité en 2026. Au fil de nos rencontres aux Assises de la cybersécurité à Monaco ces derniers jours, les spécialistes de Sekoia, Check Point, Illumio, Nomios et KnowBe4, ainsi que le responsable sécurité de SNCF Connect & Tech, ont décrit un phénomène bien plus vaste que le simple rapport sensible de la boîte copié-collé dans un chatbot. Comment répondre à ce phénomène ? Faut-il l'interdire ou l'encadrer ? Vous allez voir que les avis divergent.
Le Shadow AI, ce collègue invisible dont on préfère ne pas parler
Lorsque vous avez devant les yeux un rapport à synthétiser avant une réunion, quelques lignes de code à faire relire, ou un document trop long à résumer, le robot conversationnel de type Claude, Gemini ou ChatGPT est devenu l'allié de nombreux salariés, souvent sans demander l'avis de personne. Ce réflexe porte un nom, le Shadow AI, et Anthony Hervé, ingénieur avant-vente chez Illumio, nous en donne une définition. Il s'agit d'utiliser « des outils IA de manière générale, qui ne sont pas contrôlés, validés par les équipes IT de l'entreprise », au risque d'y partager des données sensibles. Plus de trois salariés sur dix utiliseraient déjà des assistants que leur direction informatique n'a jamais approuvés. Et chacun a son anecdote, car forcément, nous connaissons tous quelqu'un qui a collé le dernier rapport de sa boîte dans ChatGPT pour en tirer une synthèse express.
Ce scénario, François Deruty le connaît par cœur. Passé par l'ANSSI, le gendarme français de la cybersécurité, avant de prendre la direction des opérations de Sekoia, il nous explique le problème. Faute d'accompagnement, les salariés les moins à l'aise avec les nouvelles technologies découvrent souvent ces outils chez eux, ils y glissent des données de l'entreprise pour soigner un rapport, et « ils n'osent pas le dire ». Le danger tient en fait moins à l'outil qu'à ce qu'on lui confie. Par principe, le spécialiste se méfie de tout service externe, évoquant une évidente question de confiance, tant pour l'envoi du contenu que ce que les entreprises qui le traitent en font. Car une fois partis vers ces outils, les documents échappent à l'entreprise, qui ne sait plus très bien où ils sont stockés, ni qui peut y accéder.
Francis Bergey, responsable de la sécurité des systèmes d'information (RSSI) de SNCF Connect & Tech, que nous avons interrogé à l'issue de son atelier avec AWS à Monaco, pointe le piège des offres gratuites. « Dans les conditions générales, il y a écrit que ce que vous allez envoyer au LLM (Ndlr : par exemple GPT-4o, Claude 5 Sonnet ou autres) va servir à entraîner la génération d'après. » Un document interne peut ainsi finir dans le modèle dont profitent tous les autres utilisateurs. La frontière se brouille encore avec l'abonnement Mistral payé à titre personnel puis utilisé pour le travail. « La difficulté qu'on peut avoir, c'est dans l'usage pro/perso », explique le technicien.
IA fantôme : la menace se cache aussi dans les outils officiels
Puisqu'on parle de fantôme, celui-ci ne rôde pas toujours là où on l'attend. Le directeur technique France de Check Point, Adrien Merveille, rappelle qu'un logiciel acheté en bonne et due forme peut embarquer de l'IA sans que l'entreprise le sache, jusqu'à découvrir, en grattant un peu, que « derrière, c'est du DeepSeek qui tourne ». Voilà qui est fâcheux pour les nombreuses sociétés qui bannissent les modèles chinois. « On ne peut pas contrôler ce qu'on ne voit pas », insiste celui qui enchaîne les rendez-vous avec des entreprises privées de toute visibilité sur leurs propres usages de l'IA.
Chez Nomios, intégrateur de solutions de sécurité de 500 salariés, Eric Bohec a mesuré la vitesse du phénomène sur ses propres troupes, pourtant encadrées. « On a formé 500 personnes, et pourtant dans les trois semaines, il y avait 800 agents » IA. Ces assistants justement, n'importe quel salarié peut désormais les créer avec des outils fournis par l'entreprise, comme Copilot, l'assistant IA de Microsoft, et les faire agir sous sa propre identité. Pour le directeur technique, laisser chacun bricoler dans son coin, « c'est créer autant d'entrepreneurs que vous avez d'employés et à la fin autant de process dans votre boîte ».
Parlons des privilèges aussi, au sens informatique du terme. Car le vrai danger surgit quand ces agents IA reçoivent des droits sur des applications internes. Eric Bohec imagine un commercial qui, au volant, dicte à son assistant de créer une commande dans Salesforce, son logiciel de gestion client. C'est pratique, évidemment, jusqu'à la consigne mal comprise qui déclenche une action non désirée, voire efface des données clients. « Le risque est juste gigantesque. » Anthony Hervé évoque le développeur pressé qui branche un modèle non validé sur le système d'information, sans voir que « lui, il est le pont vers l'extérieur ». Car avec ces interconnexions, prévient François Deruty, « tu peux avoir un chemin jusqu'à tes données critiques ».
Ce pont, les pirates savent aussi l'emprunter. Anthony Hervé précise que chaque outil branché sans contrôle multiplie les portes d'entrée dans l'entreprise. Un pirate qui met la main sur un agent IA décroche un passe-partout, puisque cet assistant, pour être utile, est relié à tout, souvent sans garde-fou parce qu'on l'a déployé trop vite. Là où il fallait autrefois un groupe de pirates chevronnés, l'IA change la donne, en ce qu'il « suffit d'une seule personne vraiment motivée ».
Interdire ou encadrer l’IA fantôme, le grand débat
Faut-il tout simplement interdire le Shadow AI ? Eric Bohec ne tergiverse pas sur le cas le plus courant, celui du salarié qui confie des données de l'entreprise à un chatbot grand public, « ça, c'est à interdire purement et simplement ». Selon lui, la plupart des entreprises disposent déjà d'un proxy, un poste de contrôle par lequel transite la navigation internet des salariés. Il suffit d'y activer la surveillance des IA publiques pour voir, et bloquer, ces usages. Anthony Hervé balaie pourtant l'idée, pour lui, c'est « impossible. » Car le salarié privé d'IA, qui voit ses collègues ou ses amis en profiter, passera par son téléphone ou un Wi-Fi public, voire par son compte personnel, ce qui est encore pire. Interdire, prévient-il, ne fera que créer de la frustration, et engendrera ainsi des comportements toujours plus critiques.
Florian Malecki, directeur Europe du Sud de KnowBe4, fait la comparaison avec une ère plus ancienne, celle du Shadow IT, quand des services entiers contournaient la direction informatique (DSI), puis celle de l'arrivée des smartphones personnels au bureau. Son avis est que « bloquer, ce n'est pas la bonne réponse, les gens trouveront toujours un moyen de l'utiliser dans tous les cas et de le ramener au monde du travail ». Francis Bergey, dont les équipes repèrent pourtant ces usages sur le réseau et les postes de travail, et qui a déjà vu des collègues utiliser des outils non validés, ne dit pas autre chose, même s'il est concède que tout ça, « c'est hyper dur de contrôler. »
Couper l'accès aux chatbots publics ne règle pas tout. Eric Bohec s'attaque surtout à l'IA fantôme interne, donc aux agents que les salariés créent eux-mêmes sur les outils de l'entreprise. Pour garder ces agents à l’œil, il empile trois garde-fous, à commencer par une passerelle de sécurité, sorte de douanier qui lit chaque demande avant qu’elle n’atteigne l’agent et la bloque si elle sort des clous. Ensuite, un journal de bord qui enregistre tout (qui a sollicité l'IA, avec quelle demande, via quel modèle). En cas de pépin ou d'audit, l'entreprise peut ainsi retracer et prouver ce que l'agent a réellement fait. Enfin, un humain garde le dernier mot sur les actions sensibles. Le commercial qui, en sortant d'un rendez-vous, demande à son agent de créer une commande ne la voit pas partir directement : elle arrive d'abord chez l'assistante commerciale, qui la valide, ou la bloque si l'agent, ayant mal compris, réclame d'effacer des comptes clients. « La première chose, c'est de rendre visible l'action de l'IA », assure Eric Bohec.
Il y a une piste qui rallie presque tout le monde, à savoir proposer mieux que le fantôme. Francis Bergey aimerait des outils internes qui « soient les meilleurs du marché pour que les gens se disent, pourquoi j'irais chercher ailleurs ? ». Car « le Shadow AI peut naître du fait que l'entreprise n'offre pas un catalogue de services IA », souligne Anthony Hervé, partisan d'une méthode qui consiste à « éduquer, communiquer, former ». Chez Sekoia, il a fallu six mois pour rédiger une doctrine d'usage interne. Florian Malecki préconise, lui, une charte simple, partant du principe qu'à la fin, « il y aura toujours des erreurs. » Adrien Merveille, enfin, l'avoue : « Je ne sais pas où est le security by design dans l'ère de l'IA, honnêtement. » Après le Shadow IT et l’arrivée des téléphones personnels au bureau, l’histoire se répète, mais à la vitesse de l’IA. Dans cette course, l’entreprise qui tarde à proposer ses propres outils risque surtout de voir ses salariés trouver les leurs. Pour le meilleur et pour le pire.

articles.title: LG Smart TVs Vulnerable to Pre-Auth Root Takeover From Local Network
articles.text:
Three vulnerabilities in LG's webOS can be chained to give an attacker on the same local network root access to certain smart TVs without a PIN or any interaction from the owner.
LG has issued a fix, according to an advisory published by SSD Secure Disclosure on October 12.
The chain was tested on two TV models, the 32LQ636BPSA and the 27TQ600SW, running webOS 7.5.7-25 on firmware 04.54.40. Whether other models or firmware versions are affected is not known.
Owners of affected TVs should check for a firmware update. No workaround is available for those who cannot update yet.
The attack enters through a service that the TV exposes on port 3001, which is used by the LG ThinQ app for pairing. An attacker replays a manifest from sync-demo, a built-in app already on the device, signed with a test certificate the firmware trusts. A permission in the manifest causes the pairing service to skip the PIN prompt and hand over a privileged key.
With that key, the attacker launches another built-in app, cmp-client, and points it to an attacker-controlled page. The app does not check where it navigates, and the loaded page keeps access to PalmServiceBridge, an internal interface to the TV's system services.
Through that bridge, the attacker calls the system logging service, pmlogd, passing shell commands through an input field the service does not check. Because pmlogd runs as root, the injected command runs as root.
This is not the first time the local network attack surface has led to root access on LG smart TVs. In 2024, Bitdefender disclosed a different set of webOS vulnerabilities that also allowed unauthenticated access from the network, affected different components, and were patched in March 2024. A separate chain demonstrated at TyphoonPWN 2025 used a path traversal on a different port.
The chain was demonstrated by an anonymous researcher who won third place in the LG webOS category at TyphoonPWN 2026, held in Seoul in May. No CVE identifiers have been assigned, and no exploitation in the wild has been reported.

articles.title: WhatsApp oculta una función para saber quién te está espiando: revisa si es tu pareja o amigo
articles.text:
WhatsApp cuenta con una función para revisar los dispositivos que mantienen acceso a una cuenta, una verificación que permite detectar sesiones abiertas en computadoras, tabletas u otros aparatos.
La función se llama “Dispositivos vinculados” y muestra los aparatos asociados a la aplicación de Meta, incluidos aquellos que podrían haber quedado conectados sin que el titular de la cuenta lo advierta.
La revisión es útil para quienes utilizan WhatsApp Web en una computadora compartida, en una oficina, un cibercafé o un aparato prestado. Encontrar un acceso desconocido no confirma por sí solo que alguien haya espiado los chats, pero sí exige cerrar la sesión y reforzar la seguridad de la cuenta para evitar accesos sin autorización.
Dónde se revisan los dispositivos vinculados a la cuenta de WhatsApp
El listado está disponible desde la app instalada en el teléfono. En los modelos Android, el usuario debe abrir WhatsApp, tocar el ícono de tres puntos verticales, ubicado en la parte superior de la pantalla, y seleccionar la opción “Dispositivos vinculados”. Allí aparece el historial de sesiones que todavía tienen acceso a la cuenta.
En iPhone, el acceso suele estar dentro de la pestaña de configuración de WhatsApp. La función permite comprobar qué computadoras, navegadores o tabletas están conectados y, en algunos casos, ofrece información sobre la última actividad registrada. La revisión toma pocos segundos y evita que una sesión olvidada permanezca abierta durante días o semanas.
Qué datos aparecen en la lista de sesiones de WhatsApp abiertas
La sección muestra los aparatos vinculados a la cuenta y permite identificar si se trata de una computadora personal, una tableta o un navegador. El usuario debe verificar si reconoce cada dispositivo y si recuerda haber iniciado sesión desde ese aparato.
Conviene prestar atención a los dispositivos compartidos o ajenos. Una sesión de WhatsApp puede seguir activa en una computadora de trabajo, en un aparato prestado o en un dispositivo que fue enviado a reparación.
Si la lista incluye una computadora, tableta o navegador que no se reconoce, la recomendación es cerrar la sesión desde la misma pantalla. Solo hay que tocar el nombre del dispositivo y elegir la opción “Cerrar sesión”. A partir de ese momento, ese aparato pierde el acceso a los chats y deja de recibir el contenido de la cuenta.
Además, la medida sirve para eliminar conexiones antiguas que, aunque resulten familiares, ya no deberían conservar acceso. Un dispositivo personal que pasó a manos de otra persona, una computadora utilizada durante un viaje o un aparato que estuvo en un servicio técnico pueden mantener una sesión activa.
Cuáles son las estafas más comunes en WhatsApp
Los intentos de estafa suelen comenzar con mensajes, llamadas o invitaciones a grupos. Entre las modalidades comunes aparecen las relaciones afectivas fraudulentas, las ofertas de empleo falsas, las inversiones que prometen ganancias rápidas y las suplantaciones de identidad.
Asimismo, una persona puede hacerse pasar por un familiar, un amigo, una empresa o una figura conocida para pedir una transferencia o información privada.
Por esta razón, sumado a revisar las sesiones abiertas, es clave desconfiar de enlaces desconocidos, confirmar cualquier pedido de dinero por otra vía y no compartir códigos recibidos por mensaje.
Cómo reforzar la seguridad de WhatsApp
Para reforzar la seguridad de WhatsApp, conviene activar la verificación en dos pasos, registrar un correo de recuperación y proteger el teléfono con un código, huella o reconocimiento facial.
Es clave revisar con frecuencia los dispositivos vinculados a la cuenta personal en WhatsApp, cerrar sesiones que no se reconozcan y evitar compartir códigos de acceso. Ante mensajes sospechosos, hay que confirmar la identidad del contacto por otra vía y bloquear enlaces o archivos desconocidos.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6's PC version will reportedly arrive 'in the first quarter of 2027' and fans are convinced Rockstar has moved the date up to avoid a potential PS5 emulator — 'GTA 6 will probably be emulator ready a month after launch'
articles.text:
GTA 6 will reportedly launch on PC in early 2027, and fans believe it's so Rockstar can avoid clashing with 'the PS5 emulator breathing down their necks'
Fans suggest an earlier PC release will allow Rockstar to get ahead of an emulator
- The PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 will reportedly launch in early 2027, a few months after the console versions
- Some fans believe a 2028 release was possible, but Rockstar Games has moved the PC release up
- Fans speculate that Rockstar wants to get ahead of a potential PS5 emulator
A new report has claimed the PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 will launch in early 2027, and fans believe Rockstar Games wants to get ahead of a potential emulator.
The news comes from GamesBeat, which reports that Rockstar plans to release the PC version of GTA 6 "in the first quarter of 2027," and that's according to "four industry sources familiar with the studio’s plans, all of whom requested anonymity to avoid damaging business relationships."
It's worth taking this report with a grain of salt, as Rockstar has yet to announce any PC edition; However, this is GTA 6 we're talking about, and fans are already theorizing over potential reasons a PC release could arrive mere months after the PS5 and Xbox versions, despite the PC version of GTA 5 arriving roughly two years after the console editions.
Many have speculated that Rockstar moved the PC release date up to anticipate a possible PS5 emulator, which would allow PC owners access to a "PC build" of GTA 6 without having to wait and pay for the official version. This would also allow users to avoid the "double dipping" scheme that many believe Rockstar is going for.
One redditor suggested Rockstar is "Not waiting a year with the PS5 emulator breathing down their necks." Some other fan wrote something similar, saying, "GTA 6 will probably be emulator ready a month after launch. It’s almost guaranteed at this point."
Some have also pointed out the more recent leaks from 'Cyberleek' (via GamesRadar) and suggest the studio wants to get ahead of the hacker.
"I actually believe this because of the leaks and emulator thing, they probably want the game out asap," a fan said on Reddit, as another wrote, "Im leaning heavily towards an original 2028 PC launch, but some exec has seen the speed that recomps are coming out and realised if they dont release it quick, everyone will be playing it for free."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Other fans think Rockstar hasn't announced the PC release date yet in order to maximise console edition sales; we've recently seen retailers hit with huge price hikes on the PS5 and PS5 Pro in anticipation of the game's launch.
"Not the first rumour we've heard like this," one fan said. "I find it believable - I strongly suspect the PC version is already pretty much done and the 'delay' is artificial from Rockstar to maximise the console release."
We'll have to wait for an official announcement from Rockstar, but in the meantime, PS5 and Xbox users don't have much longer to wait because GTA 6 launches next month on November 19.
In other news, new details have emerged ahead of the GTA 6's launch, which details even more gameplay features and immersive systems.

articles.title: Product Walkthrough: Bitdefender AI Visibility and Control
articles.text:
A user opens a browser tab, pastes data into a chat assistant, and nothing is installed.
A developer adds a coding assistant as an editor extension, and nothing shows up in the installed programs list.
Someone downloads a local model runtime, a program that runs models directly on the machine instead of sending data to an external service, because they were told not to send company data outside.
None of this reaches your software inventory. Tasked with controlling AI, an administrator often resorts to blocking well-known AI websites and taking enforcement action without knowing what is actually running.
Bitdefender GravityZone AI Visibility and Control (AIVC) is the discovery and risk layer that answers the questions you have, first: Which AI software is present on your protected Windows endpoints, who is running it, and how much risk does each one carry.
What Your Software Inventory Was Never Built to Watch
AI Visibility and Control covers four classes of exposure, and each one sits outside a control you already own.
- AI services reached through the browser. Hosted assistants are the path most organizations already worry about. The inventory identifies which services are running, on which machines, and whether you have marked them as approved. A service with no findings is not automatically approved; a clean result on a tool your organization never sanctioned is still shadow AI. This ensures filtering decisions are based on real user activity rather than hand-picked domain lists.
- AI inside the development environment. Coding assistants run inside editors that already hold source repositories, and often credentials and configuration files in the same working directory. They are rarely covered by whatever you decided about chat assistants, because nobody classified them as the same kind of tool.
- AI running locally on the endpoint. Local model runtimes, MCP servers, and agent frameworks execute on the machine itself. A control that governs which websites an endpoint may reach does not see them at all. The MCP server is the sharpest case: its entire purpose is to hand a model access to something else, and it usually arrives as a configuration entry rather than as an install.
- AI with reach into other systems. Where a tool is configured to connect to a database, a code repository, an internal API, or a third-party model service, that connection is part of your attack surface. AI Visibility and Control records the configured scope of those connections, not the data moving across them.
How AIVC Finds and Categorizes What It Finds
GravityZone AI Visibility and Control discovery takes place during the risk scan. The GravityZone BEST agent collects metadata from each endpoint and keeps that collection minimized: it records what AI software is present and how it is configured, not what anyone does with it. AIVC does not inspect prompts, chat history, model weights, credentials, or full file content.
AI Visibility and Control recognizes more than 50 AI agents and more than 70,000 skills, the modular code packages that extend an agent's capabilities and that arrive from public registries. Because agents exercise permissions through these skills, considering only agents while ignoring skills would account for only a fraction of the total exposure.
Every discovered service is assigned to one of 17 functional categories based on its primary function (e.g., LLMs, coding, productivity, and others). The category makes the inventory actionable at the policy level because it maps to the question the reviewer arrived with. A security team investigating data-handling risk, filters to LLMs and chatbots plus Platforms and infrastructure. A development manager auditing what touches source code goes straight to Coding and Tools and skills. A governance review covering automation risk works from Agents, Automation, and MCP.
Two Views, and a Connector Nobody Installed
AI Visibility and Control appears in Bitdefender GravityZone Console as two views, each answering a different question.
AI Services answers "what AI is running in my environment?" It is the inventory: every discovered service with its risk score. This includes the function category, the related AI assets it depends on or exposes, its count of open findings, the affected resources and endpoints it was found on, its state of Active or Ignored, and whether it sits on the watchlist. Opening a service shows its details alongside mitigation guidance.
AI Findings answers "what should I look at first?" It is the prioritized risk view. Each finding includes a risk score, the service it relates to, the affected resources it was observed on, a link to mitigation guidance, and the endpoint-specific evidence behind it.
This enables you to see why a finding was raised on one machine and not another before deciding what to do. Most administrators work in AI Findings day to day and drop into AI Services for the full picture of a particular tool.
A score of 0 means AI Visibility and Control found nothing risky in how a tool is configured, not that your organization approved it. Review AI Services against your list of sanctioned tools, not just AI Findings.
Consider a developer who connects their AI assistant to the company ticketing system using a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, which is a small connector that gives a model access to external tools. The setup requires only a few lines in a configuration file: there is no installer, no entry in the installed programs list, and no network traffic for controls to inspect. It simply surfaces in AI Services alongside the assets it exposes.
The finding answers not just whether the connector exists, but what it reaches. A connector tied to a read-only reporting view presents a vastly different risk from one holding write credentials to a production database. This distinction lives entirely in its configuration. Meanwhile, the affected-host list clarifies the broader scope: whether this is an isolated shortcut or a pattern copied across the entire team.
That endpoint-specific evidence is also what makes findings usable by a SOC analyst rather than only as a posture metric. A finding tied to a local model runtime or an MCP server identifies a process executing on a specific host outside the browser sandbox, and the affected-resources list gives the host set to pivot from, in Search and Incident Advisor.
From Inventory to Enforcement
GravityZone AI Visibility and Control establishes which AI is present and what about its configuration is risky. The score orders your queue; it does not decide the outcome. A high score is not an order to remove the tool, and a score of 0 is not an approval. It does not block access, remove software, or modify program permissions. Those actions are handled separately by existing controls within the GravityZone console.
Blocking access to a prohibited service is Web Content Filtering. Most AI services are accessed through the browser, so once AIVC identifies which ones are in use, you block the domains.
Blocking a specific tool wherever it turns up is what custom detection rules do: once AIVC has named the tool, you define a rule that matches it on process name, attach Kill process as an automatic action, and every later appearance is handled without an administrator in the loop, and is company-wide or scoped to endpoints carrying a given tag.
Reducing what an installed tool is permitted to do belongs to hardening policies and to PHASR. PHASR for AI agents evaluates the agent separately from the person using the machine: processes started by a known agent binary are attributed to that agent's own behavioral profile rather than to the user's session, so the agent gets the tools its tasks require while the user's restrictions stay tied to the user's role.
Turning on AI Visibility and Control does not require a rollout project. It runs on your existing Bitdefender Endpoint Security Tools agent and can be enabled by editing a current policy. The setting sits in the General section under Risk Management and applies to all endpoints targeted by that policy. Results will appear after the next risk scan.
Summary
Bitdefender GravityZone AI Visibility and Control provides the AI inventory your traditional software inventory cannot: browser-reached assistants, editor extensions, local runtimes, MCP servers, and agent frameworks; each with a risk score, one of 17 functional categories, and a list of impacted endpoints. It covers more 50 agents and 70,000 skills, and it records what is present and how it is configured, rather than user prompts.
The two console views align with your existing workflow: AI Findings highlight what to address first, while AI Services gives a complete picture of any specific tool. A risk score tells you how exposed a tool is, not whether it is sanctioned; that decision, and the enforcement that follows, stays with you. Enforcement remains where it already lives: Web Content Filtering, custom detection rules, and PHASR, so your policy decisions stop being guesses, and you can gain greater confidence in the control you have over AI use within your organization.

articles.title: Ventes Flash Amazon : jusqu’à -31 % sur 10 produits tech ce mardi
articles.text:
Six jours après la fin des Jours Flash Prime, Amazon affiche encore des remises sur une partie de son catalogue tech, du robot laveur au téléviseur de 75 pouces. Nous avons confronté chacune à l’historique des prix et à ce que pratiquent les autres marchands, et nous signalons celles qui restent modestes.
Les Jours Flash Prime se sont achevés le 7 octobre, et le Black Friday n’arrivera que le 27 novembre. Entre les deux, Amazon continue d’afficher des pourcentages élevés, mais beaucoup sont calculés sur un prix conseillé que plus personne ne pratique. Lors de nos relevés du 12 octobre, la plupart des fortes baisses affichées correspondaient en réalité au prix courant du marché, ou à un prix plus élevé qu’à la Fnac, chez Darty ou chez Boulanger.
Nous avons retenu 10 offres, toutes vendues par Amazon ou par la boutique officielle de la marque. Le prix de comparaison indiqué n’est jamais le prix conseillé affiché sur la fiche : c’est le plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours, ou le prix le plus bas relevé ailleurs ces dernières semaines. Deux offres, le téléviseur LG de 50 pouces et le Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro, restent sous les 15 % de baisse : nous les gardons, en le précisant. Les prix peuvent avoir bougé au moment de votre visite.
Nos 10 offres Amazon, confrontées à l’historique des prix
- Robot aspirateur laveur Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 à 549,99 € au lieu de 799,99 €
- TV LG 75QNED7E 75 pouces (2026) à 679,99 € au lieu de 902 €
- Aspirateur laveur Roborock F25 LT Gen2 à 259,99 € au lieu de 349,99 €
- Écran gaming LG UltraGear 27G640A 27 pouces QHD 300 Hz à 209,99 € au lieu de 274,10 €
- Friteuse sans huile Cosori Turbo Tower 10,8 L à 132,99 € au lieu de 187,59 €
- Trottinette électrique Segway-Ninebot Max G2 E à 499 € au lieu de 600,99 €
- Aspirateur balai Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 à 109,99 € au lieu de 136,48 €
- Simulateur d’aube Philips SmartSleep Wake-up Light HF3532 à 139,99 € au lieu de 179,99 €
- TV LG 50QNED7E 50 pouces (2026) à 369 € au lieu de 428 €
- Robot aspirateur laveur Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro à 599 € au lieu de 649 €
Ce qui justifie leur place dans la liste
Une remise ne suffit pas à faire une bonne affaire. Pour six de ces offres, voici ce que le produit apporte, à qui il s’adresse et ce qu’il faut savoir avant de commander.
- Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 : haut de 7,98 cm et doté d’un LiDAR qui se rétracte pour passer sous les meubles bas, ce robot aspire à 25 000 Pa et lave ses serpillières à 80 °C dans sa station. Celle-ci mesure 34 x 48,7 x 52,1 cm : prévoyez la place. Il est vendu par la boutique officielle Roborock et expédié par Amazon, alors que la Fnac le facturait 899,99 € le 11 octobre.
- LG 75QNED7E : une diagonale de 75 pouces sous les 700 €, avec un rétroéclairage Mini LED d’après la fiche Amazon et quatre entrées HDMI. Sa dalle s’arrête à 60 Hz : pour jouer en 120 images par seconde sur console, il faut viser plus haut. Ailleurs, son prix le plus bas relevé depuis mi-septembre était de 902 €.
- LG UltraGear 27G640A : une dalle IPS de 27 pouces en 2 560 x 1 440 pixels à 300 Hz, compatible G-Sync et FreeSync Premium, avec un port HDMI 2.1 et un DisplayPort 1.4. Son écran brillant renvoie davantage les reflets dans une pièce lumineuse. Amazon l’a déjà vendu 199,99 € fin août : la remise se mesure ici face au reste du marché, où il n’est pas descendu sous 274 € en trois mois.
- Cosori Turbo Tower 10,8 L : ses deux paniers superposés, de 4,3 L et 6,5 L, permettent de cuire deux préparations à la fois sur 30 cm de largeur de plan de travail. Comptez en revanche 40,5 cm de hauteur et 9,3 kg. Le prix le plus bas relevé ailleurs est de 187,59 €.
- Segway-Ninebot Max G2 E : bridée à 25 km/h, elle annonce 70 km d’autonomie, roule sur des pneus de 10 pouces sans chambre à air et se retrouve avec le réseau Localiser d’Apple. Ses 29,4 kg la rendent pénible à monter dans un escalier. Amazon pratique ce prix depuis début septembre, selon camelcamelcamel : c’est un prix bas installé, loin des 799,99 € de Cdiscount, plutôt qu’une vente de quelques heures.
- Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 : léger, avec 1,4 kg en aspirateur à main, et doté d’une batterie amovible de 18 V. Nous avions attribué 8/10 à la version Essential dans notre test du Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 Essential, en relevant une autonomie de 27 minutes en balai et 45 minutes à la main, une aspiration limitée et 85 dB de bruit. Il vise plutôt un petit logement qu’une grande maison.
Prix du jour ou prix habituel : comment lire ces remises
Les baisses de cette sélection vont de 7 % sur le Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro à 31 % sur le Qrevo Edge 2. Trois offres sont des baisses récentes : le Roborock F25 LT Gen2 passe 90 € sous son plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours, le Qrevo Edge 2 égale son prix le plus bas relevé depuis trois mois, et le Qrevo Curv 2 Pro aussi, mais à 50 € seulement du prix pratiqué fin septembre. Les sept autres se distinguent surtout par l’écart avec les autres marchands, sans que l’on sache toujours depuis quand Amazon applique ce tarif.
Ces écarts disent aussi ce qu’il ne faut pas en attendre. L’écran LG UltraGear s’est déjà vendu moins cher chez Amazon fin août, et le Segway affiche le même prix depuis début septembre : rien n’indique qu’ils ne reviendront pas à ce niveau d’ici le Black Friday du 27 novembre. Pour les quatre aspirateurs de la liste, notre comparatif des meilleurs aspirateurs robots permet de situer les deux Roborock face aux modèles que nous avons testés.
Ventes flash Amazon d’octobre : vos questions
Le prix barré affiché par Amazon est-il fiable ?
Amazon affiche selon les produits le prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, un prix conseillé par le fabricant ou un ancien prix médian. Seul le premier mesure une baisse récente : c’est pourquoi nous n’avons pas repris les deux autres dans cette sélection.
Le téléviseur LG 75QNED7E convient-il au jeu sur console ?
Sa fiche indique une fréquence de 60 Hz, ce qui limite les jeux à 60 images par seconde. Pour profiter du 120 Hz d’une PS5 ou d’une Xbox Series X, il faut un téléviseur compatible 120 Hz.
La trottinette Segway-Ninebot Max G2 E peut-elle dépasser 25 km/h ?
Non, sa vitesse maximale est de 25 km/h, la limite autorisée pour une trottinette électrique sur la voie publique en France. Ses 70 km d’autonomie sont une valeur annoncée par le fabricant.

articles.title: Crean un sistema para frenar compras no autorizadas por humanos: ya no se usa el número de tarjeta
articles.text:
Intent Intelligence Framework es un nuevo sistema para verificar que los asistentes de inteligencia artificial solo hagan las compras que sus usuarios autorizaron de manera explícita.
Los asistentes de IA empezaron a realizar transacciones en nombre de las personas, pero su funcionamiento no es del todo predecible y pueden terminar comprando algo distinto a lo pedido. Eso abre la puerta a compras no autorizadas y a disputas con las tarjetas de crédito.
“Estas nuevas transacciones van a tener un consumidor, un comercio y un agente”, explicó Hannah Bozian, vicepresidenta de Asociaciones y Estrategia Agéntica de American Express, con TechCrunch. Bozian agregó que la empresa quiere que esas operaciones sigan siendo “fluidas, confiables y seguras”, como esperan los titulares de las tarjetas.
Cómo funciona el nuevo sistema anti compras innecesarias
El esquema arranca con una Create Intent API, una herramienta que capta la instrucción de compra del usuario junto con las condiciones que haya puesto, como el nombre del comercio, el presupuesto máximo o preferencias del producto.
Después, el usuario confirma su identidad y avala esa instrucción. Con esa confirmación se genera un Intent ID, un identificador único, y un Proof of Intent Token que resume las condiciones que puso la persona.
Ese token se usa para generar una credencial de pago digital que el asistente utiliza en el momento de pagar, en lugar del número real de la tarjeta. Así, la compra queda protegida y limitada a lo que el usuario autorizó.
El Intent ID y el token también sirven después, para que las empresas puedan rastrear qué se autorizó, cuándo y a través de qué asistente, algo que Bozian destacó como una herramienta extra contra el fraude y en la resolución de disputas.
Nueva ‘verificación de la intención’ para hacer compras virtuales
Bozian explicó que la diferencia con otras implementaciones del mercado es que se incorpora la verificación de la intención en una etapa más temprana de la transacción. “Esto ayuda a mitigar riesgos antes de que el riesgo ocurra”, afirmó.
Como ejemplo, mencionó el caso de un usuario que le pide a su asistente comprar zapatillas Nike blancas talla 9, pero el agente termina enviando el pedido a Adidas por error. Con el nuevo esquema, ese tipo de transacción quedaría bloqueada antes de completarse.
La empresa admitió que todavía no detectó un aumento de disputas vinculado al comercio agéntico, pero prefirió anticiparse mientras esta forma de comprar gana terreno. Según un informe reciente de Amex Trendex, el 66% de los consumidores estadounidenses consultados dijo que es probable que use asistentes de IA para comparar precios en los próximos 12 meses, y el 61% para pedir recomendaciones de productos.
De otro lado, Bozian anticipó un escenario donde los agentes actúen con más autonomía, por ejemplo cuando un usuario les permita reponer artículos del hogar, como papel higiénico o servilletas, sin pedir confirmación en cada compra. En esos casos, dijo, tiene sentido que la tecnología siga chequeando que la operación coincida con lo que la persona pidió.
La IA lleva las compras hacia una gestión predictiva
La inteligencia artificial transforma las compras al automatizar tareas de abastecimiento, anticipar riesgos y orientar las decisiones de los equipos. Durante SAP Connect, Novartis, Nestlé, Morgan Foods y PwC presentaron usos de asistentes y agentes que buscan reducir trabajo manual y mejorar la relación con proveedores.
Novartis desarrolló junto con SAP un piloto de Joule Sourcing Assistant para liberar a los equipos de abastecimiento de tareas repetitivas y permitirles concentrarse en la estrategia y el vínculo con sus proveedores. Morgan Foods, a su vez, explora agentes que conecten señales de demanda, inventarios y situación de proveedores para avanzar hacia una administración más predictiva.
SAP amplía la automatización en adquisiciones y comercio exterior
Las capacidades se integran en SAP Business AI Platform, que permite crear y gobernar soluciones de IA en sistemas SAP y de terceros. La compañía también incorporó alianzas con Moody’s Corporation y ORO Labs para ampliar la automatización en abastecimiento, mientras que International Trade Assistant logró reducir hasta 50% el esfuerzo destinado a la clasificación comercial.
