articles.title: MENA startup funding jumps to $1.65 billion in Q3, with Saudi Arabia taking the lead
articles.text: Startup investment across the Middle East and North Africa more than doubled in the third quarter of 2026, driven by a wave of large Saudi fintech deals that helped revive funding activity despite persistent geopolitical uncertainty. Yet the recovery remained heavily concentrated in a handful of companies and markets, raising questions about whether the momentum can extend across the wider ecosystem. Startups across MENA raised $1.65 billion through 145 deals between July and September, up 108% from the previous quarter , while deal volume increased 39%. Despite the sharp quarterly rebound, funding remained approximately 63% below the $4.5 billion recorded during the same period last year . The recovery gained momentum in September , when regional funding exceeded $1.1 billion, following a subdued July and an August rebound driven largely by two UAE-based companies. Saudi Arabia reclaimed the lead from the UAE, accounting for the majority of capital deployed during the quarter. The composition of funding also showed a notable shift. Debt financing accounted for $441 million across 10 transactions, representing 26.8% of total investment, compared with almost 59% during 2025. Non-debt funding reached $1.21 billion, suggesting that the recovery was not solely dependent on credit-backed transactions. The quarter unfolded against a challenging geopolitical backdrop, with regional military tensions, disruptions to maritime trade and volatile energy markets complicating the investment outlook. Nevertheless, several established startups managed to secure substantial financing, demonstrating continued investor appetite for businesses with the scale and growth potential to attract large commitments. But the headline figures obscure a more uneven picture. Capital remained concentrated in fintech, Saudi Arabia and the UAE dominated the regional rankings, and male-led startups captured nearly all the funding deployed. Fintech dominates as large funding rounds return Fintech strengthened its position as the region's leading investment sector, attracting $1.03 billion across 35 transactions, equivalent to approximately 62% of total quarterly funding. Mobility ranked second, raising $285 million through just two deals, followed by e-commerce, which secured $105.6 million across nine transactions. The sector rankings highlighted the outsized influence of a handful of large funding rounds. Saudi fintech companies Barq, Tabby and Lendo alone attracted a combined $762.5 million, accounting for nearly three-quarters of the capital deployed in fintech during the quarter. Funding by stage revealed a similarly concentrated landscape. Early-stage startups accounted for the largest share of deal activity, with 94 companies raising $505.4 million. Later-stage startups secured $606 million across just seven transactions, reflecting renewed investor appetite for more mature businesses capable of attracting sizable funding commitments. Another 34 startups did not disclose their funding stages, while 10 transactions were classified as debt financing. The figures suggest that while early-stage investment remained active, a small number of established companies continued to attract a disproportionate share of available capital. Business-to-business (B2B) startups maintained their lead, securing $876.2 million across 95 transactions. Business-to-consumer (B2C) companies followed with $506.7 million across 27 deals, while the remaining $264.1 million went to startups operating across both business models. The gender funding gap, meanwhile, showed little sign of narrowing. Male-led startups attracted $1.62 billion across 116 deals, representing 98.3% of all capital raised during the quarter. Startups founded by mixed-gender teams secured $15.9 million across 13 transactions, while female-led startups raised just $12.7 million through 16 deals, accounting for less than 1% of total investment. The disparity was particularly striking given the overall recovery in funding. While capital returned to the ecosystem, the overwhelming majority flowed to male-led companies, reinforcing the persistent imbalance in access to venture capital. Saudi Arabia reclaims the lead Saudi Arabia emerged as MENA's largest startup funding market in the third quarter, attracting approximately $1 billion across 62 transactions and reclaiming the top position from the UAE. The kingdom recorded a more than tenfold increase in funding from the $102 million raised in the previous quarter, largely driven by a series of large fintech transactions announced in September. The resurgence coincided with LEAP 2026, held in Riyadh from Aug. 31 to Sept. 3, which brought together technology companies, investors and startups. However, the quarter's performance was shaped primarily by a handful of large transactions rather than an evenly distributed recovery in investment activity. Fintech was the clear driver of Saudi Arabia's funding growth, attracting $815.8 million across 16 transactions. E-commerce ranked second with $98 million raised through five deals, followed by proptech, which secured $50.3 million across four transactions. Three fintech transactions stood out. Barq closed a $329.5 million Series A round at a valuation of $1.85 billion, while Tabby raised $233 million in Series F funding, valuing the buy now, pay later company at $6.5 billion. Lendo secured another $200 million through debt financing. Together, the three transactions accounted for $762.5 million, equivalent to approximately three-quarters of the kingdom's quarterly funding and more than 90% of its fintech investment. The concentration illustrates the growing influence of Saudi fintech companies on regional funding performance, particularly as larger businesses continue to attract capital amid a challenging investment environment. Debt remained an important component of Saudi Arabia's funding landscape, accounting for $372 million across six transactions. Early-stage startups nevertheless maintained a strong presence, with 34 companies raising a combined $392.7 million. Another 19 startups did not disclose their funding stages. Saudi Arabia's performance highlighted its ability to attract sizable investment commitments despite regional uncertainty. However, the significant concentration of funding in a few fintech companies suggests that the quarter's rebound was driven more by the scale of individual transactions than a broad-based increase in investment across the ecosystem. UAE slips to second despite strong late-stage activity The UAE retreated to second place in the regional rankings after leading MENA startup funding during the previous quarter. UAE-based startups raised $507 million across 41 transactions, down 14% from the $591.3 million recorded in Q2. Despite the decline, the country continued to attract substantial later-stage investment, reinforcing its position as one of the region's most established startup funding markets. Unlike Saudi Arabia, where fintech dominated investment, mobility emerged as the UAE's largest sector, attracting $250 million through a single transaction. Fintech ranked second with $164.3 million across 15 deals, followed by healthtech, which secured $25.2 million through three transactions. Two later-stage funding rounds accounted for nearly 63% of the country's quarterly investment. Mobility company Moove raised $250 million in a Series C round, while fintech Fasset secured $68 million in its own Series C financing. Together, the transactions brought in $318 million, highlighting the continued availability of large funding commitments for more mature businesses. Early-stage investment remained comparatively active, with 29 startups securing $86.5 million. Debt financing accounted for $68 million across three transactions, while another seven startups did not disclose their funding stages. The UAE's performance reflected continued investor appetite for established businesses, even as overall funding declined from the previous quarter. Yet the reliance on a limited number of large transactions also exposed the uneven nature of the recovery. Excluding Moove and Fasset, UAE startups attracted just $189 million during the quarter, illustrating the extent to which individual deals shaped the country's funding performance. Egypt struggles to regain momentum Egypt remained the region's third-largest startup funding market, but investment activity continued to weaken as startups grappled with constrained access to capital and a shortage of sizable financing rounds. Egyptian startups raised $56.4 million across 15 transactions during the third quarter, down 22% from the $72.6 million recorded in Q2. The country's quarterly performance was heavily dependent on a single transaction. Payments infrastructure provider Paymob secured $35 million in a pre-Series C round, accounting for approximately 62% of all capital raised by Egyptian startups during the period. Without Paymob's financing, Egypt's quarterly total would have fallen to just $21.4 million, underscoring the limited availability of substantial funding for other companies. Fintech remained the country's leading investment sector, attracting $45 million across two transactions. Edtech ranked second with $3 million raised through one deal, followed by e-commerce infrastructure, which secured $2.8 million in a single transaction. Early-stage startups accounted for the majority of deal activity, with 10 companies raising a combined $19.3 million. Paymob's transaction was the country's only later-stage financing round, while debt funding accounted for $1 million across one deal. Another three startups did not disclose their funding stages. Egypt's continued slowdown reflected a more challenging investment environment, with limited capital availability and fewer large transactions weighing on the country's quarterly performance. A strong rebound, but not yet a broad recovery The third-quarter rebound pushed MENA startup funding to approximately $3.4 billion in the first nine months of 2026, providing renewed momentum after a difficult first half marked by geopolitical instability and increasingly selective investment activity. The improvement was significant. Funding more than doubled from the previous quarter, deal activity recovered, and non-debt financing accounted for more than 73% of the capital deployed. The return of sizable equity rounds also demonstrated that investors remained willing to back regional companies capable of delivering scale, even as uncertainty continued to cloud the broader economic outlook. Yet the recovery was far from evenly distributed. Saudi Arabia attracted the majority of investment, fintech absorbed more than 60% of total funding, and a handful of large transactions accounted for a substantial share of the quarter's capital. Meanwhile, Egypt continued to struggle to regain momentum, and female-led startups remained severely underfunded. The geopolitical outlook adds another layer of uncertainty. Continued military tensions, disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and potential volatility in energy markets could weigh on investor confidence and complicate funding decisions in the months ahead. With the fourth quarter underway, the sustainability of the rebound remains uncertain. The latest figures demonstrate that capital is still accessible for MENA startups, particularly those operating in established sectors and major Gulf markets. What remains less clear is whether that investment appetite can extend beyond a narrow group of companies and translate into wider access to funding. For a region that has repeatedly navigated periods of economic and geopolitical instability, the third quarter offered evidence of resilience, but not yet of a comprehensive recovery. The third quarter proved that MENA startups can still attract large funding commitments. The fourth will test whether that capital can reach a broader range of companies, sectors and markets. articles.title: Apple tiene nuevo hogar inteligente con HomeView, Apple TV 4K y HomePod mini 2: precio, disponibilidad y características
articles.text:
Apple renueva su apuesta por el hogar inteligente con el lanzamiento de HomeView, una pantalla con Siri AI, un Apple TV 4K actualizado y el HomePod mini 2. La compañía presentó los tres dispositivos durante Welcome Home, una jornada dirigida a reforzar su ecosistema doméstico conectado y ampliar el papel de la inteligencia artificial.
Apple busca reunir en sus equipos el control de luces, cámaras, cerraduras y termostatos, además de acceso a entretenimiento y comunicaciones. La estrategia incorpora una pantalla doméstica propia y actualiza dos productos que ya funcionaban como centros de control dentro de la aplicación Casa. El despliegue, no obstante, dependerá de los mercados y del idioma.
HomeView incorpora una pantalla de siete pulgadas para gestionar la casa
El nuevo HomeView combina una pantalla Liquid Retina de siete pulgadas, un altavoz y una central para el hogar conectado. Apple lo ofrecerá en una versión de sobremesa con base de altavoz regulable y en otra preparada para fijarse a la pared. El modelo de mesa llegará en plata, blanco estrella, rosa y gris espacial.
Su sistema reconoce hasta seis rostros y adapta la información de cada perfil, con acceso separado a mensajes, calendarios, recordatorios y aplicaciones. También permite videollamadas mediante FaceTime y cambia el contenido según la distancia del usuario.
El equipo integra el chip A18, Apple Intelligence y Siri AI para comprender peticiones más complejas y utilizar el contexto de dispositivos compatibles. Si se vincula a un iPhone o iPad, puede consultar información personal de Calendario, Mensajes o Apple Music para responder a solicitudes concretas.
En la vivienda, permite gestionar accesorios compatibles con Matter, mostrar hasta nueve cámaras y detectar personas, mascotas, paquetes o vehículos con un plan compatible de iCloud+.
Apple TV 4K incorpora chip A19, WiFi 7 y funciones de Siri AI
El nuevo Apple TV 4K conserva el diseño de la generación anterior, pero cambia los componentes internos. Su procesador A19 aumenta el rendimiento de la CPU hasta un 50% y duplica la potencia gráfica respecto al modelo previo, según la información presentada. El dispositivo incorpora también un decodificador AV1 para mejorar la reproducción de contenidos en streaming.
La conectividad suma WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 y HDMI 2.1, mientras mantiene Dolby Vision y Dolby Atmos. Tres micrófonos de largo alcance permiten activar Siri sin utilizar el mando.
El equipo podrá controlar accesorios domésticos desde el televisor y mostrar imágenes de cámaras o videoporteros. Además, permitirá conectar hasta cuatro altavoces HomePod para crear un sistema de sonido envolvente. La configuración será compatible con los HomePod mini 2 y los HomePod de segunda generación, con ajustes automáticos de sincronización y niveles de audio según su posición en la habitación.
HomePod mini 2 mantiene su diseño e incorpora el chip S10
El HomePod mini 2 llega seis años después del modelo original, presentado en octubre de 2020. Mantiene su forma esférica recubierta de tela y su superficie táctil, pero incorpora un procesador S10, WiFi 7, Bluetooth, Thread y banda ultraancha. Estará disponible en rosa, verde, azul, blanco y negro.
El altavoz conserva un transductor de rango completo, dos radiadores pasivos y cuatro micrófonos para interactuar a distancia con Siri. También permite formar parejas estéreo, reproducir música en varias habitaciones mediante AirPlay y utilizar un Mac como fuente de audio.
Las funciones de Siri AI llegarán posteriormente mediante una actualización de software. La plataforma reconocerá hasta seis voces y, al conectarse con un iPhone o iPad compatible, podrá utilizar datos de aplicaciones personales para responder con mayor contexto. El equipo también podrá controlar luces, persianas, cerraduras y termostatos, además de detectar alarmas de humo o monóxido de carbono. Costará 299 dólares y llegará en noviembre próximo.
Precio, disponibilidad y límites de Siri AI
El HomeView tendrá un precio de 299 dólares, con reservas desde el 13 de octubre y llegada al mercado el 13 de noviembre. Apple prevé venderlo inicialmente en Estados Unidos, Reino Unido, Canadá y Australia.
El dispositivo no estará disponible por ahora en la Unión Europea, incluida España. Apple atribuye esa decisión a que Siri AI todavía no está habilitada en iOS en ese territorio y señaló que mantiene conversaciones con las autoridades europeas para encontrar una solución.
El nuevo Apple TV 4K costará 349 euros, también podrá reservarse desde el 13 de octubre y llegará el 13 de noviembre. El HomePod mini 2 tendrá un precio de 169 euros, con reservas desde la jornada de presentación y disponibilidad desde el 30 de octubre en los mercados anunciados.
Las funciones avanzadas de Siri AI estarán disponibles inicialmente en inglés y en determinados países. Por ese motivo, España no contará desde el lanzamiento con las nuevas capacidades de inteligencia artificial ni en HomeView, ni en Apple TV 4K, ni en HomePod mini 2.

articles.title: Azerbaijan blocks TikTok, Instagram, and X amid growing protests over hijab rules
articles.text:
Azerbaijan blocks TikTok, Instagram, and X amid growing protests over hijab rules
Internet monitor NetBlocks and VPN provider Surfshark confirm widespread social media restrictions on multiple providers as civil unrest grows.
- TikTok, Instagram, and X (formerly Twitter) have been restricted on multiple internet providers in Azerbaijan.
- The digital blackout follows growing citizen protests over the regulation of hijabs in local schools.
- Data from Surfshark reveals a 29% global increase in internet blackouts, with 81 new restrictions implemented across 21 countries last year
Citizens in Azerbaijan are experiencing severe social media restrictions today as the government cracks down on digital communication amid escalating protests.
Internet monitor NetBlocks confirmed that access to TikTok, Instagram, and X has been blocked across multiple internet service providers in the country.
The incident comes as citizens protest the regulation of hijabs in local schools. By restricting access to major social networks, authorities appear to be attempting to stifle the flow of information, making it difficult for protesters to organize and share on-the-ground footage with the rest of the world.
A growing history of digital censorship
While this latest shutdown is alarming, it is not an isolated incident. According to data from Surfshark's Internet Shutdown Tracker, this is the fourth restriction incident in Azerbaijan over the past six years.
Notably, this marks the first time an internet disruption in the country has been directly triggered by protests. The previous three cases were tied to broader political turmoil, encompassing three service-based restrictions targeting social media and Voice over IP (VoIP) applications, as well as one regional network disruption.
This worsening track record places Azerbaijan 14th in Asia for internet restriction incidents. According to Surfshark, this puts the nation alongside countries notorious for heavy-handed internet censorship, such as China, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan.
The global censorship epidemic
The outage in Azerbaijan mirrors a devastating broader trend. From Surfshark's 2025 global overview, it is clear that worldwide internet censorship is accelerating at a frightening pace.
Governments imposed 81 new internet restrictions across 21 countries last year, a staggering 29% increase compared to the previous year. Asia remains the undisputed leader in digital blackouts, responsible for 56 new restrictions that impacted approximately 2.2 billion people. India secured the top spot in the region with 24 new restrictions alone.
Social media platforms are increasingly finding themselves in the crosshairs. Surfshark data reveals that Telegram was the most frequently blocked platform globally last year, facing restrictions from seven different governments on nine occasions.
Meanwhile, 51 of the 81 new global restrictions were directly linked to political turmoil, while six countries imposed blackouts specifically in response to protests.
The sheer volume of these outages is reshaping how the world communicates. "Internet shutdowns, including long-term, systemic censorship, affected 4.6 billion people in 2025, more than half of the world’s population," said Luís Costa, Research Lead at Surfshark.
Costa highlighted that these tactics are spreading to new regions. "Despite growing global recognition of internet access as a fundamental human right, the scale and reach of digital restrictions continue to expand year after year."
"In 2025 alone, two new countries—Albania and Panama—implemented internet restrictions for the first time, highlighting how government-mandated shutdowns are no longer confined to a small group of repeat offenders, but are becoming an increasingly used tool of control worldwide," he explained.
As governments tighten their grip on free speech, privacy tools are transitioning from optional privacy enhancements to critical lifelines. If you find yourself in a region facing sudden censorship, understanding how a VPN works is the first step toward reclaiming your right to a free and open internet.
Rene Millman is a seasoned technology journalist whose work has appeared in The Guardian, the Financial Times, Computer Weekly, and IT Pro. With over two decades of experience as a reporter and editor, he specializes in making complex topics like cybersecurity, VPNs, and enterprise software accessible and engaging.

articles.title: FR-Alert : votre téléphone va peut-être recevoir une alerte ce mardi 13 octobre
articles.text:
Aujourd'hui, les téléphones de beaucoup de Français reçoivent ou vont recevoir une alerte. Mais ne vous inquiétez pas, ce n'est qu'un exercice !
La France a déployé depuis 2022 son dispositif dit FR-Alert, qui permet d'envoyer une alerte sur les smartphones de toutes les personnes concernées sur une zone, en utilisant les ondes radio. Un système qui permet de prévenir les Français en cas de danger, sauf aujourd'hui, ne vous inquiétez pas !
Un message d'alerte envoyé à de nombreux français durant cette Journée nationale de la résilience
Si vous ne le saviez pas, aujourd'hui, le mardi 13 octobre 2026, c'est la Journée nationale de la résilience. Et à cette occasion, l'alerte FR-Alert a été envoyée ou le sera dans la journée à des habitants de nombreux départements du pays.
Pour ceux qui n'étaient pas à au fait du programme, les autorités ont appelé les habitants à ne pas paniquer. « Pas d'inquiétude, il s'agira d'un exercice destiné à tester les dispositifs d'alerte et de sécurité » a ainsi précisé la Préfecture de Corrèze, dans un message publié sur ses réseaux sociaux.
Le Nord et le Pas-de-Calais vont recevoir une alerte le jeudi 15 octobre
À noter qu'il s'agit d'une alerte qui touchent les zones accueillant un site sensible. En Seine-et-Marne ainsi, « le FR-Alert sera mis en œuvre sur l'ensemble des zones concernées par un site Seveso doté d'un plan particulier d'intervention ». En Maine-et-Loire, cela a concerné l'usine chimique Zach Systems, près d'Angers, quand en Saône-et-Loire, seule la commune de Gueugnon (où existe une installation Seveso seuil haut) doit recevoir une alerte.
À noter par ailleurs que la mise à l'essai de ce dispositif va connaître une autre séquence, qui va toucher cette fois les départements du Nord et du Pas-de-Calais, le jeudi 15 octobre. Pour le premier, il s'agira d'une alerte pour la zone à 2 kilomètres autour de l'usine Kuhlmann de Loos, et pour le second, un périmètre de 1,6 kilomètre autour du site industriel Croda de Chocques.

articles.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Game Ready for Dozens of AAA Titles at Launch, Including DLSS 5 and Anti-Cheat Support
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
NVIDIA RTX Spark Game Ready for Dozens of AAA Titles at Launch, Including DLSS 5 and Anti-Cheat Support
NVIDIA today announced that its new RTX Spark superchip that will power the next-generation of AI-native PCs, will be Game Ready for dozens of AAA games at launch on Windows 11, providing an uncompromising gaming experience that's maxed out for 1440p. The RTX Spark superchip features a 20-core Grace CPU and a GeForce RTX Blackwell iGPU featuring 6,144 CUDA cores. NVIDIA is closely collaborating with Microsoft and the various game developers to ensure not just Spark-native ports of popular titles, but also seamless translation of games to the RTX Spark platform for both the system- and graphics APIs.
A key announcement here is that NVIDIA is working with developers of competitive online games to ensure that their anti-cheat solutions work seamlessly with RTX Spark. Modern anti-cheat solutions rely heavily on kernel-mode interactions with hardware to ensure trust, something that has the potential to break in scenarios where games originally developed for Windows x64 machines are made to run on Windows Arm64 machine through translation layers. NVIDIA's developer collaboration ensures that the hardware-end of the anti-cheat trust-chain remains intact, and you should be able to play your favorite online games such as Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, Fortnite, Marvel Rivals, NARAKA: BLADEPOINT, Rocket League, RUST, THE FINALS, War Thunder, World of Tanks, and more.Since it features a powerful iGPU based on the "Blackwell" graphics architecture with hardware readiness for Neural Rendering, NVIDIA is extending DLSS 5 to RTX Spark, including its key feature, 3D-guided Neural Rendering, which utilizes AI to generate lifelike lighting and material details that traditional rendering constraints typically restrict.
NVIDIA announced that it is working with game developers to port their games to native RTX Spark Windows versions. These would be Windows Arm64 versions with a high degree of optimization for the NVIDIA Grace CPU, Blackwell iGPU, and the memory architecture of RTX Spark notebooks and desktops. A big announcement here is that the 2027 "Call of Duty" release by Activision will include an RTX Spark version that's built from the ground up for the hardware.
NVIDIA released in-game footage captured on RTX Spark machines from a dozen game developers, you can catch all these videos in the source link below. NVIDIA RTX Spark launches on October 16.

articles.title: Ahold Delhaize takes systems offline after cyberattack — global retail giant says 'cybersecurity incident' hit systems, but stores remain open
articles.text:
Ahold Delhaize takes systems offline after cyberattack — global retail giant says 'cybersecurity incident' hit systems, but stores remain open
Ahold Delhaize loses its hold on cybersecurity once again
- Ahold Delhaize took systems offline after a cyberattack, though details remain limited
- Disruptions affected employee services and customer-facing websites across multiple retail brands
- Company is investigating the incident amid concerns of another major ransomware-related attack
Ahold Delhaize has suffered a cyberattack that forced it to pull parts of its IT network offline.
On October 12, 2026, the retail giant issued a brief statement, saying it is experiencing a “security issue” within its network. “Our teams are taking steps to assess and mitigate the issue,” it said. “This includes taking some systems offline to help protect them. At this time, our stores are open and serving customers.”
We don’t know which parts of the operation were affected, how the attack took place, and whether or not any sensitive company or customer data was exposed. We don’t know if customers were affected, how many, and to what extent.
Usually, when a company shuts down its network to contain an incident, it is due to a ransomware attack and its data exfiltration efforts. However, no threat actors have yet claimed responsibility for this attack, and no data has surfaced on the dark web, at press time.
“Protecting our infrastructure in the best interest of our customers, associates and partners is a top priority,” the company concluded. “We apologize for any inconvenience this issue may have caused customers and partners.”
Hackers get ahold of Delhaize
Ahold Delhaize is a wholesale company and a multinational retailer running more than 9,400 stores across the United States, Europe, and Indonesia.
It counts roughly 400,000 employees, which serve some 60 million customers weekly, both in stores, and online. Brands under its umbrella include Delhaize, Maxi, Mega Image, Albert, bol, Alfa Beta, Etos, Gall & Gall, and Profi in Europe, and Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Giant Food, and Hannaford in the American market, as per BleepingComputer.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Unfortunately, it has plenty of experience with cyberattacks. In mid-November 2024, an attack on the company resulted in grocery stores and pharmacies in the US being unable to service their customers properly. Even then, Ahold Delhaize shut down parts of its network to contain the attack and had trouble with disabled phone lines. It was later confirmed that it was a ransomware attack launched by the INC Ransom threat actor.
In the attack, the hackers stole sensitive data on more than 2.2 million people, the company later confirmed via a filing with the Maine Attorney General’s Office. It said the data may have included internal employment records for both current and former employees.
The combination of stolen data varied from person to person, but generally, it included full names, postal addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, government-issued ID numbers, bank account numbers, health information, and other employment-related information.
Trouble for the retailers
That attack, which apparently took more than a week to remedy, was disruptive enough to have employees voicing their annoyance on social media. At one point, the pharmacy at Stop & Shop could not refill prescriptions. The Food Lion, on the other hand, had to address missing and delayed deliveries. Instacart orders return dates were constantly being pushed back.
BleepingComputer noted employees at the Stop & Shop American regional supermarket chain are now having trouble accessing their schedules and pay stubs as a direct consequence of the latest attack. Customers have been unable to use websites, apps, and customer service platforms at Albert Heijn, Etos, and Gall & Gall stores in the Netherlands, and Delhaize in Belgium.
The publication also reported, citing an internal memo shared by Lion Food employees in the United States, that the company flagged the attack as an IT outage, and told staff their “store may be unable to shop, stage, or hand off orders.”

articles.title: Deliverance AI puts sovereign AI control to the continuity test - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Deliverance AI puts sovereign AI control to the continuity test
Sovereign AI control is becoming a business continuity issue as autonomous agents take on essential enterprise workflows. Keeping data within national boundaries addresses part of the challenge, but organizations also need control over agent behavior, external dependencies and the economics of keeping those systems operational.
Regulated enterprises need more than access to powerful models and computing infrastructure. They need software and expertise that turn those capabilities into governed production workflows, according to Mick McNeil (pictured), founder and chief executive officer of Deliverance AI Ltd.
“It’s our view that the value and the criticality in terms of business continuity does not sit with the model choice. It sits with the layer that governs the models,” he said.
McNeil spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante for the “Sovereign AI: From Strategy to Reality” video series, during an exclusive interview on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how enterprises can govern AI agents within their own environments, preserve model choice and link sovereignty requirements to measurable business outcomes. (* Disclosure below.)
Sovereign AI control starts with the operating boundary
Deliverance’s control plane observes agent activity, enforces policies and provides audit trails and a kill switch. Those safeguards help protect sensitive data and maintain operational control as agents execute enterprise workflows, McNeil explained.
“We partner with HPE; deploy a full-stack capability that’s storage, network, GPUs and all software; and go directly into the customer data center,” he said. “Only then, whenever they own the boundary around the agentic system, can they truly say that they have full control over the actions and the telemetry going in and out of that system.”
The requirements vary across government, defense, pharmaceutical and financial services organizations. Some customers need air-gapped deployments, while others accept selected external connections; those choices depend on their operating context and the risks they are prepared to take, McNeil noted.
“Our customers are the ones who own the keys to their infrastructure, plus the software on top of it,” he said. “That’s unquestionable and very explicit in how we go to market.”
Model options support workflow resilience
A customer-controlled environment still needs a strategy for dependencies outside its boundary. Deliverance’s routing technology supports frontier and open-source models, letting enterprises choose capabilities for individual workflows while planning alternatives if provider access changes, according to McNeil.
“When you purchase our products as a subscription — our operating system, the control plane — you buy the ability to deploy any model, frontier and open source,” he said. “Those mission-critical workflows have the ability to fall back to an open-source model if the frontier model gets restricted or to a different open-source model if your primary model is open source.”
Sovereign AI control also raises questions about what customers retain when a supplier relationship ends. Customers retain ownership of their agents, integrations, audit trails and accumulated learning, although transferring those assets between platforms remains a separate challenge, McNeil explained.
“Agents are becoming portable,” he said. “The market has not yet created the framework that enables all agentic organizations to port agents between different platforms, but we are leading in that thought leadership.”
Economics and expertise turn control into outcomes
Model routing also supports cost management by matching AI model capabilities and expenses to specific workloads. Deliverance assesses where agents can improve business performance, distinguishing productivity gains from measurable financial outcomes, according to McNeil.
“We deploy agents and AI at scale to defer future costs. That’s a very clear and impactful outcome on your [profit and loss],” he said.
Deliverance joined HPE’s Unleash AI partner program to bring its agentic operating system to HPE Private Cloud AI, co-developed with Nvidia Corp. Embedded engineers maintain the platform and build workflows, while strategic value advisors help customers prioritize opportunities based on return on investment, time to value and risk, McNeil explained.
“We’re about to launch a joint solution, which is HPE’s sovereign agentic knowledge engagement, that enables customers — within 90 days — to click and deploy a full-stack agentic operating system into their own environment in the most sovereign way,” he said. “For me, [enabling] enterprises to move quickly in a way that they trust the technology, trust the workflows [and] trust the agents is the key to growth and prosperity of enterprises around the world.”

articles.title: Biotecnología: este es el plan para para filtrar la sangre de bebés con sepsis en Europa
articles.text:
La empresa austríaca Efferon recibió el 22 de abril de 2026 la primera certificación europea para un dispositivo que filtra la sangre de bebés y chicos con sepsis. Es el primero de su tipo aprobado en la Unión Europea para uso pediátrico.
El dispositivo, llamado Efferon NEO, obtuvo la marca CE MDR, el equivalente europeo a la aprobación de la FDA (la agencia que autoriza medicamentos y dispositivos médicos en Estados Unidos), otorgada por el organismo certificador 3EC International.
La sepsis es una de las principales causas de muerte infantil en el mundo: provoca más de tres millones de muertes de chicos por año y representa la mitad de todos los casos de sepsis a nivel global, según datos de la compañía. Entre los pacientes más vulnerables, la mortalidad llega al 50%.
Los números del estudio clínico
La aprobación se apoyó en el estudio multicéntrico LASSO NEO, que incluyó a 78 chicos de entre un mes y 14 años tratados en ocho centros médicos. De ellos, 32 recibieron el dispositivo y 46 integraron el grupo de control con el tratamiento habitual.
La mortalidad a 28 días fue del 9% en el grupo tratado con Efferon NEO, frente al 35% en el grupo de control, una diferencia estadísticamente significativa. Los chicos tratados también dejaron de necesitar respirador y medicación para sostener la presión arterial antes que el resto.
El puntaje pSOFA, que mide la gravedad de la falla multiorgánica en pediatría, bajó a 4,9 puntos al séptimo día entre los chicos tratados, frente a 7,8 puntos en el grupo de control. La mitad de los pacientes tratados dejó de necesitar respirador artificial hacia el sexto día, contra el día 37 en el grupo de control.
El jefe de terapia intensiva del Centro Médico Multidisciplinario Infantil de Tecnologías Médicas Avanzadas de San Petersburgo, Mikhail Rusak, participó del estudio y calificó el resultado de inesperado. “Hasta ahora, ningún estudio de gran escala había mostrado un efecto de la adsorción de endotoxinas sobre la reducción de la mortalidad”, señaló.
Cómo funciona el filtro de sangre
El dispositivo extrae la sangre del paciente, la hace pasar por un cartucho con un material polimérico y se la devuelve filtrada. Ese proceso elimina al mismo tiempo las endotoxinas, sustancias tóxicas que liberan las bacterias, y las citoquinas, las moléculas que disparan la inflamación descontrolada que caracteriza a la sepsis.
“Desde que se demostró la eficacia de Efferon LPS en pacientes adultos con sepsis, quedó claro que negarles a los chicos el acceso a esa terapia que puede salvarles la vida sería simplemente poco ético”, dijo el cofundador y director de tecnología de la empresa, Ivan Bessonov.
Según explicó el propio Bessonov, el dispositivo ataca al mismo tiempo dos frentes del problema: el origen bacteriano de la infección y la respuesta inflamatoria descontrolada que el cuerpo desencadena para combatirla.
La versión pediátrica se diseñó para adaptarse al menor volumen de sangre que circula en el cuerpo de un bebé o un niño, a diferencia de un cartucho pensado para adultos. Puede usarse en pacientes de hasta 18 años.
El cofundador y director ejecutivo de Efferon, Dima Romashin, describió la certificación como “un hito central, no solo para la empresa, sino para la medicina crítica en general” y dijo que la compañía entra así “en un mercado de 40.000 millones de dólares que las soluciones existentes dejaron desatendido durante mucho tiempo”.
Expansión y próximos pasos
La tecnología de Efferon, que incluye tanto la versión para adultos como la pediátrica, ya se usó en más de 25.000 tratamientos en más de 40 países, entre ellos Australia, el Reino Unido, Alemania y Arabia Saudita.
La versión específica para chicos, Efferon NEO, ya se utiliza en unidades de terapia intensiva de unos 30 países, entre ellos hospitales europeos, Arabia Saudita y Tailandia, según datos de la empresa citados por TechCrunch.
Romashin, un emprendedor serial que asumió como director ejecutivo de Efferon a principios de este año para comercializar la tecnología, suele señalar que la sepsis en general mata a más de 11 millones de personas por año en el mundo, entre chicos y adultos, muy por encima de la inversión y la atención médica que recibe la enfermedad.
Efferon fue seleccionada este año entre las 200 startups de la competencia Startup Battlefield de TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. La compañía nació en 2016 a partir de tecnología desarrollada por investigadores de la Universidad Estatal de Moscú y hoy tiene su sede central en Villach, Austria.
Esa tecnología generó hasta ahora más de un millón de euros en ingresos acumulados, de acuerdo con cifras publicadas por la empresa.
La empresa espera cerrar este año con 2 millones de dólares en ingresos anualizados y ya prepara la presentación de su pedido de aprobación ante la agencia de medicamentos de Estados Unidos, a través de una vía regulatoria pensada para dispositivos que atienden a poblaciones de pacientes reducidas.

articles.title: Windows 11 23H2 vit ses dernières semaines, les entreprises ont un mois pour réagir
articles.text:
Les dernières éditions de Windows 11 23H2 encore prises en charge recevront leur ultime patch de sécurité le mois prochain. Pour les organisations qui n'ont pas encore terminé leur migration, il va falloir accélérer le mouvement.
Les fins de support se succèdent chez Microsoft. Alors que le Patch Tuesday de ce 13 octobre marque la fin des mises à jour de sécurité pour Windows 11 24H2 Famille et Pro, une autre version du système connaîtra le même sort dans quatre semaines, mais pour un public différent. Microsoft vient de rappeler aux organisations qui n'ont pas encore achevé leur migration que les éditions Entreprise, Éducation et IoT Entreprise de Windows 11 23H2 arriveront comme prévu au terme de leur prise en charge le 10 novembre prochain.
La solution tout-en-un pour protéger votre entreprise
Votre petite entreprise a de grandes ambitions. Protégez-là contre les pirates. Et développez sereinement votre activité !
Un mois pour une mise à niveau complète
Lancée en octobre 2023, Windows 11 23H2 devait bénéficier de trois ans de maintenance pour les entreprises et les établissements scolaires, contre deux ans pour les éditions Famille et Pro, dont le support a pris fin en novembre 2025. Après le Patch Tuesday de novembre, les machines concernées continueront de fonctionner, mais les nouvelles failles découvertes dans le système ne seront plus corrigées.
Pour continuer de recevoir des correctifs de sécurité, les organisations devront donc passer à Windows 11 25H2, dont les éditions Entreprise et Éducation seront maintenues jusqu'en octobre 2028, ou à Windows 11 26H2, disponible depuis fin septembre et pris en charge jusqu'en octobre 2029.
Attention toutefois, le passage de Windows 11 23H2 à 25H2 ou 26H2 nécessite une mise à niveau complète du système, contrairement au petit paquet d'activation proposé aux machines déjà sous 24H2 ou 25H2. Les organisations devront donc prévoir un déploiement plus conséquent, après avoir vérifié la compatibilité de leurs équipements et de leurs pilotes avec la version choisie.
La fin de support correspond à la date après laquelle Microsoft ne publie plus de correctifs de sécurité, même si le PC continue de démarrer et de fonctionner. En entreprise, cela augmente rapidement le risque d’exploitation de failles, car les vulnérabilités découvertes après cette date restent ouvertes. Cela pose aussi des problèmes de conformité (politiques internes, audits, exigences assurantielles) qui demandent souvent un OS encore maintenu. En pratique, rester sur une version hors support oblige à compenser par des mesures de réduction de surface d’attaque, rarement équivalentes à un patching régulier.
Le Patch Tuesday est la fenêtre mensuelle de publication des correctifs de sécurité Microsoft, généralement le deuxième mardi du mois. Il regroupe des mises à jour pour Windows et d’autres composants, avec des bulletins qui détaillent les vulnérabilités corrigées et leur criticité. Pour les organisations, c’est un jalon de gestion des risques : qualification en préproduction, validation applicative, puis déploiement contrôlé. Quand une version de Windows arrive en fin de support, ce cycle s’arrête pour elle, ce qui rend la gestion des failles beaucoup plus compliquée.
Une mise à niveau complète réinstalle en profondeur une nouvelle version de Windows 11 (nouveau build), avec un processus plus long, davantage de changements système et donc plus de points de compatibilité à vérifier. Un paquet d’activation est un petit correctif qui “déverrouille” des fonctionnalités déjà présentes dans le système via les mises à jour cumulatives, ce qui réduit le temps d’arrêt et les risques de régression. En entreprise, cela change la stratégie de déploiement : la mise à niveau complète ressemble à un mini-projet (tests pilotes, pilotes, chiffrement, applicatifs), alors que l’activation se gère plus comme une mise à jour mensuelle. La contrainte majeure est que l’activation n’est possible que si la base système est déjà sur une branche compatible.

articles.title: Can the RAM crisis get any worse? Quite possibly, as Intel CEO reportedly predicts another 2 to 3 years of pain, and DDR4 price has shot up 24% over the last 3 months
articles.text:
RAM is getting pricier than ever, with DDR4 up 24% in the last quarter — and Intel's CEO has reportedly said we have another 2 to 3 years of this
Reasonable prices are becoming even more of a distant memory
- Intel's CEO has said that AI hardware will be in short supply for the next 2 to 3 years
- Of course, this refers to the ongoing memory crisis, and consumers will get shorter shrift than AI players
- A new report from Barclays also shows that contract pricing for RAM has risen 24% over the past quarter for DDR4 (and 20% for DDR5)
Need more fuel to stoke the idea that the RAM crisis is here to stay? Doubtless you don't, but sadly we've had a couple more indications that the memory shortage will last for a depressingly long time, with Intel's CEO the latest to weigh in.
Wccftech reports that Intel's Lip-Bu Tan was speaking in Singapore at the Asia Future Forward event, a conference organized by DBS Bank, where the CEO discussed his thoughts regarding trends with AI – including the amount of memory it's eating up.
As flagged by Theresa Perrin on X, Tan observed that "AI hardware will stay in short supply for the next 2 to 3 years" — primarily referring to memory — and that this was "driven by persistent constraints in the underlying tech supply chain."
While the CEO is talking directly about RAM (as well as GPUs, and to an extent CPUs) used in data centers for AI applications, the fact that the AI industry is going to be short on supply for perhaps the next three years means that consumer RAM is going to be even thinner on the ground. It's no secret that the greater profits to be had by catering to the AI industry mean that this memory is the priority for chip makers.
Wccftech also noticed another post on X, from 456X, highlighting a new report from Barclays that shows contract pricing (from chip makers) for DDR4 RAM has risen 24% over the last three months, and that DDR5 has gone up 20%.
Barclays further observed that one of the big memory chip makers, Micron, will see its supply levels of RAM remain constrained through 2028. In other words, we can expect that memory supply is going to keep on being a major problem for the next two years, with 'through' 2028 meaning that this year is included in the gloomy prediction.
Analysis: yet more doom nuggets — and then there's the rise of the robots
The reported rises in the contract price of RAM according to Barclays match what we've seen at retail over the past few months, with some notable jumps in the price of DDR5 memory (which in Germany has reached a ridiculous level of 544% up on the price it was before the RAM crisis began last July).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
What Barclays, and Intel's CEO, are now telling us is that this kind of pain is likely to continue, and that RAM supply will continue to be frustratingly short until 2029. Unfortunately these kinds of forecasts are becoming more commonplace, with pretty much everyone's view appearing to align with the idea of the RAM crisis hanging around until the end of the decade.
At the very least, we can expect 2027 to be a repeat of this year — meaning more memory prices hikes, and other components besides, such as GPUs — with 2028 likely to follow in a similar vein. Indeed, Micron has said as much itself, while letting us know that robots (or 'physical AI') will be eating up a lot of RAM supply in the future.

articles.title: Avec des partenaires de renom, Apple s'attaque à la sécurisation et au pilotage de votre maison
articles.text:
Avec des partenaires de renom, Apple s'attaque à la sécurisation et au pilotage de votre maison
Apple étend son écosystème domotique avec une gamme complète d'appareils connectés, baptisée Home Collection. Conçue par ses partenaires LG et Schneider, elle compte des caméras, thermostats et serrures connectés, le tout pilotable depuis son tout nouvel écran intelligent HomeView.
C'est une petite révolution à Cupertino. Apple ne se contente plus de ses segments historiques (informatique, téléphonie, audio, montres et clés TV) et investit désormais bien plus largement l'univers de la maison. Le constructeur ne se limite pas à l'annonce d'un écran connecté, le HomeView, servant de hub domotique au cœur de la maison, mais dévoile un écosystème complet d'accessoires permettant de piloter et sécuriser le domicile. Cette gamme est conçue en partenariat avec des spécialistes du genre que sont LG et Schneider. L'occasion pour le Californien de lancer ce qu'il appelle son Apple Home Collection.
Conçus pour fonctionner avec l'application Apple Home (Maison dans notre tumultueuse contrée), les appareils en question sont pensés pour être reliés au HomeView, lequel met à profit Siri AI, sur lequel nous ne vous ferons pas l'affront de revenir. Nous nous contenterons de rappeler que si l'assistant dopé à l'intelligence artificielle est bien disponible en français, il n'est pas accessible sur le Vieux Continent pour cause de bisbille avec les instances européennes. Cela explique que l'intégralité de la nouvelle gamme de produits soit uniquement attendue aux États-Unis et au Canada, où le HomeView est annoncé.
Caméras, serrure et thermostats : le détail des nouveaux accessoires connectés
Ces produits se déclinent en une gamme complète. On y trouve la bagatelle de quatre caméras connectées, dont le flux peut évidemment être consulté depuis l'écran intelligent HomeView fraîchement présenté par le fabricant. La Video Doorbell prend la forme d'une sonnette connectée dotée d'une caméra 2,5 K, la Floodlight Cam est une caméra extérieure pensée pour la vision nocturne et la détection de mouvements, l'Outdoor Cam en est une déclinaison simplifiée et l'Indoor Cam se destine à l'intérieur du domicile. L'ensemble de ces caméras est conçu par LG. Le Sud-Coréen livre en outre un Smart Deadbolt Lock, soit une serrure connectée pouvant être déverrouillée à l'aide d'un iPhone ou d'une Apple Watch, mais aussi d'un code numérique.
Deux thermostats s'ajoutent à cette gamme déjà complète. On doit le premier à LG et le second à Schneider Electric ; ils permettent tous deux de piloter un chauffage connecté ou encore de vérifier l'humidité ambiante du domicile.
Prix et disponibilité des équipements Apple Home Collection
Côté tarifs, il faut compter entre 199 et 399 $ pour les caméras connectées, tandis que les thermostats de LG et Schneider sont tous deux facturés 199 $ (avec un capteur de température additionnel à 39 $ pour LG). La serrure est pour sa part facturée 349 $. L'ensemble de ces produits sera commercialisé à compter de décembre 2026.

articles.title: 8BitDo Launches Ultimate 3C+ Wireless Controller with Thumb Stick Tension Adjustment and Extra Buttons
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
8BitDo Launches Ultimate 3C+ Wireless Controller with Thumb Stick Tension Adjustment and Extra Buttons
8BitDo has officially launched the latest version of its Ultimate Wireless controller, the Ultimate 3C+, which is, for an intents and purposes, a more affordable version of the recently revealed special edition Ultimate 3 Wireless controllers. The Ultimate 3C comes in at a pre-order price of $39.99 on Amazon, and it will officially be launched for regular purchase on October 30. The controller itself is based on the same Xbox design as most of 8BitDo's Ultimate controllers—meaning it features the ABXY face buttons and offset thumb sticks—and it is compatible with both Android and Windows via 2.4 GHz, USB-C wired, and Bluetooth 5.4 LE connections, with the 2.4 GHz connection offering 1 kHz polling for reduced input latency. 
The 8BitDo Ultimate 3C+ has a number of flagship-tier features, like TMR joysticks with adjustable tension, separate trigger vibration motors that sync with the controller rumble, lockable back paddles, additional L/R4 shoulder buttons, Hall effect triggers with both linear and non-linear control modes, and magnetic storage on the controller for the 2.4 GHz receiver. 8BitDo says that the 500 mAh battery in the Ultimate 3C controller is able to power the controller for up to 20 hours when using the 2.4 GHz connection, while Bluetooth stretches that to 32 hours.The 8BitDo Ultimate 3C+ Wireless controller is currently available in three colorways: Stealth Black, Avocado Green, and Frost White, and it's likely that there will be more colors down the line. Compared to the Ultimate 3 Wireless controller, the 3C+ lacks the interchangeable d-pad and face buttons, 3.5 mm audio jack, and alternative thumb stick toppers. It also doesn't ship with the charging dock that doubles as a wireless receiver.

articles.title: Bitcoin: cuál es su precio este día
articles.text:
El bitcoin fue la primera criptomoneda que salió al mercado. Ideada por Satoshi Nakamoto en 2008, esta divisa digital promovía un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales luego de la crisis financiera mundial que se vivió ese año.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
El precio de la criptomoneda bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 83287.78 dólares. Esto quiere decir que la moneda digital tuvo un cambio de 0.75% en el último día, así como un movimiento de 0.0% en la última hora.
Por su nivel de capitalización, esta moneda digital ocupa la posición #1 entre las más populares.
Bitcoin alcanzó su máximo histórico
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.

articles.title: Ubitium raises $14M to build universal processor for machines that perceive, think and act - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Ubitium raises $14M to build universal processor for machines that perceive, think and act
Ubitium GmbH, a German semiconductor startup developing a universal processor for machines that perceive, think and act in the real world, today announced it has raised $14 million in additional seed funding led by Ibex Investors.
OpenOcean participated in the round alongside existing investors including KBC Focus Fund, Runa Capital and Inflection. Florian Seibel, co-founder and co-CEO of European defense technology company Quantum Systems, also joined the round. The new funding brings the total seed investment to $18 million since the company was founded in 2024.
Ubitium builds custom silicon for autonomous machines, otherwise known as physical AI, that do physical work, such as drones, robots, industrial equipment and self-driving vehicles. The company is building a single universal processor to replace today’s more specialized chips.
Autonomous AI machines rely heavily on three different things: signal processing for sensing, artificial intelligence inference and orchestration. These three foundational principles are generally stitched together across circuitry or silicon with wiring, allowing a machine to perceive, think, and act in the real world.
Today’s developers divide that work across a signal processor, a neural processing unit (or a graphics processing unit) and a central processing unit for control. The interconnection generates additional latency, data transfer time, coordination and engineering complexity.
Ubitium built a single processor using RISC-V technology and separate specialized logic as one array of programmable elements for signal processing, AI and real-time control.
“Physical AI machines bring a whole new set of computing challenges, and the inference isn’t the hardest one,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Hyun Shin Cho. “Sensing the real world and controlling the machine in it are just as hard, and today those still run on separate chips. We built one physical AI processor that does all three, proved it in silicon in a year, and this funding turns it into a product.”
The company built on RISC-V because it is a free, open-source architecture based on the reduced instruction set principle. It is open and royalty-free, unlike proprietary frameworks such as those from Intel Corp. and Arm Ltd. or, more importantly, CUDA, the standard that underpins Nvidia Corp.’s chipset.
Nvidia currently dominates the physical AI market by a wide margin, acting as the gravitational center by providing the hardware and software stacks. Estimates for the global market itself vary in scale, but it is projected to surpass $430 billion by 2030 and approach $1.6 trillion by 2040, according to a ResearchAndMarkets.com research report.
Ubitium’s first chip, the UB108 with 256 processing elements, manufactured on Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd.’s eighth-nanometer process, proved that the three processes could work together on a single silicon die. The company plans to roll out its first commercial processor, the UB410 with 4,096 processing elements, and deliver units for evaluation in 2027.

articles.title: Octobre rouge pour Apple : la firme préparerait un 2e évènement consacré à de nouveaux Mac et un nouvel iPad
articles.text:
Gros, très gros, mois d’octobre pour Apple. En parallèle de l’évènement « Welcome Home » attendu ce soir, la firme organiserait un second rendez-vous à la fin du mois. Voué cette fois à la présentation de quatre nouveaux Mac et d’un nouvel iPad, cet événement parallèle adopterait lui aussi un nouveau format, articulé autour « d’expériences ».
Nous vous avons parlé de l’évènement « Welcome home » organisé par Apple, ce 13 octobre, pour la présentation de nouveautés liées à la maison connectée, mais un second événement du même type serait également prévu par la firme, cette fois sur les 27 et 28 octobre prochains.
De tout nouveaux Mac et un iPad mini repensé pour les 27-28 octobre ?
C’est ce qu’avance cette semaine l’indéboulonnable Mark Gurman. Le journaliste de Bloomberg explique que ces deux journées de présentation s’articuleraient autour « d’expériences » vouées aux créateurs de contenus et à la presse. Attendu à Los Angeles, cet événement miserait donc sur un nouveau format, plus ludique que la traditionnelle Keynote diffusée en ligne. Un format qu’Apple inaugurera tout à l’heure lors de son rendez-vous « Welcome Home ».
Quoi qu’il en soit, Apple aurait effectivement des choses à dire et des appareils à montrer à la fin du mois. L’entreprise profiterait de ce second événement des 27 et 28 octobre pour la présentation de trois nouveaux MacBook Pro, d’un nouvel iMac et d'un tout nouvel iPad mini.
Les produits attendus et leurs principales caractéristiques
Voici les principales caractéristiques des produits pressentis :
- De nouveaux MacBook Pro de 14 et 16 pouces équipés pour la toute première fois d’un écran OLED tactile surmonté d’une Dynamic Island. Ces MacBook Pro miseraient sur un nouveau châssis plus fin et léger, mais intégreraient finalement des puces M5 Pro et M5 Max. On y retrouverait enfin des puces modem C1X ou C2 leur permettant d’offrir nativement une connectivité 5G.
- Un nouvel iMac, inchangé sur le plan du design, mais équipé de la nouvelle puce Apple M6 inaugurée sur le Mac mini il y a quelques semaines. Ce modèle conserverait le châssis et le format 24 pouces de ses prédécesseurs, mais avec de nouveaux coloris.
- Un nouveau MacBook Pro de 14 pouces avec puce M6. Ce modèle conserverait, visiblement, le même châssis et les mêmes spécificités que le MacBook Pro M5 lancé l’année dernière… mais avec plus de puissance et une efficacité énergétique renforcée par le passage de la puce M6 au 2 nm de TSMC.
- Un tout nouvel iPad mini (8e génération) équipé lui aussi d'un écran OLED, mais également d'une puce A20 Pro, d'une nouvelle caméra frontale installée au format paysage et de nouveaux haut-parleurs. On y trouverait enfin un nouveau châssis résistant à l'eau.
Apple pourrait en outre profiter de l’évènement pour lancer la commercialisation de son Mac Studio M5 Ultra 512 Go. Un modèle ultra haut de gamme pensé pour l’IA. À l’heure actuelle le Mac Studio M5 Ultra peut toutefois déjà embarquer jusqu’à 256 Go de mémoire unifiée pour la gestion locale de grands modèles de langage. Ce modèle est actuellement en test chez Clubic.

Should I pre-order Metro 2039?
We can safely (probably) approach this question for Metro 2039 in terms of the editions that will be available.
In short, if you're interested in the Collector's Edition for Metro 2039 with that super cool wearable helmet, then my advice is to absolutely pre-order. We already know that there'll be a limited number of these, so waiting around until launch to hopefully snag one is a fool's game. If you're a big fan and willing and able to place a Collector's Edition pre-order, then my advice is to definitely do that.
If you're interested in the other editions only, then the pressure probably isn't so high. Certainly not with the standard edition in terms of stock anyway; you'll be able to find this at launch naturally, but the pre-order bonuses might make it tempting.
Now, if you're keen on the Deluxe Edition that sits 'in between' the standard one and the Collector's, then I'd lean more toward placing a pre-order over not if you're interested. We often see these middle editions being super popular due to the fact that the Collector's might be too pricey for most (or sell out), but fans want something a bit more special than the standard edition, especially if they are big followers of the series.
As a result, it's slightly nuanced but, in brief: the bigger the edition, the more need for a pre-order, I reckon.
Metro 2039 pre-orders — what's in each edition?
Thanks to Smyths Toys in the UK going earlier than I expected, we now know what's in each edition of Metro 2039. First, if you pre-order any copy of the game, you get:
- The Metro 2039 Specialist Pack that includes three blueprints - three unique, swappable backpack upgrades: an Equipment Specialist Pouch, Chemtech Specialist Pouch, and Munitions Specialist Pouch
If you want to go for the Collector's Edition, you'll get:
- A copy of the game
- A wearable replica Spartan helmet
- An exclusive steelbook
- A hardback art book
- Story expansion DLC
- A digital copy of the art book
- A digital copy of the soundtrack
But if you'd rather go for the Deluxe Edition, you'll bag the following:
- A copy of the game
- An exclusive steelbook
- A hardback art book
- Story expansion DLC
- A digital copy of the art book
- A digital copy of the soundtrack

articles.title: Mercado de criptomonedas: cuál es el valor de ethereum
articles.text:
Ether, comúnmente llamada como ethereum, es la moneda digital #2 en cuanto a términos de capitalización de mercado, por lo que se trata de una de las divisas digitales que más despierta el interés entre los mineros (creadores de las criptodivisas).
Ethereum es una plataforma de blockchain de código abierto que se ejecuta con el uso de su moneda nativa, llamada ether o ETH, por lo que a pesar de que la gente usa estos nombres como sinónimos son cosas distintas.
Ether es un token que se utiliza específicamente en la blockchain ethereum para pagar transacciones. Este token es responsable de impulsar casi todo lo que ocurre en la red, misma que puede ser usada por cualquier persona para crear y ejecutar contratos inteligentes, que son programas de software que se ejecutan de manera autónoma y sin la intervención del usuario.
De acuerdo con el portal de Binance, la moneda digital solana actualmente cuenta con 122.1M de unidades creadas.
La cotización de ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 2505.76 dólares, es decir, que la criptomoneda tuvo un cambio de -0.95 % en el último día.
Por otro lado, registró un cambio de 0.0 % con respecto a su valor hace una hora. En cuanto a su popularidad, se ubica en la posición #2.
Valor de la criptomoneda Ethereum
Ethereum 2.0: las claves
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: 4K 120 Hz et double iris, la nouvelle gamme Xgimi Horizon 30 veut corriger les plus gros défauts des vidéoprojecteurs
articles.text:
4K 120 Hz et double iris, la nouvelle gamme Xgimi Horizon 30 veut corriger les plus gros défauts des vidéoprojecteurs
Xgimi vient de présenter ses nouveaux vidéoprojecteurs Horizon 30 Pro, Max et Ultra Max. Au menu, une luminosité pouvant atteindre 6000 lumens, un contraste largement amélioré et la 4K à 120 Hz.
Après les excellents Horizon 20 et Horizon 20 Max que nous avions testés, Xgimi profite de cette fin d’année 2026 pour dévoiler une nouvelle génération de vidéoprojecteurs haut de gamme : les Horizon 30. Nous avions particulièrement apprécié les performances des précédents modèles, notamment leur forte luminosité et leur polyvalence, mais le contraste restait encore perfectible, comme souvent sur les vidéoprojecteurs DLP.
Avec les Horizon 30 Pro, Horizon 30 Max et Horizon 30 Ultra Max, Xgimi entend corriger ce point faible, tout en améliorant encore la luminosité et les fonctionnalités gaming. Présentés en avant-première à l'IFA 2026, ces modèles se dévoilent désormais plus en détail, notamment du côté de leurs tarifs.
Xgimi Horizon 30 : jusqu'à 6000 lumens et un double iris pour muscler le contraste
Les trois vidéoprojecteurs Horizon 30 reposent sur une source lumineuse triple laser RVB, à l'image de leurs prédécesseurs, mais Xgimi annonce cette fois des performances en nette hausse. L'Horizon 30 Pro affiche ainsi une luminosité de 4800 lumens ISO, contre 5300 lumens ISO pour l'Horizon 30 Max et pas moins de 6000 lumens ISO pour l'Horizon 30 Ultra Max.
XGIMI Horizon 30 Pro
Des valeurs particulièrement élevées pour des vidéoprojecteurs domestiques, qui devraient permettre de profiter d'une grande image même dans une pièce relativement lumineuse. Attention, comme toujours en vidéoprojection, il faudra privilégier une pièce sombre pour obtenir les meilleurs résultats, notamment en matière de contraste.
C’est justement sur ce dernier point que Xgimi promet les progrès les plus importants. Le fabricant annonce un contraste natif de 8000:1 pour le modèle Pro, 9000:1 pour le Max et jusqu'à 10000:1 pour l'Ultra Max. Selon la marque, le contraste serait ainsi multiplié par sept par rapport à la génération Horizon 20. Une progression impressionnante et difficile à vérifier sur le papier, mais que nous ne manquerons pas de mesurer précisément lors de nos tests en laboratoire.
Pour parvenir à ce résultat, Xgimi utilise notamment un système de double iris intelligent, capable de moduler la quantité de lumière en fonction des scènes affichées. Une technologie intéressante que l'on retrouve désormais sur certains vidéoprojecteurs haut de gamme, et qui devrait octroyer des noirs plus profonds sans trop sacrifier la luminosité.
Gaming et fluidité : de la 4K à 120 Hz pour la première fois chez Xgimi
Autre évolution importante, les Horizon 30 passent désormais à une fréquence de rafraîchissement de 120 Hz en 4K, contre 60 Hz sur la génération précédente. Une excellente nouvelle pour les joueurs qui souhaitent brancher une console récente ou un PC gaming sur leur vidéoprojecteur. Ces modèles seront parmi les premiers 4K 120 Hz du marché, en marge des Iris Ultra de JMGO et des modèles à ultra-courte focale annoncés à l’IFA, comme le Lux Vision d’Awol et le Xgimi Aura 3 Max.
Xgimi annonce également la prise en charge du VRR (Variable Refresh Rate), de l'ALLM (Auto Low Latency Mode) et d'AMD FreeSync.
Ergonomie et réglages : lens shift optique, zoom et Google TV intégrés
Xgimi conserve bien entendu ce qui faisait déjà l'intérêt des Horizon 20, à commencer par leur conception avec pied intégré inclinable et pivotant. On peut ainsi orienter facilement le vidéoprojecteur vers un mur ou une toile sans avoir à utiliser de support supplémentaire.
Les Horizon 30 disposent aussi d'un zoom optique et d'un système de déplacement mécanique de l'objectif, ou lens shift, qui permet d'ajuster la position de l'image sans recourir à une correction numérique du trapèze. Un vrai avantage pour conserver une qualité d'image optimale lorsque le vidéoprojecteur n'est pas parfaitement centré face à l'écran.
Les habituelles fonctions de correction automatique de l'image sont également de la partie, tandis que l'interface reste confiée à Google TV. On retrouvera donc toutes les apps de streaming comme Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+ ou YouTube, sans avoir à brancher d'appareil externe.
Enfin, Xgimi intègre deux haut-parleurs Harman Kardon de 12 W sur chacun des trois modèles, accompagnés de la technologie DTS Virtual. Un système audio qui devrait suffire pour un usage occasionnel, même si une barre de son ou un véritable système home-cinéma restera préférable pour accompagner une image de plusieurs mètres de diagonale.
Prix et date de sortie des Xgimi Horizon 30 Pro, Max et Ultra Max
Les nouveaux Horizon 30 seront disponibles en précommande du 12 au 31 octobre 2026, avant une commercialisation officielle le 1er novembre.
L'Horizon 30 Pro sera proposé à 2500 €, mais bénéficiera d'un tarif de lancement de 2000 €. L'Horizon 30 Max passera de 2800 € à 2500 € pendant les précommandes, tandis que l'Horizon 30 Ultra Max sera affiché à 3000 € au lieu de 3300 €.
La différence de prix entre les trois modèles se justifie principalement par leur luminosité et leur contraste, puisque les autres caractéristiques annoncées sont proches, si ce n'est identiques. L'Horizon 30 Pro pourrait donc s'avérer particulièrement intéressant avec ses 4800 lumens et son contraste annoncé à 8000:1, surtout à moins de 2000 €.
