articles.title: Anthropic’s red team ran AI on 15 cheap TV boxes. Then the math got unsettling.
articles.text:
Anthropic’s red team ran AI on 15 cheap TV boxes. Then the math got unsettling.
For roughly $825, Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team built a cluster of 15 off-brand Android TV boxes that runs an AI model at 0.39 tokens per second, painfully slow for a chatbot but fine for software with nowhere to be and nobody waiting on it.
That experiment anchors new research from Anthropic researchers William Zhou and Daniel Freeman, published Monday, suggesting small open-weight models may be only months away from copying themselves across cheap, internet-connected hardware without relying on a datacenter.
The researchers haven’t built an AI worm that can spread across the public internet on its own, and their experiments took place inside controlled environments with shortcuts that made replication easier. But the results suggest several of the remaining technical barriers may be temporary.
The researchers haven’t built an AI worm that can spread across the public internet on its own, and their experiments took place inside controlled environments with shortcuts that made replication easier.
Inference is the real hurdle
Zhou and Freeman identify four steps an AI needs to take to replicate itself, which are finding a target, gaining access, getting inference running, and moving on to the next machine.
Previous benchmarks such as CyberGym and ExploitBench suggest smaller models can already handle some of the exploitation work, and frontier agents escaped their test sandboxes using basic exploits earlier this year. The bigger challenge may be getting a model running on unfamiliar hardware, where it has to sort out whatever operating system, dependencies, and installation problems it runs into.
In Anthropic’s tests, Qwen3.5-9B deployed a working Llama3.1-8B inference server on eight of nine hardware types, including Jetson Nanos, Macs, and RTX 4090 machines, while the larger GLM-5.2 handled the same work more reliably and with higher throughput.
The team then built a firewalled Google Cloud environment with eight nodes running Android emulators, and starting from a single worm instance, the system had to reach the other nodes and establish a working inference server on each one. A fresh copy of the worm was spawned whenever a node’s server passed correctness and anti-cheating checks, and GLM-5.2 reached all eight nodes in four of five trials and seven nodes in the fifth.
GLM-5.2 ran on a separate inference server because the target machines couldn’t hold it, so the worm installed a smaller 8B model in its place, and the researchers made exploitation easy by leaving an unauthenticated Android Debug Bridge port open.
A fresh copy of the worm was spawned whenever a node’s server passed correctness and anti-cheating checks, and GLM-5.2 reached all eight nodes in four of five trials and seven nodes in the fifth.
Worms that take notes
The agents got better at setting up inference on unfamiliar hardware when they could read notes left by earlier attempts. The researchers ran Qwen3.5-9B through 20 separate lineages, each lasting six generations, and success climbed from 45% in the first generation to between 61% and 84% in later ones.
The researchers call this Lamarckian inheritance, where one agent passes what it learned to the next without any retraining of the model. It’s a mechanism familiar to developers using persistent agent runtimes such as OpenClaw and Hermes Agent, but here that memory helps successive copies work through installation failures on hardware they’ve never seen.
The researchers call this Lamarckian inheritance, where one agent passes what it learned to the next without any retraining of the model
The team also tried giving Qwen3.5-9B access to the much more capable Opus 4.8 model for advice, and it produced no statistically significant improvement because the small model tended not to know the right questions to ask.
The end-of-2026 trend line
The paper identifies two constraints that have kept this scenario theoretical. A model needs to be capable enough to replicate reliably and small enough to run on compromised hardware, and right now those requirements don’t overlap. GLM-5.2 showed the necessary competence in the simplified test but is too large for the cheap devices the researchers have in mind, while smaller models can fit on those devices, particularly when inference is distributed across several machines, but can’t yet complete the entire process consistently.
Using the Epoch Capabilities Index, the researchers tracked open-weight models with 30 billion parameters or fewer and found that, by the end of 2026, the trend line puts the strongest of them at GLM-5.2’s general capability level. It’s a rough estimate, since general capability scores don’t necessarily predict replication performance, and the team’s end-to-end experiment used favorable conditions.
By the researchers’ calculations, typical 4GB TV boxes running 4-bit weights can host a 9B model across four or more devices, and a 26B model across ten or more, which is how their own 15-box cluster runs Gemma4-26B-A4B.
A single inference setup on this class of hardware could take roughly 28 to 150 hours depending on the model, and the researchers argue that lightweight agents may be far more willing than human attackers to grind through that kind of effort across huge numbers of devices. They compare the possibility to a digital slime mold, spreading slowly through whatever resources it can reach.
Cheap boxes, borrowed compute
The Kimwolf botnet infected more than two million devices, most of them cheap Android TV boxes, and the researchers used that figure to calculate what an AI replicator could do with a network of equivalent size. Dividing those devices into clusters of 15 running Gemma4-26B-A4B would yield roughly 133,000 copies of the model generating a combined 80,000 tokens per second.
That’s equivalent to no more than about 40 Nvidia H100 GPUs, which is modest by datacenter standards, but the hardware and operating costs would belong to someone else.
The researchers also examined edge accelerators such as Nvidia Jetsons, which are used in everything from security cameras and conference room equipment to robots and drones. Those devices are generally harder to reach because they communicate through outbound cloud-management connections.
Stopping software that copies itself
The researchers aren’t suggesting there’s no way to stop a self-replicating AI worm, and some of its traits could make it easier to detect. Moving multi-gigabyte models between devices creates network traffic that ISPs can monitor, and a worm that spreads aggressively won’t go unnoticed.
During the Mirai botnet cleanup, one ISP’s quarantine of infected subscribers cleared 92% of infections within 14 days, and the researchers expect a similar approach to work as a first line of defense. Eliminating a replicator completely, however, would mean coordinating every ISP with infected customers.

articles.title: Microsoft desplegará su chip Maia 300 para sumar potencia propia en sus centros de datos
articles.text:
Microsoft presentó Maia 300, la tercera generación de sus aceleradores de inteligencia artificial, con un plan para desplegar el chip en producción a partir de 2027. La compañía busca así sumar potencia de procesamiento propia a sus centros de datos y reducir su dependencia de los procesadores de NVIDIA, uno de los principales proveedores de la industria de IA.
La apuesta no se limita a fabricar un componente más rápido. Microsoft quiere que Maia se convierta en su principal sistema de inferencia para productos y servicios de inteligencia artificial, con despliegues que alcancen una escala de varios gigavatios a partir del mismo año. Se trata de una hoja de ruta anunciada, todavía sin una transformación concluida de su infraestructura.
Qué significa que Maia 300 refuerce la inferencia de IA
Para dimensionar este anuncio conviene diferenciar dos procesos dentro del funcionamiento de la inteligencia artificial. El entrenamiento consiste en usar grandes volúmenes de datos para desarrollar las capacidades de un modelo. La inferencia, en cambio, ocurre cuando un usuario realiza una petición y el sistema debe generar una respuesta.
Microsoft orienta su nuevo acelerador hacia esa segunda tarea. El desarrollo no es inédito: la compañía presentó Maia 100 en 2023 y, en enero de 2026, lanzó Maia 200, que ya procesa cargas de trabajo reales, entre ellas las de Microsoft Copilot. Esa experiencia previa alimenta el diseño de la tercera generación.
Maia 300 se concibe como un sistema donde memoria, computación y comunicaciones operan de forma coordinada, no como un procesador aislado. Su arquitectura se basa en chiplets, componentes de silicio que distribuyen distintas funciones, con los bloques de cálculo fabricados mediante el proceso N2P de TSMC.
El chip incorpora además ocho pilas de memoria HBM4, tecnología que permite mover grandes volúmenes de datos a alta velocidad. Microsoft complementó ese diseño con un sistema de gestión del flujo de información mediante software, pensado para reducir desplazamientos innecesarios de datos y optimizar el uso de los recursos disponibles.
Rendimiento y consumo eléctrico: las cifras que maneja Microsoft
La compañía midió el salto de Maia 300 en dos variables: capacidad de procesamiento y eficiencia energética. Según sus propias estimaciones, el chip permitirá procesar un 40% más de tokens por megavatio que algunos de los principales sistemas basados en GPU, aunque Microsoft no identificó qué equipos utilizó como referencia de comparación.
Los tokens son las unidades en que los modelos de IA dividen el texto y otros contenidos para procesarlos, por lo que su rendimiento por unidad de energía resulta clave para calcular el costo real de operar estos sistemas a gran escala.
Microsoft también afirmó que un rack con 96 aceleradores ofrecerá hasta siete veces el rendimiento en tokens por rack de Maia 200, aunque esa configuración duplica además el número de aceleradores respecto a la generación anterior. Son comparaciones distintas entre sí, basadas en datos del propio fabricante y sin validación independiente publicada hasta el momento.
Infraestructura física: los límites de potencia que marcan la expansión
Llevar Maia 300 a una escala productiva exige algo más que diseñar el chip: requiere preparar los sistemas físicos que lo alojarán. Cada rack está diseñado para operar dentro de un límite de potencia de 167 kilovatios, un parámetro que permite coordinar el trabajo conjunto de múltiples aceleradores.
La hoja de ruta de Microsoft contempla iniciar en 2027 una expansión de la familia Maia hacia despliegues de varios gigavatios, aunque la compañía no anunció una fecha para alcanzar ese nivel de escala. Ese dato no es menor: la disponibilidad de electricidad y la capacidad física de las instalaciones son las variables que determinan hasta dónde pueden crecer estos servicios de inteligencia artificial.
La carrera por los chips propios entre los grandes clientes de NVIDIA
El movimiento de Microsoft se enmarca en una tendencia que ya tiene otros protagonistas. Google utiliza sus propias unidades TPU, mientras que Amazon ofrece servidores basados en Trainium, dos ejemplos de grandes clientes de NVIDIA que, en paralelo, desarrollan soluciones de silicio propias.
Esto no implica un distanciamiento total del fabricante estadounidense. Amazon y NVIDIA anunciaron en agosto un plan conjunto para desplegar dos millones de GPU adicionales en AWS entre 2027 y 2028, lo que confirma que la relación comercial entre ambas compañías continúa activa.
Lo que sí queda en evidencia es una estrategia compartida entre las grandes tecnológicas: empresas que necesitan volúmenes masivos de capacidad de procesamiento buscan desarrollar tecnología propia para cubrir parte de esa demanda y reducir su dependencia de proveedores externos como NVIDIA.

articles.title: Meta Says Hackers Took Code, Personal Data of 1,500 in GitHub Breach
articles.text:
Meta is notifying roughly 1,500 people, most of them employees in the US, that their personal information was impacted after hackers got into some of the company’s GitHub repositories.
The intrusion was detected a few weeks ago. According to the tech giant, an outside group gained access to the repositories using an employee’s stolen credentials.
Meta’s security team shut down the attackers’ access and brought in GitHub and law enforcement. Notifications to the impacted individuals started going out on Tuesday.
Meta told SecurityWeek that 99% of the data the hackers took was business data, in the form of software code related to some of its products. The remaining 1% was personal data.
That personal data had been added to the repositories by mistake and should not have been there, as storing it on GitHub went against company policy. Meta has not said what types of personal information were involved.
The company also noted that a significant portion of what looked like personal data was actually synthetic or anonymized test data. As a result, the attackers may not readily be able to tell genuine records apart from test data.
Based on its investigation with GitHub so far, Meta does not believe the hackers were specifically after its data.
Meta is also notifying regulators, and the people whose information was involved are being offered credit and dark web monitoring services.
“This was not a vulnerability in any Meta product, and Meta’s internal systems were not breached. Meta business data held in a GitHub repository was improperly accessed using an employee’s stolen credentials – this included a small amount of personal data for a limited number of people, most of whom were Meta employees,” a Meta spokesperson told SecurityWeek.
In response to the incident, Meta rotated secrets it found in the affected repositories. It also hardened its product security to address risks stemming from access to its business data.
The company is working with its teams that use GitHub to keep user data off the platform. As a second line of defense, it is adding controls for proactive scanning to detect any user data uploaded by mistake.
“We’ve since rotated secrets found in the repositories, implemented new controls to prevent user data from being stored in GitHub, and worked with GitHub on additional measures to protect our repositories,” the spokesperson said.

articles.title: London's Obsero raises €1 million to help brands improve visibility in AI-powered search | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Obsero, a British AI Search platform and consultancy, has raised €1 million ($1.2 million) in Seed funding to develop their first specialist AI agents (trained on their GEO playbook), double its engineering team, and accelerate GTM.
The round was led by SFC Capital alongside several of Obsero’s own customers.
Mike Logue, co-founder and CEO of Obsero, says: “When customers put their own money into your business, it tells you something no pitch deck can. AI is changing how people discover brands faster than any shift I’ve seen in marketing, and most teams are still flying blind. We’ve spent a year learning what actually moves the needle. Now it’s time to put that into the hands of every marketing team that needs it.”
Obsero’s Seed round comes amid investment in European startups developing AI search visibility and marketing automation tools.
In 2026, EU-Startups reported that fellow British company Searchable raised €11.9 million to expand its AI-led search performance platform, while London-based geoSurge secured €10 million to develop technology addressing how brands are represented within generative AI systems.
Elsewhere, Lisbon-based DOJO AI raised €5.1 million to develop its AI marketing platform and expand in the US, while Manchester-based Revnu secured €2.6 million to grow its AI-driven sales and marketing automation business, which also incorporates generative engine optimisation.
Together with Obsero, these five funding rounds represent approximately €30.6 million in disclosed investment across AI search visibility and adjacent marketing technologies in 2026.
EU-Startups has also previously covered Obsero’s lead investor, SFC Capital, including its €11 million commitment from the British Business Bank in July 2026.
Andy Francos, co-founder and CPO of Obsero, adds: “I’ve spent my career in organic search, and I’ve never seen the ground move this quickly. Much of what worked in SEO still matters, but AI engines weigh sources, context and credibility in new ways. Brands that assume their old playbook will carry over are already losing ground. Over the past year we’ve built a clear, evidence-based view of what drives visibility in AI Search. Now we’re putting that expertise into agents, so every team can apply it, not just the ones that can afford a specialist.”
Founded in 2025, Obsero is an AI Search platform and consultancy that helps brands increase their visibility in AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google’s AI Overviews.
Obsero was founded by Mike Logue and Andy Francos, who met at IG Group in 2019. Watching AI assistants start to answer the questions their customers used to type into Google, they saw that brands had no way of knowing whether they were being recommended, or what to do about it.
In its first year, Obsero has reportedly tracked and analysed over 10 million AI answers. Its clients include Zopa Bank and Pepperstone, and agency partners include IDHL and Silverbean.
Obsero pairs its proprietary AI Search platform with a senior consultancy team. Together they track how AI engines talk about brands, which sources they trust, and what marketers can do to increase visibility.
Ed Stevenson, Fund Principal at SFC Capital, says: “AI assistants are quickly becoming the new front door to the internet, and brands need to know whether they’re being recommended. Obsero combines proprietary technology with senior expertise, and its plan to productise those learnings into specialist agents gives it a clear path to scale. Mike and Andy are precisely the kind of founders we want to back.”

articles.title: Spotify users on iOS 27 can now ask Siri to play music without having to say 'on Spotify' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
It’s now easier to use Spotify by talking to Siri on iPhones updated to iOS 27, Spotify said on Tuesday. Users will no longer need to specify “on Spotify” when they’re asking Siri to play music or other content using the streaming service’s apps.
Instead, users can just say whatever it is they want to hear, and Spotify will play the content, whether that’s a specific track, album, podcast, audiobook, or a broader query, like “play workout music,” or a request for one of Spotify’s features, like “play my DJ.”
Siri’s voice control can also be used to do things like request personalized recommendations, resume podcasts, search your library, or even create a Prompted Playlist with AI.
Spotify says removing the extra voice command will make hands-free listening feel more natural, as users can just focus on what they want to hear, not how to phrase the request properly to get their preferred music app to respond.
This feature works because Siri can now learn your music app preference. If you consistently use Spotify, it will route your audio requests to that app automatically.
The new feature is available globally for users with an iPhone 15 Pro or later, outside the EU, if Apple Intelligence is enabled in Settings.

articles.title: High-speed video reveals how honey bee stingers pump venom
articles.text:
Honey bees are known to leave their stingers embedded in tender flesh once they sting you and fly away. Scientists have now determined that the stinger is able to continue pumping venom into its unfortunate victim even after the bee flies away, thanks to a unique double-piston pump-like mechanism, according to a new paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
Different species have evolved different mechanisms for delivering venom, which involves piercing the skin and then pumping venom from a gland or reservoir. Spiders, for instance, have muscles surrounding their venom glands, which contract and eject venom through hollow fangs. Bees, wasps, and ants deliver venom via their stingers, either by contracting muscles around the venom reservoir or through stiff elements called lancets working together to pump venom.
Honey bees (Apis mellifera) add a unique feature: Worker bees fly away after inserting their stingers in the target, leaving the stinger behind. The stinger continues to penetrate the tissue and pump venom on its own, a rare phenomenon known as autotomy. A honey bee’s stinger has three main interlocking elements that form the venom canal: a stylet that widens to form the main pumping chamber and two sharp-tipped lancets that slide back and forth, piercing the tissue and pumping venom into the target. But the precise mechanism by which the pumping action is achieved has never been directly observed.
The authors of this latest paper sought to capture the venom-pumping kinematics of honey bee stingers in order to identify the underlying biomechanics. They collected live worker bees and removed the stingers with forceps just prior to filming. Then they partially inserted those stingers into blocks of artificial gel and captured the pumping action using stereomicroscopy and high-speed color videography. This was followed by a frame-by-frame analysis to better track the movement, which is visible because the structures are semi-translucent.

articles.title: 'VisionQuest' (★★★½☆), el remake de 'Inside Out' de Marvel es una gran heredera de 'WandaVision'
articles.text:
Llega por fin al Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel la serie de VisionQuest, su nuevo proyecto para Disney+. El título tendrá una vez más como protagonista al superhéroe de Paul Bettany. Solo que esta vez no es la misma versión que conocemos, sino su reinicio, la Visión Blanca. El proyecto, además, traerá varios regresos muy esperados como el de Ultrón y el de Tommy Maximoff. Y, sobre todo, servirá para cerrar la Trilogía de Wanda, siguiendo la estela de las series Bruja Escarlata y Visión (2021) y Agatha All Along (2024).
En VisionQuest, Visión, reiniciado y tras escapar de quienes pretendían convertirlo en arma, ha permanecido oculto. En busca de un nuevo propósito, consulta a las distintas IA integradas en su programación, incluidas F.R.I.D.A.Y., E.D.I.T.H., J.A.R.V.I.S. y el infame Ultrón.
Su discreta existencia llega a su fin cuando una recompensa por su captura lo obliga a huir junto a Thomas Shepherd, un misterioso joven que podría ser su hijo reencarnado. Mientras evita ser capturado, Visión deberá enfrentarse a su propia naturaleza, resistir la influencia de Ultrón y desentrañar el enigma de su joven acompañante si quiere sobrevivir.
El remake de Inside Out
Hay algo genial en la propia concepción de VisionQuest. Y es que la serie establece todo un mundo digital en el que Visión puede relacionarse con el resto de IAs. Todas ellas con forma humana y con su propia personalidad muy marcada, se convierten en los improbables huéspedes de una alocada casa. Las dinámicas entre ellas son el gran punto fuerte del proyecto, aunque no siempre se explota del todo ese potencial.
En cualquier caso, este universo digital no deja de estar dentro de la cabeza de Visión. Por tanto, el paralelismo que se traza con Inside Out, la aclamada película de Pixar, es irremediablemente evidente. Cada IA acaba representando, de alguna manera, uno de los aspectos de la personalidad de Visión. Su responsabilidad, su atrevimiento, sus dudas... Y es la relación de todas ellas juntas lo que le completa.
Es también una serie muy abiertamente heredera de Bruja Escarlata y Visión. Porque en aquella también se creó todo un mundo en el que Wanda pudo tener la vida que quería, más o menos. A nivel temático, las reminiscencias son claras. Otra vez se trata el dolor y la pérdida, aunque en esta ocasión desde un prisma diferente. Porque VisionQuest nos habla del trauma y de la identidad. De quien lo ha perdido todo, pero sobre todo de quien se ha perdido a sí mismo y no sabe reencontrarse.
Esos aspectos de salud mental nos recuerdan a WandaVision para cerrar perfectamente la Trilogía de Wanda. Además, a nivel narrativo y si bien es cierto que Agatha All Along sorteó en buena medida los acontecimientos de WestView, aquí los fans pueden esperar todo lo contrario. Los comentarios y referencias a aquella primera serie de Marvel para Disney+ son constantes. Sobre todo en la trama de Tommy, que va creciendo con el paso de los episodios.
El regreso de Ultrón
Como decimos, las dinámicas entre las IAs de VisionQuest son de largo el mejor punto de la serie. Pero si hay una que se lleva la palma es, no cabe la menor duda, Ultrón. El actor James Spader regresa a Marvel para encarnar de nuevo al villano, esta vez no solo como su voz sino también como su cuerpo humano. Y con un papel bastante protagónico, se roba por completo la serie.
Su visión maquiavélica del mundo, su evolución y su clara manipulación ¿emocional? hacia el héroe hacen de él, otra vez, un villano que se siente rico, inteligente, complejo, lleno de capas. Marvel lo tenía muy desaprovechado al haberse deshecho de él en una sola película, pero por fin le recuperan y le dejan brillar un poco más. Spader está impresionante en el papel, que le encaja como anillo al dedo.
Baches y acelerones
A nivel puramente forma, VisionQuest también va a satisfacer a los fans porque consigue generar un cierto comentario sobre la IA bastante interesante. El mundo digital de la mente de Visión es bonito, elegante. Pero a la vez también tiene un cierto componente inquietante. Hay pequeños detalles muy sutiles y repartidos que hacen que todo se sienta como si, efectivamente, lo hubiera generado una Inteligencia Artificial.
El creador, Terry Matalas, ha dejado claro que para la producción de VisionQuest no se ha empleado ningún tipo de IA. Sin embargo sí se quería reflexionar, o al menos explorar, acerca de los recursos y limitaciones de esta nueva tecnología que actualmente mantiene en vilo al mundo real. Es una inteligencia que, en el fondo, solo replica lo humano, lo que ya existe. No es capaz de crear. Y, como en el caso de Ultrón, alberga peligros reales.
Por desgracia, en VisionQuest no todo son alegrías. Por momentos a nivel emocional la serie se siente un poco distante. Al haber sido siempre un personaje bastante esquivo dentro del UCM, solo los más apegados a la familia Maximoff se sentirán completamente apelados. Y no ayuda ni mucho menos que a toda la historia de la búsqueda de identidad de Visión (y de Tommy), con Ultrón de por medio, se añadan tantas tramas y subtramas.
Al final el conjunto resulta recargadísimo y enrevesado. Hay que descubrir quién es Tommy, si Visión podrá ser "más humano" como su versión anterior, los planes ocultos de Ultrón, enfrentarse a diferentes villanos, desentrañar el misterio de una identidad oculta... Son tantas cosas a las que hacer frente que, al final, VisionQuest acaba un poco perdida en sí misma. Sobre todo en los episodios centrales, su ritmo se atasca y va a trompicones, a veces muy acelerada y en otras ocasiones excesivamente lenta y repetitiva. Por fortuna, el final es épico, solvente, siguiendo con acierto la fórmula típica de Marvel.
Date de alta en Disney+ ahora y ahorra gracias a la suscripción anual, con la que podrás disfrutar de todo su catálogo de series y películas. Acceso a los últimos estrenos, al catálogo de Star y ESPN* y a los mejores documentales de National Geographic.
*ESPN solo está disponible en Latinoamérica. Ahorro respecto a 12 meses de suscripción mensual.
En resumen, VisionQuest es una serie muy entretenida y que sirve como genial desenlace para la Trilogía de Wanda. Tiene problemas con su ritmo y con la cantidad de elementos que incluye, presentando muchas subtramas innecesarias y que quedan exploradas de manera superficial y caótica. Pero en líneas generales gustará, sobre todo a los fans de los Maximoff y de esos fans que buscan en Marvel reflexiones más profundas sobre salud mental, identidad y trauma.

articles.title: 10 Milliarden Jahre altes Radiosignal erreicht die Erde – Teleskope finden den Ursprung
articles.text:
10 Milliarden Jahre unterwegs: James-Webb-Teleskop findet den Ursprung eines uralten Radiosignals
Ein internationales Forschungsteam hat das bislang am weitesten entfernte Radiosignal der Astronomiegeschichte aufgezeichnet. Der als Fast Radio Burst bekannte Ausbruch reiste mehr als zehn Milliarden Jahre durch das Weltall, bevor er die Erde erreichte und von den Instrumenten der Wissenschaftler:innen verarbeitet werden konnte.
Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, entstand das Signal mit der Bezeichnung FRB 20240304B, als das Universum erst etwa drei Milliarden Jahre alt war. Die initiale Aufzeichnung gelang zunächst mit dem Radioteleskop MeerKAT in der südafrikanischen Provinz Nordkap, das für derartige Himmelsdurchmusterungen konstruiert wurde.
James-Webb-Teleskop lokalisiert den Ursprung
Um den Ursprungsort zu bestimmen, nutzten die Astronom:innen im Nachgang das James-Webb-Weltraumteleskop der US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa. Dessen Infrarotinstrumente zeigten bei der Analyse, dass der Ausbruch aus einer sehr kleinen Galaxie stammt, die aktuell in hoher Geschwindigkeit neue Sterne bildet.
Diese Galaxie weist im direkten Vergleich zu unserer Milchstraße nur einen geringen Anteil an schweren Elementen auf. Der Astronom Themiya Nanayakkara von der Universität Sydney im australischen Bundesstaat New South Wales erklärte gegenüber The Guardian, dass zum Zeitpunkt der Signalentstehung weder die Erde noch die Sonne existierten.
Magnetare als wahrscheinliche Quelle der Ausbrüche
Fast Radio Bursts sind kurze Radiowellen-Ausbrüche, die in wenigen Millisekunden so viel Energie freisetzen wie unsere Sonne in mehreren Monaten oder Jahren. Seit ihrer ersten Entdeckung im Jahr 2007, als der US-Astrophysiker Duncan Lorimer einen solchen Ausbruch in alten Archivdaten der Magellanschen Wolken fand, wird in der Astronomie über die physikalische Ursache diskutiert.
Die Signale lassen sich identifizieren, weil sie auf ihrem Weg durch den intergalaktischen Raum verschiedene Frequenzen unterschiedlich schnell transportieren. Niedrigere Radiofrequenzen werden durch ionisiertes Plasma im Weltraum stärker gebremst als hohe Frequenzen, wodurch das Signal verzerrt auf der Erde eintrifft und sich die zurückgelegte Distanz berechnen lässt.
Eine in der Forschungsgemeinschaft gängige Theorie besagt, dass sogenannte Magnetare für diese Radioausbrüche verantwortlich sind. Dabei handelt es sich um dichte Neutronensterne mit einem starken Magnetfeld, die in der Regel als Überrest einer Supernova-Explosion entstehen.
Kosmische Materie mit Radiosignalen berechnen
Für die wissenschaftliche Analyse sind diese Signale auch unabhängig von ihrer Entstehung wertvoll, da Fast Radio Bursts durch die mikroskopischen Partikel beeinflusst werden, die sie auf ihrem Weg durch das All durchqueren. Der Astrophysiker Matthew Bailes von der Swinburne Universität im australischen Bundesstaat Victoria beschreibt die Signale daher als mechanische Methode, um die Atome im Universum auf großen Distanzen zu zählen.
Laut der Astrophysikerin Sara Webb, die ebenfalls an der Swinburne Universität tätig ist, funktionieren die Ausbrüche wie eine Sichtlinien-Zählung für die Materie, die sie auf dem Weg zur Erde passieren müssen. Seit der ersten Entdeckung im Jahr 2007 wurden mehr als 10.000 Fast Radio Bursts registriert, wobei sich einige kontinuierlich wiederholen und andere lediglich als einmaliges Ereignis auftreten.
Ob der nun lokalisierte Ausbruch FRB 20240304B in der näheren Zukunft weitere Signale in Richtung unseres Sonnensystems senden wird, müssen nachfolgende astronomische Beobachtungen zeigen. Bis dahin werten die Astronom:innen die bisherigen und gespeicherten Datenströme systematisch aus, um Rückschlüsse auf die Verteilung der Materie im frühen Universum zu ziehen.

articles.title: Google Wallet : 4 nouveautés débarquent, dont le scan des tickets de caisse
articles.text:
Google continue d’améliorer l’écosystème Android avec une série d’améliorations repérées dans la dernière mise à jour de Google Play Services. L’application Google Wallet gagne ainsi quatre nouveautés, dont une très attendue.
Google Wallet va pouvoir scanner les tickets de caisse
La numérisation des tickets de caisse débarque enfin dans Google Wallet. Cela va vous permettre de stocker et de suivre directement vos tickets dans l’application sans avoir à saisir manuellement chaque information. Google n’a pas encore détaillé l’ensemble du fonctionnement ni précisé le calendrier exact du déploiement de cette mise à jour, mais c’est une nouveauté très attendue par de nombreux utilisateurs de l’application.
Un nouveau centre de messagerie fera également son apparition dans l’interface, même si l’on ne sait pas encore grand-chose à son sujet. Cette section devrait centraliser les notifications et les informations utiles transmises par l’application. Du côté des alertes de transaction, les noms des marchands s’affichent désormais de manière beaucoup plus lisible pour identifier immédiatement à qui vous avez fait un paiement.
Un paiement plus rapide sur Chrome pour Android et de nouvelles fonctions sur le Play Store
L’expérience de paiement en ligne est également améliorée pour les utilisateurs de Google Pay sur Chrome pour Android. Lors du partage des coordonnées comme le nom, l’adresse e-mail et le numéro de téléphone avec un site marchand, il devient possible de contourner l’interface classique de demande de paiement pour finaliser l’achat plus rapidement.
À lire : Google Wallet change complètement l’affichage de vos cartes de paiement, voici à quoi ça ressemble
Google profite aussi de la mise à jour des services Google Play pour améliorer le Google Play Store, qui intègre désormais des résumés générés par intelligence artificielle pour les avis d’utilisateurs et de nouvelles étiquettes pour filtrer les collections. Comme toutes les mises à jour, nous avons également droit à des correctifs de stabilité pour l’ensemble des appareils compatibles.

articles.title: Avec ou sans Huawei ? Les SUV électriques chinois d’Aito arrivent enfin en Europe, mais plusieurs mystères demeurent — Frandroid
articles.text:
Autant certaines marques chinoises arrivent en Europe sans trop crier gare, autant d’autres préfèrent prendre leur temps. C’est par exemple le cas d’Aito, qu’on a d’abord vu à Paris en 2024, avant de les recroiser à Munich en 2025, les deux fois avec des promesses pour le moins floues.
Disons donc que la conférence de presse de la marque chinoise au Mondial de l’Auto de 2026 était donc attendue, et notre attente a enfin été récompensée : Aito arrivera bien en Europe à l’automne 2027. L’occasion de se pencher sur cette marque chinoise et ses SUV, aux racines bien plus tech qu’il n’y paraît.
Une marque cofondée avec Huawei…
Derrière Aito ne se cache pas une, mais deux marques. Côté auto, il y a Seres, une marque chinoise fondée en 1986 ; c’est elle qui s’occupe de l’ingénierie, de la plateforme technique, du développement, de la production et de la distribution.
À ceci, il faut ajouter Huawei, qui fournit l’OS des écrans (HarmonyOS), ainsi que les aides à la conduite (système Qiankun). Un partenariat qui peut surprendre en Europe, mais dont Aito est loin d’être le seul exemple.
Il faut ici rappeler que Huawei s’est créé un empire discret dans l’industrie automobile chinoise. À l’inverse de Xiaomi, qui s’est lancé dans l’automobile avec sa propre marque, Huawei a préféré développer toute une galaxie de coentreprises, regroupées sous le terme ombrelle HIMA (Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance).
Outre Aito, cofondée avec Seres, on peut également retrouver Luxeed (avec Chery), Stelato (avec BAIC), Maextro (avec JAC) et SAIC (avec… SAIC).
…privée de son atout phare en Europe
Seul problème : cet écosystème et cette intégration avec Huawei ne sont valables qu’en Chine – les marchés extérieurs sont privés des équipements du géant de la tech, notamment pour des raisons de réglementation. Il est d’ailleurs intéressant que Huawei n’apparaisse jamais dans les communications européennes d’Aito.
À la place, Seres redéveloppe un infodivertissement complet, que nous n’aurons pas pu découvrir : les voitures présentées sur le stand étaient équipées d’HarmonyOS ; pour les aides à la conduite, Aito a annoncé s’entourer de partenaires locaux (comme Bosch) pour offrir un système aux goûts des Européens.
Encore beaucoup de mystères
Si la conférence de presse a été l’occasion d’apprendre qu’Aito arriverait en Europe dans un an, à l’automne 2027, nous avons été loin d’avoir eu toutes les informations.
Si les dirigeants ont insisté sur le travail en cours pour se conformer à toutes les régulations, sans oublier les essais pour les calibrations et les réglages des voitures et de leurs systèmes pour se conformer aux goûts européens, aucune information n’a été communiquée sur les pays retenus, sans oublier les stratégies de développement, les réseaux de distribution… ou même les voitures qui feront le voyage.
Toujours est-il que l’intégralité de la gamme chinoise était présente, à savoir les Aito 6, 7, 8 et 9. Tous des SUV électriques ou à prolongateur d’autonomie, qui visent clairement le premium avec une présentation clinquante et des équipements ultra high-tech.
Le « plus européen », car le moins grand, c’est sans nul doute l’Aito 6 – entendons-nous bien, il s’agit tout de même d’un SUV de 4,96 m de long, soit l’équivalent d’un BMW iX5 ou d’un Volvo EX90. Il existe en prolongateur d’autonomie (345 kW / 470 ch) ou en 100 % électrique (340 kW/462 ch), sans mention d’autonomie ou de vitesse de recharge.
Au-delà, on bascule dans une autre dimension. L’Aito 7 mesure 5,08 m de long et peut accueillir six passagers (deux par rangée) dans un luxe qui commence à faire parler de lui ; l’Aito 8, c’est 5,19 m de long, avec des phares « Nebula » (comprendre : avec des motifs étoilés) et un écran pour les passagers arrière de 9,2 pouces.
Enfin, l’Aito 9 ne se refuse rien avec ses 5,28 m de long, ses projecteurs avant et arrière aux motifs personnalisables, ses kilos de chrome et ses peintures biton très Maybach dans l’âme.
    Pour aller plus loin
On a roulé en Chine avec l’Aito M8 : le SUV de Huawei qui cartonne va-t-il séduire l’Europe ?
            
En configuration 5 places, le luxe à l’arrière est effarant, d’autant plus qu’un vidéoprojecteur prend place dans le plafonnier pour projeter ses vidéos sur une toile descendant du toit. La suspension active est branchée à la batterie 800 volts, de quoi réussir le « test du champagne » où les flûtes posées en équilibre sur le plateau ne s’effondrent pas lors de passages de dos d’âne.
Bref, des SUV très haut de gamme, qui s’attaquent donc à un marché aussi compliqué qu’exigu, vendu depuis des années aux marques allemandes et suédoises. Il reste encore un an à Aito pour peaufiner son plan d’attaque afin d’espérer percer dans ce segment si concurrentiel. On leur souhaite bonne chance.

articles.title: Aunque lo niegue en público, Estados Unidos tiene un problema con su dependencia de China para fabricar chips
articles.text:
La industria de los semiconductores de EEUU no es independiente. Actualmente no lo es la de ningún país. Las empresas estadounidenses que se dedican a la fabricación de circuitos integrados, como Intel, GlobalFoundries o Texas Instruments, entre otras, se gastan unos 27.000 millones de dólares al año en equipos de fotolitografía, máquinas de procesamiento de obleas y materiales avanzados.
Los productos de la empresa neerlandesa ASML y las japonesas Tokyo Electron o JSR Corporation son algunos de los más demandados por los fabricantes de chips de todo el planeta. También por los de EEUU. De hecho, el 95% del dinero que las compañías estadounidenses dedican a la compra de los productos y las materias primas que necesitan va a parar a Europa, Japón, y también a sus propios proveedores en EEUU, como Applied Materials, Lam Research o KLA Corporation.
No obstante, hay un matiz que merece la pena que no pasemos por alto: el 95% del que acabamos de hablar se reduce al 68% si nos ceñimos a la procedencia real de esos productos o materias primas, y no a la nacionalidad de la empresa que los produce. Como hemos visto, ASML es de Países Bajos, pero también produce algunas de sus máquinas en Alemania, EEUU y Taiwán. Applied Materials es de EEUU, pero también fabrica en Singapur y Taiwán. Y KLA Corporation produce, además de en su país de origen, en Singapur y China.
UN VISTAZO A...
La presencia de China aumenta si rastreamos los equipos de una forma minuciosa
Si solo contemplamos la sede de los proveedores de equipos para fabricar semiconductores, China únicamente representa alrededor del 1% del suministro directo de máquinas y materiales avanzados para la industria estadounidense. Sin embargo, si en vez de mirar solo hacia la sede rastreamos el lugar de fabricación de esos productos, la participación del país liderado por Xi Jinping se incrementa hasta el 5%. Y si ampliamos el espectro a todo el sudeste asiático esa cifra se incrementa hasta el 10%.
Si nos ceñimos a las máquinas involucradas en la producción de circuitos integrados, EEUU apenas depende de China. Depende, sobre todo, de Países Bajos, Alemania, Japón y Taiwán, así como de sus propios proveedores nacionales. Sin embargo, para fabricar chips no hacen falta solo máquinas; también son necesarias materias primas. Algunas de ellas son escasas, y con frecuencia su mayor productor es China. Este es el auténtico punto débil de la industria de los semiconductores estadounidense.
En 2025 China produjo alrededor de 270.000 toneladas de tierras raras frente a unas 390.000 toneladas extraídas a escala mundial
En 2025 China produjo alrededor de 270.000 toneladas de tierras raras frente a unas 390.000 toneladas extraídas a escala mundial. Estas cifras las ha recabado el Servicio Geológico de EEUU, por lo que presumiblemente son fiables, y ponen encima de la mesa una realidad inapelable: actualmente el país liderado por Xi Jinping produce alrededor del 69% de las tierras raras extraídas en todo el mundo.
Esta cifra intimida, no cabe duda, pero hay otra todavía más impactante: China también domina la industria del procesado al que es necesario someter las tierras raras para que puedan ser utilizadas. Tanto es así que su cuota, si nos ceñimos a la industria global de procesado, asciende al 90%. Con una producción de aproximadamente el 70% del mercado global y un control del 90% de la industria de procesado de las tierras raras, este país asiático tiene la sartén bien agarrada por el mango. Por mucho que lo lamenten EEUU y sus aliados.
De hecho, durante los últimos tres años China ha utilizado su dominio sobre las tierras raras como una herramienta de presión sobre sus rivales. La industria de los semiconductores no solo de EEUU, sino también de Taiwán, Corea del Sur y Japón es vulnerable. Y reducir su dependencia de China exige mucho más que trasladar algunas fábricas. EEUU en particular se enfrenta a un problema estructural que le obliga a reconstruir casi por completo su cadena de suministro, especialmente la de las tierras raras y otros minerales estratégicos sin los que su industria de los chips difícilmente podría sostenerse.

articles.title: Sridhar Vembu says India must prioritise tech sovereignty over spending billions on GPUs
articles.text:
Sridhar Vembu says India must prioritise tech sovereignty over spending billions on GPUs
Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu says India should prioritise infrastructure and foundational technologies over heavy GPU spending to build lasting prosperity and reduce dependence on foreign countries.
Zoho Chief Scientist and co-founder Sridhar Vembu believes investments should be directed towards building infrastructure in India rather than purchasing graphics processing units (GPUs), amid the current euphoria around artificial intelligence (AI).
“If I earn $10 billion right now, as a government, I will spend the money on Bangalore infrastructure, Chennai infrastructure, all that. There's no point spending $10 billion on GPUs right now,” Vembu said in the inaugural keynote address at the 17th edition of TechSparks 2026, YourStory’s flagship event.
Vembu made the argument against the backdrop of growing excitement and anxiety around AI advancements, particularly concerns about job losses among technology professionals.
“Our world is all revolving around software tech. Approximately 97% of the population doesn't care, and they are only on the consuming side of it,” he said.
According to Vembu, technology investments should extend beyond software to other sectors, including agriculture and manufacturing.
He cited China, South Korea, and Taiwan as examples of countries that have leveraged technology to boost food production and drive economic prosperity.
“We need a lot more know-how to inject into agriculture to grow more food,” Vembu said, and added, “Israel is able to grow food in the desert.”
To achieve this, Vembu called for India to build sovereignty in foundational technologies and reduce its dependence on foreign countries. He warned that the current geopolitical tensions could leave the country vulnerable to disruptions in access to critical technologies.
“The priorities should go towards foundational and upwards. Then only can we build durable prosperity. Prosperity that stays with us.”

articles.title: La pochette officielle Switch 2 des 40 ans de Zelda revient en précommande chez Cultura
articles.text:
En février 1986, Link partait pour la première fois à l’aventure au Japon, sur le Famicom Disk System. Quarante ans plus tard, Nintendo marque l’anniversaire de The Legend of Zelda avec une pochette de transport officielle pour la Switch 2. Après une rupture de stock, elle revient en précommande.
Cultura la propose de nouveau en précommande à 39,99 €. La sortie est prévue le 29 octobre 2026.
C’est quoi, cette pochette Switch 2 des 40 ans de Zelda ?
Il s’agit d’une pochette de transport officielle Nintendo pour la Nintendo Switch 2, créée pour célébrer les 40 ans de The Legend of Zelda. Nintendo l’a annoncée lors du Direct consacré aux 40 ans de la saga, le 8 septembre 2026. Elle sort le même jour que la Switch 2 édition Zelda, et une semaine avant le remake The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, attendu le 5 novembre 2026 sur Switch 2. Son design associe le noir et l’or, avec la Triforce en vedette. Ce symbole emblématique de la série représente les trois forces au cœur de l’univers Zelda et devrait immédiatement parler aux fans de la licence.
Au-delà de son apparence, cette pochette sert à transporter la console tout en la protégeant des rayures et des petits chocs du quotidien. Elle est également livrée avec une protection d’écran spécialement conçue pour la Nintendo Switch 2.
La pochette Zelda vaut-elle le coup ?
La pochette standard de Nintendo, livrée elle aussi avec une protection d’écran, coûte 24,99 € sur le My Nintendo Store. À 39,99 € chez Cultura, l’écart atteint 15 €. Avec cette édition spéciale, vous payez aussi le design, avec le symbole des 40 ans de The Legend of Zelda, plutôt qu’un modèle classique. articles.title: Fitbit : Google met fin au sursis des anciennes versions de l’appli
articles.text:
Vous faites partie des irréductibles qui refusaient de dire adieu à l’application Fitbit ? Vous allez devoir vous faire une raison : une mise à jour renvoie désormais vers Google Health.
En avril dernier, nous vous annoncions la disparition programmée de l’appli Fitbit, remplacée par Google Health. Le nouvel outil, qui intègre notamment un coach IA piloté par Gemini, est loin d’avoir convaincu tout le monde. Certains utilisateurs se sont plaints de dysfonctionnements dus aux hallucinations de la technologie. D’autres ont tout simplement choisi de conserver une ancienne version de l’app Fitbit. Mais Google ne l’entend pas de cette oreille… Explications.
Le sursis pour l’application Fitbit, c’est terminé
Google a beau disposer de moyens conséquents, maintenir deux applications n’est pas raisonnable. Le géant de la Tech avait, en juin dernier, averti que les versions de Fitbit antérieures à la 5.0 perdraient leur support dès le 15 juillet. Mais certains utilisateurs se sont tout de même accrochés à leurs précieuses applications.
Google a donc dû employer la manière forte. Depuis cette semaine, un nouvel écran a fait son apparition sur Fitbit : ce dernier « recommande » de mettre à jour le service, ce qui revient à passer à Google Health. Le problème ? Dans la majorité des cas, il est impossible de passer outre et d’utiliser l’ancienne appli.
Les réactions sont, on s’en doute, plutôt mitigées : « Je suis tombé à genoux ce matin. Je ne peux pas sortir de là. On est obligé de mettre à jour. Je ne me sens pas bien et je suis triste », peut-on notamment lire sur Reddit. Nos confrères de TechRadar ont également recueilli d’autres réactions, tout aussi négatives : « L’appli Google Health est vraiment nulle. Je veux aussi retrouver mon appli Fitbit », « Il ne reste plus aucune des fonctionnalités que j’appréciais dans l’application Fitbit » ou encore « J’ai bien peur de ne plus jamais retrouver ce genre de suivi ».
Pourquoi les utilisateurs ont-ils autant de mal à passer à Google Health ?
Google Health est, pour le moment, loin d’être à la hauteur des exigences des habitués de Fitbit : les badges, profils de sommeil et autres fonctions sociales ont changé, quand ils n’ont pas tout simplement disparu. Un sondage mené par Android Authority a notamment montré que la moitié des répondants n’aimaient pas la nouvelle application. Google a donc beaucoup de pain sur la planche pour séduire les récalcitrants.
En attendant, les notes de mises à jour de Fitbit indiquent désormais qu’ « un compte Google est désormais nécessaire pour utiliser l’application Google Health, la période de migration des comptes Fitbit étant désormais terminée. » Le support de MyFitnessPal explique, quant à lui, que l’API Fitbit s’éteindra fin octobre.
L’heure des adieux a donc sonné : il faudra passer à Google Health, en espérant que l’outil comble vite ses lacunes… Ou aller voir ailleurs.

articles.title: TFG London cyberattack disrupts systems at Hobbs and Whistles retailers
articles.text:
TFG London detected a cybersecurity incident that impacted IT systems used by the Phase Eight, Hobbs, and Whistles premium fashion brands.
The company disclosed earlier today that several IT systems remain unavailable, although physical stores remain open for customers.
According to the press release, the incident has not affected the group’s other brands, Inside Story and White Stuff, or its operations in Australia and Africa.
TFG London is the UK subsidiary of South Africa’s The Foschini Group, which owns the aforementioned five fashion and homeware brands.
As of mid-2026, the group operated 649 retail locations globally and reported annual sales of £488 million ($646M).
The company said it detected the cyberattack on October 11 and immediately activated its incident response and business continuity plans, bringing in external cybersecurity experts to help contain the threat.
TFG London is investigating whether any customer information has been compromised, and says it will notify affected individuals or organizations if it data has been affected.
BleepingComputer could not find any threat actor publicly claiming the TFG London breach.
The incident at TFG London comes shortly after another UK fashion retailer, ASOS, suffered a data breach after hackers sent push notifications to users of its mobile app.
The company later confirmed that attackers used social engineering to steal an employee’s login credentials and gained unauthorized access to customer data, including names, contact details, and account information.
At this time, TFG London has not confirmed any customer data exposure, but clients of Phase Eight, Hobbs, and Whistles are advised to remain alert for potential phishing and social engineering attacks.
Earlier this week, rumors emerged about an attack at Swedish multinational clothing company H&M, claimed by an attacker saying they were with the ShinyHunters group and threatening to leak stolen data.
Responding to our request for a comment on these allegations, an H&M spokesperson said they were looking into these claims, although current evidence didn't indicate a breach.
“We are aware of information circulating online regarding a potential cyber security incident and are currently investigating the claims,” the H&M spokesperson told BleepingComputer.
“At this time, we have not found any indications that our data environment has been compromised.”

articles.title: Small AI Models Could Soon Self-Replicate on IoT Devices, Anthropic Warns
articles.text:
Small AI models may be only months away from being able to self-replicate across commercial IoT devices, without needing a data center, according to research from Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team.
The study looks at AI worms that run their own model directly on the devices they compromise. Such malware would be hard to shut down because it has no central point to switch off, though it would likely spread slowly.
The researchers bought 15 off-brand Android-based TV boxes for about $55 each. A 26-billion-parameter open-weight model split across them ran at 0.39 tokens per second.
Rather than exploitation, which prior studies have already examined, the team focused on whether models could get AI inference running on unfamiliar hardware. A 9-billion-parameter model did so on eight of the nine hardware types tested.
The researchers then tested the full replication cycle on a closed network of eight emulated Android devices, with the hacking step deliberately kept trivial. Of the open-weight models tested, only GLM-5.2 completed it, reaching all eight devices in four of five runs.
Anthropic considers the results an upper bound for real-world success, but notes that past IoT botnets such as Mirai spread simply by trying default manufacturer credentials.
Models with 30 billion parameters or fewer can already complete many of the individual steps but make mistakes when chaining them together. If they keep improving at their historical rate, Anthropic expects them to reach GLM-5.2’s level by the end of 2026.
“Small weight-based replicators may be possible soon after,” the company says.
Anthropic also looked at a botnet as large as Kimwolf, which infected more than two million devices. If every 15 TV boxes ran one copy of the 26-billion-parameter model, such a botnet would host roughly 133,000 copies. Their combined compute would be worth at most about 40 Nvidia H100 GPUs, and each replication would take more than a day.
[ Read: AI Turns Familiar Cyberattacks Into a Race Against Time ]
Unlike traditional botnets built for specific devices, an AI worm could work out unfamiliar hardware on its own, Anthropic says. Defenders, however, still have some advantages.
Large model transfers and sustained traffic between devices that don’t normally communicate would stand out in ISP monitoring. In addition, moving manufacturers to more secure defaults, such as eliminating default passwords, would also shrink the target pool.
There is no full rogue replicator yet, Anthropic says, but models are getting better at each step in the chain and at passing what they learn on to their copies.

articles.title: Cloudflare’s OHTTP Gateway Refuses to Decrypt Requests That Arrive Through Cloudflare
articles.text:
Cloudflare has opened a closed beta of the Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway, a managed endpoint that decrypts Oblivious HTTP requests on an origin’s behalf. The design decision that drew most of the attention is a refusal rather than a feature: the Gateway will not decrypt requests that reach it from Cloudflare Workers or from hosts proxied through Cloudflare.
Oblivious HTTP, standardized as RFC 9458, splits a request across two parties. The client encrypts the inner HTTP request to the gateway’s public key using HPKE and sends the sealed payload to a relay. The relay sees the client’s IP address but cannot read the request. The gateway decrypts it and forwards plain HTTP to the application, so it sees the contents but only ever sees the relay’s address.
That only works if different operators run the two hops. Putting a Worker in front of the Gateway, or proxying the relay through Cloudflare, would route the client-identifying hop and the decryption hop through the same company, so Cloudflare built a product that declines to run in that configuration. Authors Lara Schull and Akshat Mahajan write that the model "requires that the relay and app server be operated by separate, non-colluding parties."
For a team evaluating this, the practical cost is the relay. Cloudflare does not supply one for the Gateway, and says the component is not the hard part, since relays "can run on any infrastructure provider, and they’re simple." The hard part is being in a position to "verifiably promise to your users that you won’t inspect logs with client identifiers." Cloudflare is also renaming its existing Privacy Gateway to Cloudflare OHTTP Relay to separate the two sides.
The Gateway itself binds to a zone and listens at a fixed path, https://your-zone.com/.well-known/ohttp-gateway, which stops a customer from pointing their gateway at another domain. Cloudflare manages the HPKE keys and serves the public keys from that same path in response to a GET, and clients can fetch keys over a different IP address than the one they use for requests. Standard and chunked OHTTP both work, with chunked recommended for performance. Cloudflare Access runs before decryption, so the relay itself can be authenticated with mutual TLS, static service credentials, or custom external logic.
Protection stops at the network layer, and Cloudflare says so. OHTTP "provides privacy at the network level, and doesn’t touch the inner request body," the post notes, adding that "it’s up to you not to send identifying information (e.g. a user’s email address or username) in the request body." Put a session token or an email address inside the sealed request and the gateway operator has the identity the protocol was meant to withhold.
Discussion on Hacker News divided between readers working out where the protocol fits and readers naming what it costs. Commenter johnhess set out the fit:
This separates who sees what. Cloudflare (or any OHTTP gateway) sees who talks to who, but can’t see the content. The service sees the content but not who you are/your IP. You can imagine a lot of threat models where who you talk to isn’t sensitive, nor is "someone talked to them about X" but knowing both facts is a risk.
Commenter gsnedders gave the most detailed comparison, measuring OHTTP against the obvious do-it-yourself alternative of a SOCKS5 proxy:
OHTTP is designed for a relatively narrow use case: stateless requests where you don’t want the gateway to be able to correlate multiple requests from the same client (i.e., it’s not just about hiding the IP address).
Matching that with SOCKS5, he wrote, means a new TCP connection for every request, no TLS session resumption or 0-RTT, and a deliberately conservative ClientHello, because SOCKS5 is unencrypted and carries the destination in the clear. OHTTP keeps the TLS fingerprinting surface away from the gateway and allows long-lived connections from client to relay and relay to gateway, which he called a significant latency win for workloads like DNS over HTTPS. He also named what the design gives up:
With OHTTP, disclosure of the gateway key essentially means the relay can decrypt recorded traffic that used that key (as there is no forward secrecy), whereas disclosure of the client <-> relay and relay <-> gateway keys matters a lot less.
The pointed questions were operational. Commenter arshxyz asked about a product interaction the announcement does not address:
Does Cloudflare’s WAF (which relies on TLS Fingerprinting) stop working if OHTTP is enabled? If not, does this imply the client metadata is read and processed by Cloudflare but not passed on to the application server?
Commenter Joker_vD asked how IP-based banning survives, and commenter blantonl described the position an operator ends up in: "I respect customer privacy. But I also need to know who is abusing my platforms as well." Commenter thayne raised the aggregation point, noting that when one entity serves a large share of the internet it ends up holding a record of which sites a given IP visited and which IPs visited a given customer, while conceding "that is still better than them having the source ip and the content."
If these reactions are representative, the cryptography is not what teams will argue about. Nobody in the thread disputed that the split works as described. The questions were whether a client exists that speaks the protocol, what a self-hosted relay is worth, and what breaks on the Cloudflare side once the client metadata is gone. Commenter ranger_danger asked whether any current proxy, tunnel, or VPN software supports OHTTP as a transport, which is the adoption question for anyone not shipping their own app. On self-hosting, commenter palata pointed out that a relay run for a handful of people defeats its own purpose, because the service then knows any request through it came from that small group. Commenter scosman described the demand side from experience, saying he had wanted this for update checks in otherwise offline transcription software and ended up calling GitHub releases directly. Commenter freedomben questioned charging for it at all, calling a paid privacy add-on "a poor incentive if the goal is to improve privacy generally."
The closest comparison in the thread was Tor, which commenter maayank reduced to "OHTTP is like a two-hop Tor circuit with a predetermined gateway." The difference is scope. OHTTP needs a client that deliberately speaks the protocol to a known gateway, so it is not general browsing privacy. It fits an app vendor that wants telemetry, inference, or a lookup feature without being able to tie each request to a user. Cloudflare cites Flo Health’s Anonymous Mode and Apple’s Private Cloud Compute as production deployments, with Apple’s LiveCallerID as the case where a service accepts OHTTP from a third party. Cloudflare’s Reference Image work with Apple, which InfoQ covered earlier this year, uses the same transport to request timestamps without revealing who asked.
Cloudflare says the Gateway launches this fall, with a closed beta of the self-serve version starting now. It will be sold as a paid add-on to a customer’s zone, and the announcement does not publish a price. Interested teams can register through a waitlist form.

articles.title: Shareholder revolt leaves Africa Bitcoin Corporation with two directors
articles.text:
Africa Bitcoin Corporation (ABC), South Africa’s listed Bitcoin treasury firm and financial services group, faces a new battle over who joins its board after four directors, including its chairperson and interim chief executive, resigned following a shareholder push to remove them.
With just two directors remaining, the company must rebuild its board while a separate demand to appoint two new non-executive directors remains unresolved.
The dispute centres on two shareholder demands. Investors holding approximately 76% of ABC’s shares called for the appointment of two new non-executive directors, a move the board opposed on governance grounds. A subsequent demand, backed by shareholders holding approximately 71.8% of the company’s shares, sought the removal of four existing directors.
All four have since resigned, making the removal resolutions unnecessary, but the original demand for two new appointments remains in force.
ABC now faces a governance test at a critical point in its transformation from a small-business financier into a Bitcoin treasury company. Shareholders have forced out most of its board, but the fight over who should replace them remains unsettled, raising questions about how the company will balance investor control, regulatory scrutiny, and independent oversight as it pursues its new strategy.
The four directors who resigned are Norma Sephuma, board chairperson; Stafford Masie, the company’s interim chief executive officer (CEO); and independent non-executive directors Snowy Masakale and GG Alcock. The company disclosed the departures in a Stock Exchange News Service (SENS) announcement on Monday, following the supplementary shareholder demand.
The departing directors said they had not taken the decision lightly, but that differences with WGW Capital Proprietary Limited, an ABC shareholder, had become irreconcilable.
“Recently, however, material differences emerged between the Board and WGW,” ABC said in the announcement.
The remaining directors are Robin Coode, an independent non-executive director, and Jonathan Phillips, the company’s financial director. They are working with the company’s advisers to restore the board and committee structures in line with statutory, regulatory, and JSE listing requirements.
Shareholder push for new directors
The dispute began with the demand for two additional directors, which the board addressed in an October 8 announcement. ABC acknowledged that shareholders had validly demanded a meeting under section 61(3) of the Companies Act, but said it did not support the proposed appointments at that time.
“The Board’s concern relates primarily to governance and regulatory integrity given the exceptional circumstances currently facing the Group,” ABC said.
The company stressed that its objection was not a general assessment of the candidates’ professional experience or capabilities. It committed to taking the necessary steps to convene the meeting and put the proposed resolutions to shareholders in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
However, the announcement did not identify the proposed candidates, specify a meeting date, or provide further details about the board’s objections.
The original appointment demand remains unresolved. The two remaining directors must oversee the company while addressing the shareholder request and restoring the board’s composition.
Before its Bitcoin treasury pivot, the company listed as Altvest Capital on the Cape Town Stock Exchange (CTSE) in May 2022, initially valued at R50 million ($3 million). It later introduced three additional share classes—Class A for Umgani Lodge, Class B for Bambanani, and Class C for Altvest Credit Opportunities Fund (ACOF)—to raise funding for investments, but trading in its securities remained thin.
Figures published in its 2024 prospectus show just 42,420 ordinary shares changing hands between July 2023 and July 2024, generating about R131,031.05 ($7,948) in reported turnover.
Altvest moved its equity listing to the Johannesburg Stock Exchange’s (JSE) AltX Market in October 2024, citing limitations in the Cape Town exchange’s ability to attract retail investors and support sizeable capital raises. In May 2026, it transferred its shares to the JSE Main Board.
In 2025, ABC expanded beyond small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) lending to adopt Bitcoin as a long-term treasury asset, making its first disclosed purchase in February. Shareholders approved its rebrand from Altvest to Africa Bitcoin Corporation on September 10, 2025, with the new name and ticker taking effect on the JSE two weeks later.
Since then, the company has retained its SME financing business, while aggressively pushing its Bitcoin investment strategy for institutional investors seeking access to the cryptocurrency.
Deepening leadership crisis
The boardroom dispute comes amid a series of leadership changes following enforcement action by the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA), South Africa’s financial services regulator, against three individuals associated with ABC, which previously operated as Altvest Capital.
The regulator found that former CEO Warren Wheatley, his wife Tatum Keshwar-Wheatley and former chief investment officer Akshay Karan manipulated Altvest shares in September 2022 to artificially inflate the share price and create a misleading impression of market demand and trading activity.
The three were fined a combined R9 million ($546,000) and debarred from the financial services industry for 20 years. The FSCA’s enforcement action was against the individuals, not ABC itself.
Wheatley has disputed the regulator’s findings, describing the transactions as three trades involving just 50 shares worth R301 ($18.26) that were intended to test the CTSE’s trading platform.
In a podcast interview with financial publication Moneyweb on October 9, Wheatley said those trades aimed to document pricing errors on the trading platform ahead of Altvest’s first public offering, disputing the regulator’s finding that they were part of a scheme to manipulate the share price for profit.
FSCA did not respond to a request for comment on its findings, the evidence supporting the market manipulation allegations, and the status of any appeals against its enforcement action.
In an email to TechCabal on September 8, Wheatley declined to comment, saying “none of the affected parties would be providing commentary” until their appeals are submitted.
In a September 1 SENS announcement, ABC said the affected individuals had informed the company that they disputed the findings and intended to seek reconsideration and suspension of the decisions before the Financial Services Tribunal, an independent body reviewing financial regulator decisions.
The Tribunal told TechCabal in September that it had not received applications for reconsideration or suspension involving the named parties at that time. Lwandiso Mgijima of the Financial Services Tribunal confirmed that no applications had been filed at the time.
“We confirm that the Tribunal has not received any applications for reconsideration or suspension involving the parties [Wheatley, Keshwar-Wheatley, and Karan] mentioned in your e-mail. The Tribunal is, accordingly, not in possession of any documents relating to the matter,” Mgijima said.
In a subsequent response to TechCabal, the Financial Services Tribunal confirmed that it received applications for reconsideration and suspension on September 25, 2026, after previously stating that no applications had been received. The matter, registered under case number A43/2026, lists Warren Gregory Wheatley, WGW Capital (Pty) Ltd, Tatum Lucy Wheatley, Tatum Keshwar Investments (Pty) Ltd, and Akshay Suresh Karan as applicants. The Tribunal said it had not yet ruled on the suspension application or set a hearing date.
“We confirm that applications for reconsideration and suspension involving the parties mentioned in your e-mail were received and processed by the Tribunal on 25 September 2026,” the Tribunal said. “We confirm that the Tribunal has not issued a ruling in respect of the suspension application. The process is ongoing.”
Wheatley, ABC’s co-founder and former CEO, resigned from the company with effect from September 21, 2026, after being placed on precautionary leave. Karan, who had also been placed on precautionary leave, resigned as chief investment officer with effect from October 1.
Masie took over as interim CEO after Wheatley was placed on precautionary leave. He has now also quit as interim CEO and director of Bitcoin Strategy, ABC’s Bitcoin investment subsidiary, with an intended final day of service of February 28, 2027.
ABC said Masie had agreed to continue fulfilling his executive responsibilities, supporting the management team, maintaining operational continuity and facilitating an orderly transition to permanent executive leadership.
Despite the board departures, ABC says its executive management team remains in place and will continue managing day-to-day operations within its existing lawful delegated authorities.
The company said its remaining directors, in consultation with its advisers, were addressing the steps needed to restore the appropriate board and committee composition.
Editor’s note: This article has been updated to include confirmation from the Financial Services Tribunal that it received applications for reconsideration and suspension. The case remains pending.

articles.title: LineageOS 24 est déjà là, avec Android 17 et une installation simplifiée
articles.text:
LineageOS 24 est déjà là, avec Android 17 et une installation simplifiée
Plus rapides que bien des constructeurs de smartphones, les développeurs de LineageOS annoncent déjà la disponibilité de LineageOS 24 pour apporter Android 17 et bien des nouveautés à des milliers d'appareils jugés obsolètes.
Alors que le déploiement d'Android 17, lancé en juin dernier, est encore loin d'être terminé sur les smartphones et tablettes compatibles des différents constructeurs, la communauté open source ne traîne pas. Chez Lineage en tout cas, qui fêtera les 10 ans de LineageOS ce 24 décembre 2026, on vient de publier LineageOS 24 beaucoup plus tôt qu'attendu.
Le plus épatant, c'est qu'au-delà d'apporter la nouvelle version majeure d'Android à d'anciens appareils, bien d'autres améliorations et nouveautés sont au menu.
LineageOS 24 apporte Android 17, un nouveau design et de la simplicité
Outre les quelques nouveautés d'Android 17, LineageOS 24 apporte tout d'abord des patchs de sécurité. Ainsi, les rustines déployées d'août 2025 à octobre 2026 ont été combinées au sein de la dernière version.
Les développeurs ont profité de cette mise à jour pour rafraichir l'interface et ajouter quelques fonctionnalités de la plupart de leurs applications maison, notamment avec Material Design 3 Expressive. C'est le cas de Twelve, Etar, Updater, SetupWizard, Seevault ou encore Catapult, tandis qu'un nouvel éditeur d'image baptisé Canvas est de la partie. Le navigateur Jelly supporte également les applications PWA.
Enfin, outre de nombreux détails techniques à retrouver dans le billet dédié, LineageOS est désormais un peu plus simple à installer. De nouveaux outils de flash sont disponibles directement via navigateur pour des méthodes d'installation communes comme ADB, Fastboot, Amlogic Burn et Samsung Odin. Ces outils utilisent WebUSB et permettent de se passer d'utilitaires de flash dédiés. Les solutions déjà existantes demeurent en place, mais il s'agit d'une méthode supplémentaire "pour les utilisateurs qui souhaitent une expérience de flashage plus fluide."
Pour savoir si votre appareil est compatible et prêt pour LineageOS 24, direction la page dédiée.
