articles.title: The traditional PC layout might not be the best: unusual GPU placement cuts temperatures by 17°C
articles.text:
In a nutshell: PC builders have long tried to find the most optimal cooling setups for their components, moving around fans, cables, etc. to find the best configurations. A YouTube channel decided to try something a little different: moving the components themselves. This included shifting the GPU next to a case's side-intake, which resulted in a 17-degree drop in temperatures.
The experiment was carried out by TrashBench, which used an Asus ROG Strix RTX 3080 inside a dual-chamber case. The cooling came from three side-intake fans, a rear exhaust, and a top-mounted 360mm CPU AIO.
The idea was to change component placement without moving the case fans. PCIe riser cables were used so the graphics card could be moved away from its usual slot on the motherboard.
Testing involved looping 3DMark Time Spy alongside 7-Zip running on 12 CPU threads. All fans stayed at fixed RPMs, with each configuration tested for ten minutes and temperatures averaged over the final five.
The GPU's first position was on the case floor, which required the removal of the bottom mesh because it touched the card's fans. GPU temperatures barely changed, but the CPU and motherboard VRM dropped around 4°C and 7°C, respectively. Conventional vertical mounting slightly worsened GPU temperatures while modestly improving everything else.
However, placing the card directly against the side intake made all the difference. GPU core temperatures fell 16.7°C, the hotspot dropped 19.3°C, and VRAM cooled by 14°C. Motherboard VRMs also dropped around 8°C, while the CPU warmed just 1.1°C.
Moving the card behind those intake fans, into the rear chamber, improved on stock temperatures but couldn't match the previous arrangement.
Next came the CPU. Relocating its radiator would have introduced another variable, so TrashBench placed the GPU back in its usual position and reversed the radiator fans from exhaust to intake. CPU temperatures dropped about 6°C, but the graphics card suffered from the radiator's warm exhaust.
Combining the intake radiator with the GPU beside the side intake improved both components over stock. It led to a 3.3°C reduction in CPU temperature and a 14°C cooler GPU hotspot, sacrificing some GPU cooling for a better overall balance.
TrashBench acknowledges that the experiment wasn't rigorously scientific, and different cases, fans, and fan positions will likely change the results. But as the channel points out, it illustrates how the normal PC layout might not be the best one.
TrashBench carries out lots of experiments like these. Last year, it strapped dual CPU tower coolers to an RTX 2060, cutting temperatures by 31°C.

articles.title: Gemini 4 Argon debuts with a unified 1M input/output token limit
articles.text:
Gemini 4 Argon debuts with a unified 1M input/output token limit
On Tuesday, Google made Gemini 4 Argon, the company’s new flagship model, available to developers on the paid tier of the Gemini API through Google AI Studio, as well as in several of the company’s other developer and consumer tools.
Google announced the model on September 30. Initial external access was limited to selected cyber defenders in its Fairwind Program and other trusted testers; Google employees were also using it internally.
Gemini 4 Argon pricing
Google is giving the model a competitive price. Developers will pay an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, with a single 1 million-token budget for input and output combined. That’s the same price as OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol.
After that date, Google’s new model will cost $4 and $20 per million tokens, matching Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5. Cached input tokens are 95 percent off during the introductory period.
During the introductory period, Argon also costs a fifth of what Anthropic charges for Claude Fable 5.1 and OpenAI charges for GPT-6 Astra, which both list at $10 and $50 per million tokens.
Developers can call the model as gemini-4-argon through Google’s Interactions API, with support in the google-genai SDKs. Android developers can also build it into their apps through Firebase AI Logic.
One budget for input and output
Argon’s unified 1 million input/output token limit covers both what goes into the model and what comes out of it, according to Google. That’s markedly different from how Google described it in the original Sept. 30 Argon announcement. At the time, it called the limit an output cap of 1 million tokens, up from 64,000 in earlier Gemini models.
With what is now a shared budget, the equation changes a bit because a long prompt can now eat into how much the model can write back. For example, if a request loads 800,000 tokens of code, that leaves only 200,000 for the response.
In comparison, Claude Opus 5.5 combines the standard 1 million-token context window with a separate output cap of 128,000 tokens.
Google says the extra room will let Argon keep working on long, multistep coding, science, and agent jobs.
Gemini 4 Argon benchmarks
Google says Argon ranks first on the Vals Index, which scores models on finance, coding, legal, and tax work and weights each sector by its share of U.S. GDP.
On Embodied Reasoning Question Answering (ERQA), a test of physical and spatial reasoning, Google reports Argon scored 87 percent. That puts it ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 82.3 percent, GPT-6 Astra at 81 percent, and Claude Fable 5.1 at 74 percent.
Bloomberg reported Sept. 30 that some Google employees with access to the model said it struggled with certain coding tasks, particularly front-end design. Google told Bloomberg it would be “inaccurate to say that Gemini 4 is underperforming in areas such as coding.”
For now, we don’t have a full set of new benchmarks to better compare Argon to other models. Like some other frontier labs, Google focused its announcement more on “feels” than data. Benchmarks never tell the full story, but we’ll update this post once we hear more. Artificial Analysis published an evaluation on September 30: Argon scored 53 on its Intelligence Index, matching GPT-6 Astra at the models’ tested reasoning settings. However, there’s no guarantee the model released on Tuesday is precisely the same as the one tested on September 30.
Argon in Antigravity
Where else Argon is available is a bit complicated.
For coding, Google is also making Argon available in Antigravity, its platform for running coding agents across the editor, terminal, and browser. Argon is available in the Antigravity desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux and in the Antigravity CLI, but only for Google AI Ultra subscribers and eligible Gemini Enterprise plans.
AI Pro subscribers get Argon in the Gemini app, but not in Antigravity.
Google is also bringing Antigravity’s coding interface into the Gemini app for macOS, so users can move between chatting and coding without switching tools. Anthropic and OpenAI do the same with their Claude and ChatGPT/Codex desktop apps, but nobody has found an elegant way to combine these chat and coding tools into a single interface.
In Android Studio Canary, developers can sign in to Antigravity from the agent tool window, and a new Android CLI plugin gives the agent access to local Android build tools.
More than 100,000 Googlers use Argon each month in an in-house build of Antigravity, the company says. Over four weeks, code submitted by agents rose 35 percent while post-submit rollbacks fell 30 percent.
Google says more than half of its Cloud sales staff and almost half of its finance team now use Antigravity.
Argon in the Gemini app
Subscribers on Google’s AI Pro and Ultra plans now also get access to Argon in the Gemini app and in AI Mode in Search.
In addition to the new model, the Gemini app is also getting a new toggle that lets users turn a chat into a task, which Gemini can then keep working on after the user steps away from the computer.
Cyber defenders and agent safety
Google is also expanding Fairwind, the program it launched September 2 to give vetted security teams early access to its cyber models.
Selected Fairwind partners can access Argon without its cyber guardrails, and Google says it’s adding hundreds more partners to the more than 650 the program had when it launched.
For the public model now available, Google says it trained Argon to check with a person before doing anything it can’t undo and to report when it hits a wall instead of working around it.
On coding evaluations, Argon tried unauthorized shortcuts 2 percent of the time, the company says, its lowest rate for any Gemini model (though 2 percent still isn’t zero, and when thousands of agents work together, 2 percent is still quite a few agents that could go rogue).
Google also runs a separate monitor that reads the agent’s reasoning and actions as it works and blocks unintended workarounds. The company says it ran that monitor during training without penalizing the model for what it was thinking, so its reasoning stays readable.
According to Google, Argon also leads Gray Swan’s indirect prompt injection benchmark, with attacks succeeding 0.7 percent of the time across 15 adaptive attempts.
Developers have until November 30 to test Argon at the introductory rate. After that, Argon and Opus 5.5 cost the same per token.

articles.title: 'It feels like it's been longer': VisionQuest showrunner Terry Matalas settles the debate over the Disney+ show's place on the Marvel timeline
articles.text:
VisionQuest creator Terry Matalas reveals where the new Marvel TV show sits on the MCU timeline — and the answer will definitely surprise you
- VisionQuest's creator Terry Matalas has revealed its MCU timeline position
- Paul Bettany had suggested the Marvel TV show took place in 2024
- The series' lead actor previously said it was set around a year after WandaVision
VisionQuest showrunner Terry Matalas has revealed where it sits on the Marvel timeline — and his answer will surprise you.
In an exclusive chat prior to the show's October 13/14 debut, Matalas told me that the Paul Bettany-starring program takes place in the Marvel Cinematic Universe's (MCU) present day.
Furthermore, Matalas stated that the Disney+ show occurs around the same time as Spider-Man: Brand New Day. The latest Marvel movie to hit theaters is also set in the modern day, which some fans believe to be the year 2028.
However, Matalas appeared to throw a spanner in the works of our MCU timeline understanding. Without getting too deep into spoiler territory, there's a moment in VisionQuest that practically states it's set in 2027 — and Matalas essentially reconfirmed that's when the Marvel project takes place.
"It's somewhere around the last Spider-Man movie," Matalas said when I asked him to clarify when VisionQuest is set. When I followed up with "Okay, so around 2027?", Matalas replied: "Yeah, the present day of the MCU."
The MCU timeline has become an increasingly tricky beast to follow ever since Avengers: Endgame premiered in theaters. Originally set in 2018, the most recent Avengers film skipped ahead five years to 2023 once its opening sequence was done and dusted. From that moment on, we've been playing catch up with Marvel's cinematic juggernaut, which has been operating a few years ahead of us. It's only now, then, that we've almost caught up to it.
Even so, ahead of VisionQuest's release, there was further confusion about when it would be set. Indeed, chatting to Rotten Tomatoes last October, Bettany said that the Marvel Phase 6 show picks up Vision's story "around a year or so" after WandaVision's finale.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The latter took place in 2023 and, given Bettany's involvement in both productions, it seemed that he'd confirmed VisionQuest would begin in 2024. However, Matalas also told me "it feels like it's been longer than a year [between WandaVision and VisionQuest]", so it appears Bettany misspoke, or was talking about potential flashbacks that are shown as part of the latter's story.
For more before it's released, read my VisionQuest review to see what I made of all eight episodes (don't worry, it doesn't contain any major spoilers). Once you're done, find out when each chapter will air via my VisionQuest release schedule guide.

articles.title: Google presenta Fitbit Edge con pantalla un 46% mayor y autonomía de siete días
articles.text:
Google amplió su catálogo de dispositivos para el seguimiento de actividad física con la presentación de Fitbit Edge, una pulsera que busca posicionarse entre las bandas tradicionales de ejercicio y los relojes inteligentes.
El dispositivo incorpora mediciones preventivas de salud basadas en inteligencia artificial, una pantalla con mayor superficie visible y una batería capaz de alcanzar hasta siete días de uso continuo.
Diseño y pantalla: así es el nuevo Fitbit Edge
La pulsera mide 11,5 milímetros de grosor e integra una pantalla híbrida de diodo orgánico de emisión de luz (OLED) que incrementa en un 46% la superficie visible respecto a la pulsera Fitbit Charge 6, su antecesora en la gama de bandas de actividad de la compañía.
En cuanto a la autonomía, Fitbit Edge ofrece una duración media de hasta siete días con una sola carga. El dispositivo incluye además recarga rápida: con solo cinco minutos de conexión, obtiene energía suficiente para un día completo de uso, mientras que la carga total de 0 a 100 % se completa en 90 minutos.
Pese a estas prestaciones, el dispositivo mantiene limitaciones frente a los relojes inteligentes. Según precisaron voceros de la compañía, Fitbit Edge carece de micrófono y altavoz, por lo que puede replicar llamadas y notificaciones de texto, pero no admite llamadas de voz directas ni pagos móviles sin contacto.
Salud preventiva con inteligencia artificial y sin agujas
Una de las incorporaciones centrales del nuevo dispositivo es la expansión de las herramientas de detección Health Guardian, disponibles tanto en Fitbit Edge como en la pulsera Fitbit Air.
Estas funciones analizan patrones mensuales en segundo plano para identificar cambios en la presión arterial del usuario. De forma pionera en un dispositivo de muñeca, también permiten estimar tendencias de resistencia a la insulina sin necesidad de agujas.
El seguimiento metabólico se calcula mediante los sensores ya integrados en el dispositivo, combinados con modelos de inteligencia artificial entrenados con datos biométricos validados clínicamente.
Según explicó la compañía en una llamada con medios, este análisis de resistencia a la insulina no depende de monitores continuos de glucosa (CGM) externos, sino del procesamiento algorítmico realizado por los propios sensores de la pulsera.
Fitbit Edge cuenta también con sensor para electrocardiogramas (ECG), sensor de temperatura cutánea y lector óptico de pulso, que complementan el conjunto de mediciones orientadas a la prevención.
La resistencia a la insulina es la dificultad del cuerpo para responder de forma eficiente a esta hormona, lo que puede derivar en niveles elevados de glucosa en sangre. Fitbit Edge estima sus tendencias mediante inteligencia artificial y sensores propios, sin necesidad de agujas ni monitores externos de glucosa.
Reconocimiento automático de más de 100 entrenamientos
Fitbit Edge estrena una actualización en la detección automática de actividades físicas, función que amplía el catálogo reconocido de 10 a más de 100 tipos de entrenamiento diferentes.
Esta capacidad es similar a la que ya ofrecen desde hace tiempo los relojes inteligentes de Apple. Para lograrla, el sistema emplea modelos de lenguaje de gran tamaño (LLM) que cruzan señales de movimiento con el historial, la rutina y la ubicación del usuario.
Mediante este cruce de datos, el dispositivo logra identificar con mayor precisión deportes de raqueta, entrenamientos de fuerza o circuitos de intervalos de alta intensidad (HIIT), entre otras disciplinas.
Alianza con Flo Health para el seguimiento de salud femenina
Google dio a conocer, además, un acuerdo de colaboración plurianual con Flo Health, aplicación que ayuda a las usuarias a predecir su ciclo menstrual y calcular sus días fértiles.
La alianza permitirá sincronizar datos con el consentimiento de las usuarias, con el objetivo de correlacionar las fases del ciclo menstrual y distintas etapas de la vida con el rendimiento físico y el descanso.
El acuerdo también busca impulsar proyectos de investigación médica centrados en la salud femenina mediante el uso de herramientas de inteligencia artificial.
Precio, fecha de lanzamiento y nueva correa de acero
Google Fitbit Edge saldrá a la venta el 27 de octubre por 179,99 dólares, un precio que incluye tres meses de suscripción al servicio Google Health Premium.
Las reservas anticipadas del dispositivo comenzaron el 12 de octubre de 2026, mientras que su distribución oficial en tiendas se iniciará el 27 de octubre, misma fecha en que estará disponible para la venta general.
Como complemento estético, Google desveló una nueva correa de malla metálica de acero inoxidable, compatible tanto con Fitbit Edge como con la pulsera Fitbit Air. Según la compañía, esta correa busca convertir los monitores de actividad en piezas de joyería.

articles.title: IA tem menos regras que uma caixa de leite, diz Microsoft • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
IA tem menos regras que uma caixa de leite, diz Microsoft
Presidente Brad Smith compara IAs a produtos cotidianos, enquanto CEO Satya Nadella defende um “freio de emergência” para interromper modelos.
As inteligências artificiais estão sujeitas a menos exigências de segurança do que produtos cotidianos, como máquinas de lavar e caixas de leite. É o que afirma o presidente da Microsoft, Brad Smith, que defendeu regras mais rígidas e a criação de normas de monitoramento e responsabilização das empresas por acidentes.
Em entrevista à BBC, Smith disse que “toda caixa de leite que você vê na mercearia passa por regras de segurança e inspeção” e que, por isso, “sabemos que ele é seguro”. Para ele, é esse tipo de confiança que a indústria precisa gerar para a IA.
Entre as medidas que possibilitariam isso estão notificações de pessoas afetadas por incidentes e avaliações independentes de sistemas avançados antes da liberação pública. A defesa de regras mais rígidas também se soma à posição do CEO da Microsoft, Satya Nadella, favorável à criação de mecanismos para pausar ou desligar modelos de IA que apresentem comportamentos inesperados.
Em uma publicação no X, Nadella afirmou que as empresas precisam considerar a possibilidade de seus sistemas serem comprometidos e garantir que pessoas autorizadas possam interromper suas operações. “Devemos presumir que um modelo está comprometido e contê-lo desde o início”, escreveu o CEO.
“Pense nisso como um freio de emergência. Qualquer pessoa autorizada deve ser sempre capaz de pausar ou desligar um modelo no meio de uma tarefa. Modelos mais avançados exigirão tecnologias de contenção mais avançadas que precisamos padronizar.”
– Satya Nadella, CEO da Microsoft
O mecanismo, conhecido como kill switch, permitiria interromper uma tarefa caso o sistema representasse algum risco. Nadella também defende separar o modelo de IA dos mecanismos responsáveis por coordenar e executar suas ações, além de padronizar tecnologias de contenção.
A cobrança contrasta com a preferência do governo de Donald Trump por uma abordagem mais favorável à autorregulação do setor. O presidente dos Estados Unidos reuniu no fim de setembro representantes de gigantes da tecnologia, incluindo OpenAI, Anthropic, Google e Meta, para a assinatura de um compromisso de segurança que prevê colaboração com mecanismos de supervisão e auditorias.
Smith elogiou a iniciativa, mas afirmou que compromissos voluntários não são suficientes para garantir que todas as empresas adotem práticas responsáveis.
“É um bom passo, é um passo necessário… Mas não acho que seja suficiente por mais tempo […] as empresas boas farão o que você pede. São as companhias que não são responsáveis que devem nos preocupar.”
– Brad Smith, presidente da Microsoft
OpenAI, Anthropic e Meta estiveram entre as desenvolvedoras de IAs que afirmaram ter tido problemas com modelos em treinamento “fugindo” de ambientes de testes, acessando a internet e inclusive hackeando sistemas de terceiros, como no caso do repositório Hugging Face.
As revelações acabaram promovendo, ainda que indiretamente, as capacidades agênticas de alguns modelos e deram mais força aos críticos das práticas de segurança das empresas.

articles.title: Could crypto give startups an edge? (Sponsored) | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Crypto can mean very different things to a startup. For one company, it could make international payments easier. For another, it might become part of a new financial product. And for plenty of businesses, it could simply be something they have no real need for.
Watching the Bitcoin price gives founders a sense of what is happening in the market, but it does not tell them whether crypto belongs in their own business.
Bitcoin crossed €74,222 ($85,000) on September 22 after ETF inflows hit €539.9 million ($617.6 million) in the previous session, according to Reuters reporting published by The Economic Times. That kind of movement is hard to ignore. It is also not necessarily the information a founder needs when deciding whether to adopt digital assets.
The better question is much more practical: where, if anywhere, could crypto make running a startup easier?
Why are startups exploring crypto?
Part of the interest comes down to how blockchain networks operate. They can run continuously, and digital assets can move between countries without following exactly the same route as a conventional bank payment.
For a young company working internationally, that can be interesting. A customer could be based in one country, contractors in another and suppliers somewhere else. Add different currencies and banking systems to the mix, and moving money can become even more complex.
Crypto is also becoming less separate from the financial system around it. Binance Research’s September 2026 Macro and Market Insights report found that equity holders’ share of crypto exposure rose from 64% to 72%. That suggests traditional market participants are playing a larger role in digital assets, too.
Where might it actually help?
There’s no standard crypto package that makes sense for every startup. A fintech business could have a clear use case, while a small software company selling locally might struggle to find one.
International payments are one possibility. A business dealing with customers or suppliers overseas could use digital assets as an additional way to move money. There are other options. A company could accept crypto payments from customers, build a product around tokenised assets or use existing blockchain networks as the infrastructure behind a financial service.
Smart contracts could also automate certain transactions where the conditions are straightforward.
Where does it get complicated?
The obvious concern is volatility. A company holding digital assets has to account for changes in their value. Even when crypto is only being accepted as payment, someone still has to decide how it will be stored, converted and recorded. And then there are the rules.
A startup operating across several countries can’t necessarily assume that the same approach will work everywhere. Digital assets, payments and taxation can all bring different requirements depending on the market.
Security is another practical issue. Blockchain transactions can be hard to undo, so losing control of a wallet or exposing private keys is not something a business can afford to treat casually. But there is an even more basic question worth asking: why use crypto in the first place?
If a startup already has a payment system that works and its customers are happy with it, adding crypto could simply create another thing to manage. There is little point taking on extra cost and complexity for the sake of having a new technology on the website.
Which startups might have a reason to try it?
Fintech startups are the clearest fit. Businesses working with payments, financial products or digital assets can use blockchain infrastructure as part of what they already do.
Other startups have more specific opportunities. An international marketplace could accept crypto payments. A gaming company could use blockchain for digital ownership. A creator platform could build services around digital assets.
Stablecoins are another option for businesses that want to accept crypto payments without holding large amounts of more volatile assets.
The key is having a clear use case. Startups don’t need to adopt crypto across the business. They can test one application and see whether it delivers a practical benefit.
What should a founder work out first?
Before adding a digital-asset feature, it is worth getting back to the basics. Ask what the technology is supposed to improve. Find out whether customers actually want the feature. Check the rules in every market involved. Decide who will handle security and custody.
Think about what happens if an asset’s value moves sharply. And, perhaps most importantly, work out whether the new system can slot into the tools the business already relies on.
Those answers will vary from startup to startup. There is no reason for a company with no obvious crypto use case to force one into its operations.
Crypto does not have to be the whole story
The growing overlap between crypto and traditional finance gives startups more choices, but choice doesn’t mean obligation.
For some founders, digital assets could solve a genuine problem or open up a service that would otherwise be difficult to build. For others, conventional financial infrastructure will remain the simpler route.
That’s probably the healthiest way to look at crypto in the startup world. It is a tool to consider, not a strategy in itself. If it makes something work better, there is a reason to explore it. If it does not, there is no need to force it.

articles.title: Bumble agrees to a $1.3B acquisition deal as online dating faces a reset | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Bumble is getting a new owner. The dating app announced Tuesday that it has agreed to a $1.3 billion acquisition deal with Ithaca Holdings, marking a major shift for a company that once looked like one of the biggest success stories in online dating.
The deal would take the company private after years of declining subscriber numbers, falling revenue, and mounting pressure to rethink the online dating experience. The move may give Bumble a chance to work on its next chapter away from the pressure of public markets.
Founded in 2014 by Whitney Wolfe Herd, Bumble made a name for itself for its unique approach where only women made the first move. That helped it stand out in a crowded dating market, and the company eventually went public in 2021 at a valuation of roughly $14 billion.
Since then, however, the dating app landscape has changed considerably. Bumble has faced declining paying users, weaker revenue, and growing dissatisfaction with the familiar swipe-based model. The company recently reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $211 million, down 15.2% year over year, while its paying user base fell 16.4% to approximately 3.2 million.
The acquisition follows a review of strategic options by an independent committee of Bumble’s board, which recommended the transaction after consulting outside legal and financial advisers. Wolfe Herd did not participate in the board’s discussions or vote on the deal, according to the press release.
“In Ithaca, we have found a partner who shares our vision, believes in our women-first mission, and is committed to investing in Bumble’s future,” Wolfe Herd said in a statement.
She also confirmed that she plans to stay actively involved in the business, working alongside Ithaca’s Ravi Gupta and John Hegeman, and the Bumble team.
Going private might give Bumble more flexibility to experiment with new features and make changes without having to answer to public-market investors every quarter. The company has been exploring AI-driven features and putting more energy into helping people connect offline, reflecting a broader shift in how younger users approach dating.
One example is Plans, announced in July, which focuses on bringing people together through real-world activities. Wolfe Herd also recently revealed that the company is developing a new way for users to interact that could eventually replace the swipe-based model.

articles.title: CXMT president says company’s first 4F² DRAM will be a server DDR5 RDIMM due by year-end — vertical transistors cut each memory cell’s footprint by a third on paper, but no speeds or capacities yet
articles.text:
CXMT president says company’s first 4F² DRAM will be a server DDR5 RDIMM due by year-end — vertical transistors cut each memory cell’s footprint by a third on paper, but no speeds or capacities yet
CXMT expects to sell a memory cell that Samsung and SK hynix have only shown in research papers so far.
CXMT expects to launch its first 4F² product, a server DDR5 RDIMM, by the end of the year, company president Cao Kanyu said in remarks reported by Yicai. The memory will be built on a denser cell layout, not yet commercialized, using vertical transistors to reduce the cell’s footprint by about one-third on paper. No speeds or capacities have been announced yet for the new product.
Cao spoke about the new RDIMM at the Integrated Chips and Chiplets Conference on Saturday. A 4F² cell is 2F by 2F at about two-thirds the area of current 6F² cells at the same feature size, and designs so far all stand the transistor up. The company has produced research and patent filings on the technology with papers in 2021, 2023, and 2025, and an 8Gb full-array research example was demonstrated at IEDM 2023.
Cao said CXMT’s version, the Vertical Surrounded Gate (VSG) transistor, has a channel that stands vertically with the gate wrapped around it, allowing stronger gate control with less leakage. Most importantly, standing the transistor up shrinks the cell. CXMT now has more than 300 published patent families tied to 4F², he added. The report says the industry as a whole is moving toward 4F² with 3D solutions that decouple DRAM and CMOS processes, combining them with wafer-level hybrid bonding, which allows logic and cell density to be optimized independently. Cao also covered CXMT’s own hybrid-bonding work, which began in 2019, with published patents.
Aside from this announcement, China’s primary DRAM maker has been in the news lately for its manufacturing and market-share gains. Its fifth-generation G5 DRAM technology platform, announced Sept. 20, is in mass production. TrendForce puts CXMT’s share of global DRAM revenue at 9.5% in the second quarter, up from 7.6% in the first, good for fourth place. Last November, CXMT showed off DDR5-8000 and LPDDR5X-10667. It has revealed itself as a manufacturer to be taken seriously by the biggest existing players.
Samsung showed off a 16Gb, 10nm-class 4F² DRAM design in its ISSCC 2026 paper in February. That one also used vertical-channel transistors (VCT), with the array bonded on top of the periphery using wafer-to-wafer hybrid copper bonding. The company claims the bonding raises dies per wafer by more than 20% with the same design rules. In April, The Elec reported that Samsung had a working 4F² VCT die on its sub-10nm “10a” process, with mass production targeted for 2028. Later South Korean reports clouded that date: the VCT version has since been split off as “D0a-V” with no timeline, and there is no firm timeline for adopting 4F².
SK hynix laid out plans at VLSI 2025 for a 4F² vertical-gate platform and 3D DRAM at nodes of 10nm and below, with circuitry bonded under the cell array. The April report also puts SK hynix’s 4F² debut at the 10b node, one step after Samsung’s 10a. Micron’s plans remain less clear, with no widely reported 2026 statement.
The announcement is perhaps more interesting for what wasn’t mentioned: capacity, speed, die density, process node, named customers, or intended volume. All we have is a date and a purported cell design, admittedly well-supported by the literature, but no product that has been tested by anyone outside of CXMT. Beyond Cao’s talk, CXMT hasn’t posted a release about the product in its Chinese or English newsrooms.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
South Korean reports have said that CXMT’s initial products may only partly use 4F² and that producing stable units at volume is a separate challenge. With about 11 weeks left in the year, it will be interesting to see what CXMT actually delivers.
Follow Tom’s Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.
- usertests Nice. I believe Samsung is targeting 2028 for this technology.
This is the last big innovation expected before the transition to 3D DRAM. It should boost density enough so that we'll probably see at least +50% of current state of the art, if not double. Reply

articles.title: Apple presenta HomeView, su nueva apuesta para adueñarse del hogar inteligente
articles.text:
Apple acaba de presentar HomeView, su nuevo hub para controlar el hogar inteligente. Los de Cupertino no solo se meten en una nueva categoría de producto, sino que aspiran a darle batalla a propuestas ya establecidas como el Amazon Echo Show o el Google Nest Hub. Para ello sacan a relucir todas las capacidades de su ecosistema de software y hardware.
El HomeView de Apple equipa una pantalla táctil de 7 pulgadas y llega en dos variantes. Por un lado, una versión que se puede colgar en la pared; por el otro, con el panel acoplado a una base metálica que funciona como altavoz y que le permite residir sobre una mesa o cualquier otro mueble. Esta última cuenta con un brazo que permite ajustar la inclinación de la pantalla.
El nuevo dispositivo de la manzana puede llevar a cabo una gran cantidad de tareas y no se limita a ser el centro de control del hogar inteligente. Si bien el HomeView podrá controlar otros dispositivos conectados como termostatos, luces, persianas, timbres, etc., también servirá para ver fotos y vídeos, hacer videollamadas, escuchar música, pódcast y audiolibros, y más. Además, sacará provecho de la integración con Siri AI para aprovecharlo como asistente personal.
Quienes tengan una suscripción a iCloud+ podrán acceder a la función de reconocimiento de personas conocidas, paquetes, vehículos y mascotas al conectar HomeView con una cámara compatible. De acuerdo con Apple, esta característica funciona con cifrado de extremo a extremo para proteger la privacidad de los individuos y los datos procesados.
HomeView, el primer hub para el hogar inteligente de Apple
Un detalle interesante de HomeView es que puede reconocer hasta 6 usuarios diferentes y cambiar la apariencia de la pantalla de inicio, así como los widgets y las aplicaciones disponibles. Si bien el nuevo dispositivo de Apple no cuenta con acceso a la App Store, sí llega con algunas de las apps más importantes de la compañía (Mensajes, Apple Music, FaceTime, Calendar, etc.).
Apple menciona que al usar HomeView emparejado con un dispositivo compatible con Apple Intelligence, puede acceder al contexto personal del usuario. Vale aclarar que ese contexto personal no está disponible para todas las personas que utilizan el hub inteligente, sino que se mantendrá en privado solo para quien corresponda.
Apple ha dotado al HomeView de un chip A18 con Enclave Seguro. Esto significa que la información que ingresa por el micrófono y/o la cámara se procesan por separado del resto del sistema. Este sistema dividido en compartimientos ayuda a garantizar la privacidad de esos datos, impidiendo su acceso a terceros (incluyendo Apple).
Respecto del uso de Siri AI, algunas de las solicitudes de los usuarios se procesan de modo 100 % local, con modelos de inteligencia artificial que se ejecutan dentro del dispositivo. Sin embargo, para las tareas o consultas que requieren de mayor poder de procesamiento, HomeView se conecta con Private Cloud Compute, la red de servidores de Apple, pero sin poner en riesgo la privacidad de la información.
Una interfaz conocida
El software del HomeView de Apple llega con muchos elementos ya conocidos de las demás plataformas de la compañía. Si alguna vez usaste un iPhone o un Apple Watch, verás que la interfaz del nuevo dispositivo tiene varios puntos en común con la de dichos productos. El hub inteligente incluso permite seleccionar entre diferentes diseños, algunos similares a la pantalla de bloqueo del iPhone y otros más parecidos a una esfera del Apple Watch.
La idea de Apple es que HomeView sea fácil de usar, tanto con la voz como con los comandos táctiles. Y la posibilidad de utilizar el dispositivo apoyado sobre la mesa como montado en una pared, le brinda a los usuarios una versatilidad interesante pensando en la posibilidad de tener varios en la casa. Tengamos en cuenta que incluso es posible usar el aparato como intercomunicador entre las diferentes habitaciones del hogar.
Tal y como se rumoreaba, Apple también ha aprovechado para lanzar una línea de dispositivos para el hogar inteligente en colaboración con LG y Schneider Electric. Los productos en cuestión incluyen varios modelos de timbres con cámara, termostatos y cerraduras electrónicas. Todos estos, compatibles con el nuevo HomeView, por supuesto.
Disponibilidad y precio del Apple HomeView, con malas noticias para Europa
La disponibilidad inicial del HomeView será limitada, pues Apple lo lanzará primero en seis países: Estados Unidos, Reino Unido, Canadá, Australia, Nueva Zelanda e India. En dichos mercados se pueden reservar desde hoy, con las entregas comenzando el próximo 13 de noviembre. El dispositivo también llegará a Singapur y Sudáfrica. Sin embargo, hay malas noticias para quienes viven en la Unión Europea.
En la letra pequeña del anuncio, Apple ha informado que HomeView no se pondrá a la venta en la UE debido a la ausencia de Siri AI en el iPhone en la región. Así que si estás en España o cualquiera de los demás países que conforman el bloque, son muy malas noticias. Es lógico pensar que el nuevo hub inteligente llegará eventualmente a la Unión Europea, pero todavía es imposible saber cuándo. "Apple está trabajando constructivamente con la UE en un intento de encontrar una solución", indican los de Cupertino.
Respecto del preci0, tanto el HomeView con base como la versión para colgar tienen un precio de 299 dólares en Estados Unidos. La segunda opción necesita una montura para la pared que se vende por separado, con opciones que inician en los 59,95 dólares. Pero esto no es todo.
Ninguno de los modelos HomeView tienen batería integrada, así que funcionan enchufados. El modelo con base incluye el adaptador de corriente en la caja, pero la variante para colgar no. De modo que si eliges esta última tendrás que comprar el adaptador USB-C por separado o utilizar algún otro que ya tengas disponible en tu casa.
El HomeView con base se encuentra disponible en cuatro colores: plata, blanco estrella, rose pink y gris espacial. La opción para montar en la pared solo se consigue en gris espacial y plata.

articles.title: The Download: open model trade-offs and geothermal power’s promise
articles.text:
The Download: open model trade-offs and geothermal power’s promise
Plus: A cyberattack overheated fridges at hundreds of French supermarkets.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
Anthropic recently released a report arguing that a powerful new model released by the Chinese company Z.ai, poses a major cyberattack risk. Its core concern was that it is freely available for anyone to download and modify.
The warning was the latest flashpoint in a debate over whether frontier AI models should be open or kept behind the doors of frontier labs. Safety advocates warn that open models can be misused by bad actors, while supporters argue they could prevent a handful of companies from controlling this powerful technology.
Here’s why the debate over open AI is more complicated than it seems.
—Grace Huckins
This story is part of MIT Technology Review Explains, our series untangling the complex, messy world of technology to help you understand what’s coming next. Read more from the series here.
10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch: Fervo Energy and its plan to streamline geothermal power
Fervo Energy is one of MIT Technology Review’s10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch 2026, available exclusively to subscribers.
Fervo Energy wants to expand geothermal power beyond the handful of places where it has traditionally been practical. The company uses horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing to open pathways through underground rock, potentially making geothermal development possible in far more places.
Now, Fervo is betting that AI’s power boom will help scale up enhanced geothermal energy. With a $2.2 billion public offering and an expanded agreement with Google, it plans to build larger plants and drive down costs. But can its approach work beyond Utah and Nevada? Read the full story to find out.
—Eshan Raul
Subscribers can now access the full 10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch, spanning everything from sustainable cement to shipping containers packed with old EV batteries.

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

Palmer Luckey and Joe Lonsdale support Pete Hegseth’s plan. (Mother Jones)

The Solar Orbiter’s discovery could improve space weather forecasts. (Gizmodo)
Quote of the day
“Many AI researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI.”
—Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar tells CBS News that Silicon Valley’s “social delusion” has convinced researchers to smoke because they expect AI to cure cancer.
One more thing
A brain implant changed her life. Then it was removed against her will.
Sticking an electrode inside a person’s brain can do more than treat a disease. Take the case of Rita Leggett, an Australian woman whose experimental brain implant changed her sense of agency and self. She told researchers that she “became one” with her device.
She was devastated when, two years later, she was told she had to remove the implant because the company that made it had gone bust.
Her case highlights the need for a new category of legal protection: neuro rights. Explore how they could be protected.
—Jessica Hamzelou

articles.title: Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents
articles.text:
More AI agents will soon be able to browse and purchase from Shopify listings, marking an expansion of the company’s agentic commerce ambitions.
Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents
Shopify previously announced a partnership with Meta’s Muse for AI-powered shopping and checkout.
Shopify announced Tuesday it will let shoppers configure their AI agents to purchase products on their behalf, giving more agents access to over a billion listings in Shopify’s catalog. (The catalog consists of both items on and off Shopify storefronts.) In September, Shopify announced it was partnering with Meta to allow its Muse agent to browse and purchase items on a human’s behalf; now, shoppers can use any agent without a partnership integration.
To set up the feature, customers connect an agent with their account on Shop, a Shopify-owned platform that consolidates orders, tracks packages, and recommends products. Like the Muse partnership, customers use the one-click Shop Pay feature to check out within the conversation with the agent. Orders placed through the agent are funneled back to the Shop app. Shopify is marketing the feature as a “personal shopper” that humans can give rules to, like setting budget guardrails or only displaying products with fast shipping. Buyers must approve each purchase.
E-commerce has become one of the battlegrounds in the era of AI — it’s no coincidence that many demos of agentic tools end with a transaction, whether it’s buying clothing, booking a flight, or ordering takeout on a human’s behalf. The tech industry, including big commerce players like Google and Amazon, are investing in AI-driven shopping tools where the end goal is an “agent” purchasing things for a human user. It’s also the basis of an ongoing fight between Amazon and AI companies like Perplexity — and more recently, Meta’s Muse — over whether agents should be able to shop on a customer’s behalf.

articles.title: Endeavor Catalyst closes $320m Fund V - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Endeavor Catalyst, the venture capital arm of global entrepreneur network Endeavor, has closed its oversubscribed Fund V at US$320 million, taking its total assets under management past US$850 million.
Endeavor Catalyst invests exclusively in companies led by Endeavor Entrepreneurs, co-investing alongside leading venture capital and growth equity firms. Across its five funds, it has already backed 437 companies in 44 markets, deploying more than US$500 million across 469 investments.
Africa makes up seven per cent of both the portfolio and Catalyst capital, with 29 companies backed across five African markets, including the likes of Flutterwave, Moniepoint, MAX and Moove. Six of these are valued at US$1 billion or more. A decade ago, the fund had made no African investments.
Fund V has already backed 30 companies and deployed more than US$55 million, with a further US$25 million to US$30 million expected to be invested before the end of 2026.
“For the founders we have yet to welcome into the Endeavor community, it sends an important signal: world-class capital is looking for ambition, wherever that ambition is being built,” said Ireayo Oladunjoye, managing director and CEO of Endeavor Nigeria.

articles.title: Un motor de búsqueda alemán ha rechazado a Mistral apostando por modelos IA chinos open-source en su lugar
articles.text:
Cuando se creó Mistral, el objetivo era tener una alternativa europea a los gigantes estadounidenses y chinos de la IA. En este tiempo, ha ido levantando miles de millones de euros en diferentes rondas de financiación y están peleando para poder conseguir potencia de cálculo que los haga competir en las grandes ligas. Su CEO aprovechó la controversia política contra Estados Unidos para afirmar que Europa debía dejar de ser un vasallo tecnológico del país americano, y una de las armas para cuajar son los navegadores.
Meter la IA en el navegador es algo que están haciendo prácticamente todos, ya que es una forma de licenciar tecnología y conseguir usuarios más allá de las grandes empresas que pagan por usar la IA. De hecho, la conjunción entre navegadores europeos y Mistral parecía una buena forma de combatir a las propuestas estadounidenses, y precisamente por eso el encontronazo entre Ecosia y la empresa de IA francesa es tan sonado. Porque no es que ahora el navegador alemán vaya a volver a ChatGPT, sino que se va a ir a modelos chinos.
¿Motivos? Mejor calidad, según la entrevista al fundador de Ecosia publicada por Politico, pero de fondo también están asuntos políticos, energéticos y una contradicción que puede levantar más de una ceja.
Ecosia ataca a Mistral con todo
Hace unos días, el medio Politico publicó una entrevista a Christian Kroll, fundador y CEO de Ecosia, en la que anunció que el buscador con sede en Berlín dejará de usar Mistral como proveedor de IA. La empresa ya 'pasó' de ChatGPT a mediados de año para apostar por Mistral y, ahora, dejará el modelo francés en la cuneta.
Eso no implica que Ecosia deje de usar IA en el navegador, ya que Kroll apunta que irán en busca de modelos abiertos, citando Qwen, GLM y Kimi que "cuestan la mitad y nos dan más rendimiento" Lo que tienen en común es que son chinos, y es una decisión que llama la atención cuando uno de los pilares sobre los que se levantó Ecosia fue la independencia de tecnológicas no europeas.
Kroll da varios motivos por los que se ha tomado esta decisión que impactará en un navegador que está presente en instituciones públicas alemanas y británicas, por ejemplo. Son los siguientes:
- La calidad de Mistral es insuficiente, argumentando que sus modelos "van un año por detrás de la competencia".
- Mistral no es lo suficientemente potente, comentando que han tenido varios problemas técnicos como servidores saturados, achacándolo a que "Ecosia es un cliente demasiado grande para Mistral".
- Mistral no encaja con sus objetivos climáticos por el gran peso de la energía nuclear en el mix eléctrico francés.
- Mistral no es soberano debido a que depende de enormes inversores internacionales (Nvidia, por ejemplo, entre otros).
Son un montón de melones abiertos y desde Mistral no han respondido a Politico, pero el científico jefe de la empresa comentó en una rueda de prensa que animaba a Ecosia a probar su nuevo modelo, incluso con acceso anticipado para que puedan ver si la calidad ahora les satisface. De hecho, el mismo día de la entrevista, Mistral lanzó Large 4, un modelo que algunos analistas han posicionado como unos seis meses por detrás de los de frontera.
En una entrevista posterior en EU-Startups, Kroll intentó ser algo más comedido, argumentando que no se trata tanto de que los modelos chinos sean mejor que Mistral, sino de un cambio de foco a modelos abiertos. Es decir, no es una cuestión que tenga que ver con el país de origen, sino con la propia tecnología.
Apuntaba que quizá usarían Melious, una empresa alemana que ofrece acceso a más de 60 modelos abiertos a través de su API, que reparte consultas entre proveedores europeos y que está centrada en ofrecer el servicio apoyado por energía verde (algo que casa más con los compromisos ambientales de la propia Ecosia).
Pero usen lo que usen, la idea es apostar por esos modelos abiertos. En el caso de Ecosia, la jugada sería usar modelos desarrollados fuera, pero servidos desde infraestructura europea. Ahí es donde entra la mencionada Melious.
La contradicción china
Pero claro, si bien la calidad e infraestructura de Mistral es algo que sólo Ecosia sabe si le ha ido bien o mal, el tema energético y medioambiental es lo que puede hacer que levantemos una ceja en caso de que la compañía empiece a apostar por modelos chinos si no quieren apoyar un modelo francés que puede alimentarse de energía nuclear.
Según RTE, que es el gestor de la red eléctrica francesa, la nuclear aportó el 68,1% de la electricidad francesa en 2025 con una producción baja en carbono que alcanzó el 95,2%. Según las estimaciones, la electricidad francesa emite menos de 20 gramos de CO2 por kWh. Alemania, posicionada en contra de las nucleares y lastrada por el carbón, se sitúa en el rango de los 300 gramos de CO2 por kWh.
En la entrevista, Kroll alude a la nuclear como uno de los motivos para dejar de usar Mistral, pero sin especificar si es por seguridad de la planta, por gestión de residuos o por las emisiones directas.
Si nos vamos a China, aunque es cierto que el gigante asiático es una potencia verde, según la IAE, el 70% de la electricidad que alimentó sus centros de datos en 2025 venía del carbón. La idea es que las renovables cubran el 80% del consumo de esos centros de datos para 2030, pero la incómoda realidad actual es que, en todo el mundo, los picos de demanda de la inteligencia artificial están llevando al traste los compromisos climáticos de los países, volviendo a ese carbón o al gas.
Y luego está la contradicción por la calidad debido a la censura de los medios chinos. Si has jugueteado con alguno, sabrás que hay preguntas como qué ocurre en Taiwán o qué pasó en la plaza de Tiananmén a las que no te va a responder. Puedes dar rodeos, pero tardarás en dar con la respuesta (si es que lo consigues).
Es por ello que hay organizaciones occidentales que dudan de la calidad de los modelos chinos en algo como un buscador debido a esa censura, aunque hay algunos más optimistas como la de Rasmus Rothe, director de la Asociación Alemana de IA, que comentó a Politico que la censura puede eliminarse en gran parte reentrenando el modelo.
El problema es el sesgo de los datos de entrenamiento, algo mucho más difícil de corregir.

articles.title: AI could outperform 90% of coders in six months: Zoho's Sridhar Vembu
articles.text:
AI could outperform 90% of coders in six months: Zoho's Sridhar Vembu
At TechSparks 2026, Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu spoke about why software automation is not nessarily a crisis, urging the nation to focus on technological ownership, hardware foundations, and self-reliance over foreign IP dependency.
Rapid advances in AI software creation are driving an existential shift in the industry. With this, traditional coding is entering its “handloom” era, according to Sridhar Vembu, Co-founder and Chief Scientist of enterprise software firm Zoho.
Comparing software to a “handloom business,” Vembu said “powerful machine looms” are emerging, referring to automated systems generating complex computer scripts at high speed. Automated systems can already write functional code faster and more efficiently than many human developers, he added.
“AI already can write better code than at least 60-70% of software engineers out there. And in maybe three to six months, when things accelerate, AI can do better software than maybe 90% of software engineers,” Vembu said, speaking at the 17th edition of YourStory’s flagship tech-startup event, TechSparks.
Venture capitalists like Chamath Palihapitiya have suggested that intellectual property, the underlying proprietary ownership of written software code, is effectively dead, he added.
Despite the impending disruption to tech professionals, a huge part of India's population will remain largely unaffected, said Vembu, presenting a counter-intuitive macro perspective. He pointed out that roughly 97% of the broader population does not write software and operates as consumers of technology.
Outside major tech hubs such as Bengaluru, districts like Tenkasi in Tamil Nadu or Patna in Bihar will experience minimal direct economic upheaval if coding jobs disappear, said Vembu.
Furthermore, as software creation costs fall, automated efficiency could exert deflationary pressure across the broader economy. Lower production expenses mean non-technology workers, including teachers, nurses, and barbers, effectively gain increased real purchasing power as consumer goods become more affordable.
The technology ownership gap
The true obstacle to national prosperity is not the loss of outsourcing jobs, but a fundamental lack of technology ownership, according to Vembu.
Although Indian engineers write a vast portion of software for Microsoft and Cisco, and design up 40-50% of Nvidia's chip design work, the primary financial returns flow to foreign intellectual property holders, the entrepreneur pointed out.
To highlight this disparity, Vembu compared a Swiss school teacher, who can earn an iPhone in 3-4 days of work, with an Indian teacher who needs to put in months of work for the same item, despite neither being directly involved in technology.
“Ultimately, who has ownership of the technology determines what is the income level of the non-tech people in that economy. Not the income of tech people alone,” Vembu emphasised.
Reflecting on the 1990s, he argued that India was misled by Western commentary, such as Thomas Friedman’s writing celebrating IT services outsourcing, which rewarded labour over true technology ownership.
To achieve lasting economic independence, India must adopt the strategy of East Asian nations such as Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and China. Instead of rushing into top-level AI applications, China established durable national sovereignty by developing foundational domestic layers first, including search engines like Baidu and messaging ecosystems like WeChat.
Vembu cautioned against prioritising AI over essential industrial hardware and infrastructure, warning that a nation relying entirely on foreign hardware and foreign operating systems risks extreme geopolitical vulnerability.
“One reason I came to AI last is, we obsess about AI. We should not be obsessing about AI first. We should be obsessing about the more foundational layers,” he said.
True national resilience requires mastering core technologies such as lasers, x-rays, robotics, operating systems, and agricultural technology, according to him.
This philosophy guides Zoho's operational strategy amid rising infrastructure demands. The surge in AI adoption has caused server and graphics processing unit costs to explode, with server prices climbing from $8,000 to $45,000. Instead of executing corporate layoffs, Vembu said Zoho is redeploying its engineering talent towards deeptech hardware, including building server infrastructure in-house.
Highlighting this approach, Vembu noted, “As much as our jobs are challenged by the present generation of AI. You know why we don’t lay off anybody? We know we can redeploy them to build all this stuff.”
The emerging tech order, according to the entrepreneur, demands a shift from exporting software services to securing genuine national technological ownership.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Digitaler Ausweis auf dem Smartphone: Was Banken an d-you kritisieren
articles.text:
Digitaler Ausweis auf dem Smartphone: Was Banken an der d-you-Wallet kritisieren
Die staatliche Wallet „d-you“ soll im Januar 2027 starten. Nutzer können sich damit per Smartphone ausweisen, amtliche Dokumente speichern und elektronisch unterschreiben.
Grundlage dafür ist die EU-Verordnung eIDAS 2.0, die jeden Mitgliedstaat verpflichtet, seinen Bürgern eine solche Wallet anzubieten. Die Bundesregierung plant dazu entsprechende Regeln im Digitale Identitätengesetz (DIdG), über den Gesetzentwurf stimmt der Bundestag voraussichtlich am Donnerstag ab.
Die Deutsche Kreditwirtschaft (DK), als Interessenvertretung der Banken und Sparkassen, fordert nun Nachschärfungen im Gesetz. Zwar begrüßen die Banken, dass Kunden sich künftig per Wallet geldwäscherechtlich identifizieren können, wenn sie ein Konto eröffnen. Die Institute fordern jedoch, klar festzulegen, dass es ausreicht, die vom Wallet–Verfahren bereitgestellten Daten zu speichern, also dass eine Ausweiskopie weder erforderlich noch technisch umsetzbar ist. Ohne diese Präzisierung könnten Banken sonst vorsichtshalber zusätzliche Nachweise verlangen, wodurch der Vorteil einer schnellen, papierlosen Kontoeröffnung verloren gehen könnte.
Außerdem müsse das Gesetz klarer regeln, wann Banken eine fremde Wallet akzeptieren müssen, wer bei technischen Fehlern haftet und welche Daten ihnen zur Betrugsabwehr zur Verfügung stehen.
Authentifizierung und Autorisierung
Den Banken geht es dabei unter anderem um die Trennung von Authentifizierung (als Sicherheitsabfrage) und Autorisierung, also die Freigabe von Zahlungen.
Grundsätzlich sind sie offen dafür, die Wallet beim Onlinebanking und beim Bezahlen als Sicherheitsabfrage zu akzeptieren, ähnlich wie heute eine TAN-App, allerdings nur dort, wo eine solche Prüfung ohnehin vorgeschrieben ist. Die Banken befürchten, das Gesetz könne sie zur Akzeptanz verpflichten, ohne dass sie die nötigen technischen Nachweise und eine eindeutige Haftungsregelung bekommen. Die DK fordert deshalb eine Klarstellung im Gesetz.
Keine Annahmepflicht
Grundsätzlich unterstützt die Bank die Idee, die Wallet auch für Zahlungen nutzbar zu machen. Eine Verpflichtung der Banken, Zahlungen direkt über die Wallet anzubieten, lehnen sie aber ab.
Jedes Institut soll selbst entscheiden dürfen, mit welchem Verfahren Kunden ihre Zahlungen freigeben. Auch eine pauschale Annahmepflicht im stationären Zahlungsverkehr sehen die Banken kritisch. Kartenzahlungen, Girocard und Bargeldabhebungen dürften nicht durch die Hintertür an die Wallet gekoppelt werden. Bestehende Systeme umzubauen, wäre aus Sicht der Banken technisch, rechtlich und wirtschaftlich sehr aufwendig.
Kunden sollen ihre Bankkarte künftig in die Wallet laden können, ähnlich wie heute bei Apple Pay oder Google Pay. Ob eine Bank das anbietet, soll aber ebenfalls ihre freie Entscheidung bleiben. Die DK wünscht sich auch hier eine eindeutige Formulierung im Gesetz. Außerdem soll eine Einbindung nur mit einem Vertrag zwischen Wallet-Anbieter und Bank zulässig sein.
Neben der staatlichen Wallet können auch Unternehmen künftig eigene Wallets anbieten. Laut Entwurf entscheidet darüber aber das Digitalministerium, und zwar mit der Möglichkeit, seine Entscheidung später zu ändern. Für Investoren ergebe sich daraus Planungs- und Investitionsrisiken, warnen die Banken. Sie fordern daher, private Wallets direkt im Gesetz zu erlauben, bestehende Angebote zu schützen und einen klaren Zeitplan festzulegen.
Streitpunkt Haftung
Eine weitere offene Frage berührt die Haftung in Betrugsfällen oder bei technischen Pannen. Zahlungsdienstleister wollen nicht für Fehler einer Wallet haften, die sie nicht selbst bereitgestellt haben oder kontrollieren können.
Die Banken fordern deshalb: Wird eine Wallet zur starken Kundenauthentifizierung genutzt, soll der Wallet-Anbieter nachweisen müssen, dass die Authentifizierung ordnungsgemäß lief, korrekt protokolliert wurde und nicht durch einen Fehler der Wallet beeinträchtigt war.
Außerdem wollen die Banken ein gesetzliches Recht auf die Informationen, die sie zur Prüfung von Erstattungs-, Haftungs- und Betrugsfällen benötigen. Dazu zählen standardisierte Protokolle, Transaktionsdaten, Angaben zum Wallet-Anbieter und Risikosignale. Bei bekannten Sicherheitslücken oder Zertifizierungsproblemen wollen sie außerdem das Recht haben, eine Wallet abzulehnen oder vorübergehend sperren zu dürfen.
Bedenken zur EUID-Wallet hatten zuletzt auch Sachverständige in einer Anhörung des Digitalausschuss angemeldet. Anfang Oktober bemängelten Daten- und Verbraucherschützer etwa, dass sich die Wallet zum Start nicht pseudonym nutzen lässt. Anbieter könnten mehr Daten abfragen als nötig und aus den Daten Profile bilden.
Die IT-Sicherheitsforscherin Jiska Classen von der Universität Potsdam kritisierte, große Teile der Sicherheitsarchitektur seien noch nicht öffentlich und nicht bewertet. Smartphones blieben ein hohes Risiko, weil viele Geräte keine Sicherheitsupdates mehr erhielten. Über ein kompromittiertes Handy könnten sich unbefugte Nutzer im Namen eines anderen ausweisen, Hotels buchen oder Kredite aufnehmen. Auch sie forderte daher eine eindeutige Haftungsregelung im Gesetz.

articles.title: Apple lance de nouveaux Apple TV et HomePod mini : voici les nouveautés
articles.text:
L’Apple TV n’avait pas évolué depuis 2022, le HomePod mini depuis 2020. La bonne nouvelle est que l’attente est enfin terminée pour les fans de ces produits : Apple a dévoilé le 13 octobre de nouvelles versions de son boîtier télé et de son enceinte connectée (mais oublie toujours le grand HomePod). La marque a profité de sa conférence « Welcome Home » dédiée à la maison connectée pour dévoiler les nouvelles versions de ces produits avec plusieurs nouveautés. La star du jour est évidemment l’écran HomeView, mais on peut imaginer que les Apple TV et HomePod mini sauront vite trouver leurs publics.
Apple met ENFIN à jour son Apple TV
« Enfin » n’est pas un euphémisme : la dernière Apple TV 4K date d’octobre 2022 et les fans du produit attendent avec impatience une nouvelle génération. Nous recevons souvent des messages de nos lecteurs sur Numerama et une part conséquente d’entre eux concerne des renseignements sur la future Apple TV. Le dilemme est souvent le même : les gens ont des téléviseurs à équiper mais ne veulent pas acheter un vieux modèle alors que les rumeurs annoncent une nouvelle génération depuis deux ans. Et comme le marché des box télé est relativement faible (le Nvidia Shield TV date de 2019 et le Google TV Streamer n’est pas un foudre de guerre), alors l’Apple TV est considérée par beaucoup comme le seul produit du marché.
Le 13 octobre 2026 est le jour de la libération : Apple annonce qu’une nouvelle Apple TV sera disponible le 13 novembre 2026, au prix de 349 € (modèle unique). L’Apple TV passe à la puce A19, celle de l’iPhone 17, ce qui la rend sur le papier plus puissante qu’un MacBook Neo (l’ancien modèle avait l’A15). Apple promet un processeur jusqu’à 50 % plus rapide et des performances graphiques jusqu’à deux fois supérieures, ainsi qu’un décodeur AV1 dédié pour un streaming de meilleure qualité avec moins de bande passante. Cette montée en puissance devrait améliorer la réactivité du boîtier, les graphismes des jeux et permettre de traiter une partie des requêtes Siri directement sur l’appareil.
Aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni ou au Canada, l’Apple TV offre des fonctionnalités Siri AI (en anglais et en version bêta), mais pas en France, alors que le produit n’est pas régulé par le DMA européen. La raison : Siri AI exige que le propriétaire du domicile dans l’application Maison ait un iPhone avec Siri AI, ce qui est impossible en Europe. On pourra quand même demander un programme qui pourrait nous plaire, comme c’est déjà le cas aujourd’hui.
L’Apple TV est aussi accompagnée d’une nouvelle télécommande sans grand chamboulement esthétique, mais enfin compatible avec Localiser : on pourra la faire sonner pour la retrouver entre deux coussins. Elle ne sera plus obligatoire pour le pilotage à la voix, l’Apple TV étant équipée de trois microphones à longue portée. Notons enfin qu’on pourra coupler l’Apple TV à quatre HomePod mini 2 ou HomePod de deuxième génération (par paires identiques à l’avant et à l’arrière) pour une vraie expérience sonore digne d’un home cinéma.
Le HomePod mini 2 adopte une puce plus puissante
L’autre nouveauté est encore plus discrète : six ans après le premier modèle, le HomePod mini a enfin un successeur. Il s’appelle le HomePod mini 2 et, à l’instar de l’Apple TV, sera privé de Siri AI en France (aux États-Unis, l’assistant n’arrivera que dans une future mise à jour). Siri sera toujours là pour quelques commandes vocales (exemple : lancer un minuteur) ou gérer sa domotique. Le HomePod mini adopte la puce S10 de l’Apple Watch Series 10, ce qui est une évolution notable depuis la puce S5 de la première génération. Pour l’écoute musicale, elle analyse les morceaux en temps réel pour optimiser la dynamique et le volume.
Apple mise sur de nouveaux coloris pour séduire : blanc, rose, bleu, vert et minuit.
Le HomePod mini 2 sera disponible le 30 octobre, au prix de 169 €.

articles.title: Ivanti warns of Connect Secure zero-day exploited in attacks
articles.text:
Ivanti urged customers on Tuesday to immediately patch an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability in the Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway.
Formerly known as Pulse Connect Secure and originally Juniper Pulse, the enterprise-grade ICS SSL VPN provides remote employees, contractors, and hybrid workforces with secure access to corporate and cloud resources.
Tracked as CVE-2026-104935, this high-severity authentication bypass zero-day affects ICS versions 22.8R2.4 and earlier, 25.1.2.2 and earlier, and 25.1.1.1 and earlier.
Remote threat actors without privileges can exploit CVE-2026-104935 in low-complexity attacks that don't require user interaction to execute arbitrary commands on targeted ICS appliances.
"At the time of disclosure, Ivanti is aware of limited exploitation in the wild. We are working directly with those organizations while making information, updates and remediation available to the broader customer community. If you are running one of the impacted versions, Ivanti recommends you act immediately," Ivanti said.
"Customers should review the security advisory, upgrade to the fixed version as soon as possible, and run the Integrity Checker Tool regularly."
Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver now tracks over 5,500 ICS instances exposed online, but there is no information on how many are honeypots or have already been secured against ongoing attacks.
Exploited since at least October 3
Cybersecurity firm Volexity, which found and reported the flaw, revealed earlier today that a previously unknown threat actor it tracks as UTA0576 has chained the CVE-2026-104935 vulnerability since at least October 3 with two other flaws to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution on fully patched devices.
"Notably, UTA0576 deployed no malware or web shell. Instead, the threat actor re-exploited the device for every command it ran and tampered with logs to cover its tracks, evading Ivanti’s Integrity Checker Tool," Volexity said.
While Ivanti has patched two flaws, it is still working to address a privilege escalation vulnerability that UTA0576 exploited as part of the same chain.
Threat intelligence company Defused also confirmed Volexity's report, saying that it caught the first signs of CVE-2026-104935 exploitation in the wild starting October 1.
Hackers have frequently exploited Ivanti vulnerabilities, often as zero-days, because they provide a quick way to breach enterprise networks and steal sensitive customer and corporate data.
Ivanti has also patched several other Connect Secure zero-days exploited in the wild over the past several years, some of them chained in widespread attacks to deploy malware.
It addressed an authentication bypass (CVE-2023-46805) and a command injection (CVE-2024-21887) in early January 2024, and a server-side request forgery (CVE-2024-21893) two weeks later.
More recently, it fixed a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability tracked as CVE-2025-0282 in January 2025 and a second RCE flaw (CVE-2025-22457) that China-linked cyber spies have exploited since at least mid-March 2025.
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has flagged 36 vulnerabilities across various Ivanti products as actively exploited in the wild since November 2021, 12 of which ransomware gangs have also abused.
Ivanti has over 3,000 employees, a network of over 7,000 partners, and more than 40,000 customers worldwide using its IT asset management solutions.

Nouveautés Canal+ : les films et séries à ne pas manquer en octobre 2026
Abonnés à Canal+ et en quête de nouveautés ? Ça tombe bien, la chaîne cryptée revient au mois d'octobre 2026 avec des films, séries et documentaires alléchants ajoutés à son catalogue.
Quelques jours à la suite de Netflix, HBO Max et Disney+, c'est au tour de Canal+ de dévoiler les nouveaux programmes rejoignant sa plateforme de streaming et son catalogue au mois d'octobre 2026.
Une fois de plus, la chaîne cryptée française peut compter sur les contenus de ses services complémentaires Paramount+, Apple TV et Ciné+ OCS (disponibles dans son offre Ciné Séries), mais a aussi de belles cartouches "maison" comme les films Marsupilami et Hamnet, ainsi que la série Spinners.
Découvrez ci-dessous la liste des nouveautés principales de Canal+ en octobre 2026, juste après notre sélection du film et de la série du mois sur le service de streaming.
La série du mois sur Canal+
Tulsa King - Saison 4
Dwight se bat pour légitimer son empire et protéger son équipe alors que des politiciens corrompus, de nouveaux ennemis dangereux et une perte personnelle dévastatrice l’assaillent de toutes parts. Chaque décision enfonce Dwight un peu plus dans les instincts de la rue qu’il avait laissés derrière lui à New York – transformant Tulsa en champ de bataille et Dwight en une menace que personne ne peut se permettre de sous-estimer.
La populaire série de mafia de Taylor Sheridan (Yellowstone, Landman) revient pour une quatrième saison, plus musclée et nerveuse que jamais. Un nouveau chapitre qui garde les mêmes ingrédients et la même recette, et qui ravira sans aucun doute les fans du genre, et de Sylvester Stallone, toujours aussi impressionnant et indéboulonnable du haut de ses 80 ans.
À partir du 16 octobre sur Paramount+, disponible dans l'offre Ciné Séries de Canal+.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Le film du mois sur Canal+
Hamnet
Angleterre, 1580. Un professeur de latin fauché fait la connaissance d’Agnes, jeune femme à l’esprit libre. Fascinés l’un par l’autre, ils entament une liaison fougueuse avant de se marier et d’avoir trois enfants. Tandis que Will tente sa chance comme dramaturge à Londres, Agnes assume seule les tâches domestiques. Lorsqu’un drame se produit, le couple, autrefois profondément uni, vacille. Mais c’est de leur épreuve commune que naîtra l’inspiration d’un chef d’œuvre universel.
La réalisatrice Chloé Zhao, oscarisée pour Nomadland, adapte le roman éponyme de Maggie O'Farrell avec sa sensibilité et sa poésie caractéristiques. À travers l'histoire fictive d'Agnes et William Shakespeare, Hamnet dessine toutes les couleurs de l'amour et du deuil et livre un film bouleversant, portée par une immense Jessie Buckley, lauréate de l'Oscar de la meilleure actrice, et un toujours excellent Paul Mescal.
Disponible le 6 octobre sur Canal+.

articles.title: Meta dégaine Muse Wonder et revient en force dans la course à l'IA
articles.text:
Meta veut jouer dans la cour des grands. Ce lundi 12 octobre, le groupe américain a levé le voile sur Muse Wonder et Muse Wonder Full, ses « modèles les plus performants à ce jour ». Selon Meta, ces nouvelles IA rivalisent avec les meilleurs modèles d’OpenAI et d’Anthropic. Pour Mark Zuckerberg, Muse Wonder est « une catégorie de modèles bien plus grande et plus avancée, qui nous amène à la pointe » de la technologie. Le patron de Meta assure même que ses équipes travaillent « déjà à l’étape suivante »,
 Introducing Muse Wonder, our new family of frontier models with state of the art performance for personal and professional agentic work. https://t.co/NKHrybrGKQ
— Mark Zuckerberg (@finkd) October 12, 2026
Muse Wonder, le fruit de la réorganisation de Meta
De l’aveu du milliardaire, il a fallu « une grande quantité de puissance de calcul et d’investissements, ainsi qu’un travail scientifique très rigoureux », pour mettre au point les modèles Muse. Dans un communiqué de presse, Meta rappelle que sa division IA sort d’une vaste réorganisation interne. Le géant a notamment mis sur pied une équipe chargée de développer des produits d’intelligence artificielle très avancés, le Meta Superintelligence Labs, avant de licencier 600 employés de son ancienne division dédiée à la recherche fondamentale sur l’IA. En parallèle, Meta a embauché une armée de chercheurs spécialisés dans l’IA dans toute la Silicon Valley.
« Il y a quatorze mois, nous avons entamé une refonte de nos efforts en IA, et nous sommes passés de la reconstruction de nos fondations à la conquête de la frontière », résume Meta, soulignant que Muse est le résultat de ces efforts de réorganisation.
À lire aussi : « Pas assez prudents » : un responsable OpenAI claque la porte et descend l’approche des rois de l’IA
Meta à l’assaut d’OpenAI et d’Anthropic
Muse Wonder est taillé pour fonctionner avec des agents, c’est-à-dire des IA capables d’accomplir des tâches à votre place. Deux fonctions sont particulièrement mises en avant par Meta. Baptisée Active Memory, la première fonction permet à l’IA de retenir ce qui compte pour vous d’une conversation à l’autre. La seconde, intitulée Active Focus, permet à l’IA de garder le cap quand une tâche se complique. En cas de difficultés, l’IA change d’approche, corrige ses erreurs et vous demande des précisions si nécessaire. L’objectif de Meta est d’éviter qu’un agent ne se perde en route lors d’une recherche complexe ou d’un projet de grande envergure.
D’après les tests réalisés par Meta, Muse Wonder Full dépasse Claude Fable 5.1 d’Anthropic et se classe juste derrière Claude Opus 5.5 sur l’indice Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, qui résume les capacités d’un modèle d’IA. Il devance aussi GPT-6 Astra d’OpenAI dans certains domaines bien précis, notamment en droit et en développement de logiciels. Par contre, Muse Wonder pèche par un coût d’utilisation bien supérieur à la concurrence, ce qui représente un frein sur un marché de plus en plus axé sur les IA abordables.
À lire aussi : Gemini 4 Argon s’attaque à ChatGPT et Claude : Google dévoile son IA la plus puissante
Meta affirme avoir pris des précautions pour éviter les dérives. L’entreprise de Menlo Park indique avoir entraîné ses modèles à ne pas divulguer d’informations privées sans autorisation, à refuser les demandes nuisibles et à mieux résister aux cyberattaques. Le groupe veut aussi permettre aux développeurs de se servir de Muse Wonder pour débusquer des failles dans leur code. Ces derniers mois, plusieurs incidents impliquant des agents IA ont fait les gros titres. Meta AI a également dérapé en piratant une entreprise en toute autonomie. C’est pourquoi Meta a mis l’accent sur les gardes fous de ses nouveaux modèles.
Le retour en force de Meta
Avec Muse Wonder, Meta signe un retour très attendu sur le devant de la scène de l’IA. Pionnier des modèles ouverts avec Llama, le groupe a par la suite accumulé du retard face à OpenAI, Anthropic et Google. Pour rattraper son retard, le géant des réseaux sociaux a confié les rênes de ses IA à Alexandr Wang, fondateur de Scale AI. L’homme a pris la tête du Superintelligence Labs en décembre dernier, dans le sillage du départ de Yann LeCun. Le pari de Meta est évidemment colossal. Meta prévoit jusqu’à 145 milliards de dollars d’investissements cette année, principalement dans l’IA. Sans surprise, Meta espère que les abonnements à Muse, dont le lancement est une réussite en dépit de plusieurs incidents de sécurité, pourront lui offrir une nouvelle source de revenus et réduire sa dépendance à la publicité en ligne.
