articles.title: Vienna-based reebuild raises €3 million to build the AI operating system for construction and real estate | EU-Startups
articles.text:
reebuild, the Vienna-based AI-native back-office automation platform for construction and real estate, has raised a €3 million Seed round.
The round was led by Fortino Ventures, a Ghent-based VC firm backing B2B AI and software companies across Europe from its third-generation VC fund. Other investors in the round include Rise PropTech and CuriosityVC, and existing backer Hansmann Family Office also participated.
“We know the problems of this industry firsthand, and we build reebuild together with our customers, extremely close to the day-to-day reality on site. The software many construction companies and developers still work with today has barely evolved in decades and has fallen behind rising expectations. We’re convinced that we can shake up this market with a team that combines deep construction and technology know-how. Not with another tool, but with a solution that truly understands how construction sites and projects are handled on the commercial side,” said Alexander Kornell, CEO and founder of reebuild.
Founded in 2022 by Alexander Kornell (CEO), Matteo Cimadom (CRO) and Luca Papay (CTO) joined as co-founders, reebuild operates as a vertical AI platform that reads every incoming document line by line, whether a PDF, photo, scan, or e-invoice, and converts it into structured data and automates invoice review, cost management, and material tracking.
On its platform, delivery notes, invoices, and order confirmations are matched automatically, and the software progressively learns from the decisions of commercial managers, reducing repetitive administrative workload over time. On site, a foreman can photograph a delivery note with the mobile app and have it instantly embedded in the system.
With cost administration between departments still largely managed in spreadsheets and paper folders, invoices matched by hand, approvals lacking transparency and early-payment discounts routinely unclaimed, reebuild wants to fix this gap with AI agents preparing work, flagging repetitive tasks and recommending next actions, while keeping human teams in charge of final approvals.
The company says its platform has processed more than €530 million in invoice volume across over 120 construction companies and property developers, spanning more than 8,200 construction sites and projects. It has automatically handled more than 345k documents, counts more than 2,350 active users across its customer base, and includes Pittel+Brausewetter, 3SI Immogroup, Rödl & Herdegen, and Kratzert Gruppe. It also reports that invoice handling time has been cut from over 20 minutes to approximately three minutes, while customers have indicated a reduction in procurement costs by up to 20%.
“We believe now is the time for construction companies to digitise and automate their back-office processes with SaaS and AI. reebuild is the right team to execute on this, with the founding team having their family roots in the construction sector,” said Wouter Goossens, Partner at Fortino Ventures.
The funding will be deployed across three areas: geographic expansion beyond reebuild’s established markets in Austria and Germany, the development of new AI-native modules that fully automate contractors’ workflows from calculation to accounting; and team growth at its Vienna headquarters, where the company currently employs around 25 people.
For reebuild, AI-native modules are the first step, but the company intends to become the agentic back office for the construction industry, where AI agents independently handle routine tasks such as invoicing, on-site documentation, and project estimation, covering a contractor’s entire commercial workflow from calculation to accounting.

articles.title: ¿Cuánta IA hay en los libros más vendidos? Mucha en novelas románticas de Amazon y en el superventas de Alvise Pérez
articles.text:
¿Cuánta IA hay en los libros más vendidos? Mucha en novelas románticas de Amazon y en el superventas de Alvise Pérez
EL PAÍS ha analizado 175 libros populares con el detector Pangram. En 2019 no hay ni rastro, pero ahora uno de cada tres superventas autopublicados está escrito en su mayor parte con inteligencia artificial
La inteligencia artificial llega también al mundo de los libros. EL PAÍS ha comprobado el uso de IA en una muestra concreta de 119 libros populares de 2025 y 2026: hemos analizado los volúmenes aparecidos en las listas de superventas en Amazon y la Casa del Libro, y en los ganadores de un gran premio literario.
Todos los libros con un uso mayoritario de IA que ha encontrado este periódico han sido autopublicados, muchos de ellos en la categoría de novelas románticas. Son libros con numerosos lectores: tienen entre 270 y 2.000 valoraciones en Amazon.
El caso más visible es Devuélveme mi país, del político Alvise Pérez. En febrero de 2026 fue número 1 en Amazon. Pangram clasifica como generado por IA el 97% de todo el libro; ese porcentaje es la parte del libro que atribuye a una máquina. Es decir, que casi todo el texto saldría de un programa como ChatGPT o similares y solo un 3% sería solo humano, según la herramienta, que no dice quién usó la IA ni cómo lo hizo. No aclara si le pidieron el texto completo o si le dio sus notas o ideas para que las ampliara. Pasada la medianoche, Pérez respondió con un email, que publicó en redes, supuestamente redactado por su IA, en el que asegura que escribió su libro “palabra a palabra”.
Los demás libros con un uso mayoritario de IA son novelas, casi todas románticas. Pangram atribuye a una máquina el 100% del texto de Mr. Sterling. Romance con el CEO, del autor con seudónimo Violeta Dark; el 86% de Mi jefe es el Anticristo (versión sexy), de Estrella Correa; el 75% de El asesino del mapa, de Pablo Poveda, y el 53% de Novia del CEO por Navidad, del seudónimo Leila Yoon. EL PAÍS ha mandado mensajes a las páginas de contacto, correos y cuentas en redes sociales de estos autores. Nadie ha respondido.
De cada libro hemos analizado con la herramienta de detección Pangram tres fragmentos de 1.000 palabras, equivalente a unas 10 páginas. Además, analizamos el texto completo de 12 de los libros con más IA (incluidos todos los citados en este artículo). Este ejercicio lo repetimos con 56 libros publicados en 2019 y 2020, cuando no existían los modelos de IA actuales. Ninguno de los libros de 2019-20 tiene trazas de IA: dan todos 0%. ¿Resultados en 2025 y 2026? De los 119 analizados, 35 tienen algo de IA (29%) y 13 pasan del 50%.
Autopublicados sí, grandes nombres no
El uso de IA se concentra en las obras autopublicadas: son 13 de 44, el 30%. La novela romántica domina porque es también lo que más abunda entre los superventas de Amazon.
Los escritores asentados no dan positivo, y las editoriales tradicionales tienen métodos de control, según fuentes del sector. Nadie ha confirmado el uso de Pangram, pero sí que tienen en cuenta la IA: “Nuestra regla es que todo debe empezar con un humano y acabar con un humano. Y a partir de ahí aspiramos a una conversación transparente con autores y lectores”, dice Miguel Aguilar, editor de Penguin Random House.
El detector no encuentra IA en los libros de los autores más conocidos. Dan un 0% los últimos de Javier Cercas, Antonio Muñoz Molina, Isabel Allende, María Dueñas o Dolores Redondo, y también los ganadores del Planeta o el Nadal. Lo mismo ocurre con otros libros de política muy vendidos, como los de Iván Espinosa de los Monteros o el juez Manuel Marchena.
Aun así, hay 9 libros de editorial que tienen alguna traza. Eso incluye cuatro obras de no ficción con entre el 12% y el 34% de IA, todas populares y de autores conocidos.
Pangram no es infalible. En fragmentos cortos, a veces basta tocar una palabra para que cambie de criterio. Para nuestras pruebas hicimos dos controles. En el primero, analizamos esos 56 libros de 2019 y 2020: no marcó ninguno de los 168 fragmentos. En el segundo control, generamos 29 textos con IA que imitaban el estilo de libros reales: Pangram los detectó todos.
Muchos libros tienen algo de IA en capítulos puntuales. La IA no se reparte igual dentro de cada libro: hay capítulos casi enteros generados junto a otros sin rastro. Pero aunque ese uso masivo de la IA se da por ahora sobre todo en autores autopublicados en géneros concretos, el uso discreto y controlado tiene pinta de ir a más. Entre los libros de no ficción de editorial, ninguno de los 16 analizados de 2019-20 daba señal; en 2025-26 la dan 7 de 22. Hay influencers que escriben libros y parecen dejar a la IA las explicaciones más obvias. Es un poco el uso que se le podía dar a la Wikipedia o el Rincón del vago en el pasado: un recurso para los fragmentos más obvios.
Ninguna de estas acciones es ilegal ni un delito. Las editoriales suelen tener ya cláusulas sobre IA en algunos de sus contratos, pero la IA solo será un problema central si los lectores le dan importancia y deciden no comprar ningún libro escrito con IA. El debate sobre la autoría con IA de un libro ha estallado en 2026 en distintos países, sobre todo gracias a la mejoría de Pangram y al increíble éxito de una primera novela en francés de un poco conocido autor canadiense, Thélyson Orélien. Este mismo lunes se ha sabido que el ganador del premio Caine de escritura africana, valorado en 11.800 euros, estaba probablemente escrito con IA. Es difícil saber ahora si en unos años, con la IA haciendo de todo en muchos ámbitos, el público se habrá adaptado.
De momento es un asunto polémico, que los escritores afrontan con vehemencia. “Yo he escrito más de una docena de novelas sin usar la IA y me ha ido bastante bien, así que, obviamente, jamás usaría la IA para escribir una”, dice Marcos Nieto Pallarés, autor de una de las novelas analizadas por este periódico y que ha dado 0% de IA. “Sí he notado una bajada en las ventas en lo que respecta a la autopublicación. Pero viendo una portada en una lista es difícil saber si se ha escrito con IA, así que no sé hasta qué punto las novelas escritas con IA han invadido Amazon”, añade.
109 libros en año y medio
Amazon pide que se identifique el contenido generado con IA, pero no está prohibido. El contenido hecho con IA lo es aunque luego se haya editado: “Se considera ‘generado por IA’, aunque después hayas aplicado ediciones sustanciales”, dicen las directrices de contenido de la plataforma. “Nuestras directrices de contenido determinan qué libros pueden publicarse para su venta, y adoptamos medidas tanto proactivas como reactivas para prevenir, detectar y eliminar contenido que incumpla esas directrices, ya sea generado por inteligencia artificial o no”, dice un portavoz de Amazon, sin dar más detalles sobre cómo lo hacen.
“No tengo pruebas” de que hay más IA en libros autopublicados, dice Yanira García Fernández, autora de otra de las novelas analizadas y que ha dado 0% de IA. “Aunque sí creo que no hay ningún tipo de control. La editorial tradicional hace una criba y Amazon no hace ese trabajo previo, cualquier persona es capaz de crearse una cuenta, subir su libro y listo, por eso es más sencillo publicar cualquier cosa porque es tan sencillo como darle a un botón y dejar que el lector sea el que escoja”, añade.
Violeta Dark ha publicado 109 libros en cinco idiomas en Amazon desde el 1 de marzo de 2025, al menos 21 en español. Mr Sterling. Romance con el CEO de enemigos a amantes salió en agosto de 2025 y es el que más reseñas ha recibido. Es también el primero de una serie llamada Los Mr. irresistibles. En octubre de 2026 sigue siendo el número 3 en ficción contemporánea de Amazon. Así se describe Dark en su página web: “Violeta Dark crea historias de amor intensas y apasionantes donde mujeres fuertes encuentran un amor que desafía todos los obstáculos. Sus novelas combinan romance, suspense y emoción, garantizando siempre ese final feliz por el que merece la pena luchar”.
Los lectores también empiezan a usar la IA como un motivo de queja en los comentarios de Amazon: “Nada recomendable, empieza bien pero da unos giros que no tienen coherencia ninguna, parece escrito por IA. Ya había leído algo de esta autora y no estaba mal”, dice una lectora del libro de Estrella Correa. O sobre el libro de Alvise Pérez, escribe un usuario de la plataforma: “Parece escrito por una IA. Aunque su mensaje es directo y a veces repetitivo, hay momentos en los que todo suena demasiado igual, casi como si hubiera sido escrito de forma automática y sin demasiados matices”.
Quizás es solo el principio
Un artículo científico de agosto analizó una muestra de 14.419 libros electrónicos autopublicados en Amazon. Los autores consideraban más del 25% como un uso sustancial de IA, y les salió que lo superaba 1 de cada 5 libros. Entre los superventas autopublicados que ha analizado EL PAÍS en España, la proporción se eleva: 39%. No es un espacio predominante, pero es obvio que estamos al principio de una nueva era.
Pangram usa un método propio para detectar texto generado. Pero hay signos habituales que se han convertido en pequeños trucos para saber si hay IA en unas páginas: contrastes negativos tipo “no es X ni Y sino Z”, enumeraciones de tres elementos, paralelismos, dos puntos y guiones, resúmenes aforísticos o ritmo de frases uniformes. “Sus palabras me atraviesan como un cuchillo. Precisa. Directa. Implacable”, escribe Violeta Dark al principio de su libro. “No hablo de un pasado idealizado ni de una postal nostálgica, sino de una certeza íntima compartida: trabajabas, te esforzabas, cumplías con tu parte”, es la segunda frase del libro de Alvise Pérez. “Éramos una nación dueña de su destino”, es la última frase del primer párrafo.
Este análisis señala un cambio: en 2019 no había rastro de IA en los libros más populares y ahora empiezan a observarse señales. Además, hay que entender qué detectan estos sistemas: reconocen que un texto ha sido generado con IA (porque sigue ciertos patrones), pero eso no dice exactamente qué rol tuvo una persona en el proceso. Se puede usar IA para una escritura muy perezosa, casi automática, pero también para convertir en palabras pensamientos propios o dictados. Los grises abundan. Lo que viene es un debate. Que tampoco será por completo nuevo. Las memorias de Andre Agassi las escribió el periodista J. R. Moehringer después de 250 horas de conversación con el tenista. ¿Quién es el autor? En la portada solo figura Agassi, aunque quizás no escribió una palabra.
Metodología. La prueba se ha hecho con una suscripción a la versión 4 de Pangram, uno de los detectores mejor valorados por la comunidad científica.
Para escoger los libros, partimos de las listas de más vendidos de Amazon.es (top 50 en Libros y en Kindle) y de Casa del Libro (top 10 de ficción y de no ficción). No las revisamos a diario: usamos una captura de cada lista por mes, guardada en Internet Archive, entre enero de 2025 y septiembre de 2026. Es, por tanto, una muestra de los libros populares, no un censo. A esa lista añadimos los ganadores de 13 premios literarios. De esa lista hemos analizado todos los libros que teníamos disponibles (119, aproximadamente la mitad). Ningún libro se eligió ni se descartó por su autor o por su contenido. Son todos libros para adultos, escritos originalmente en español y publicados en 2025 o 2026.
De cada libro hemos escogido al azar tres fragmentos de 1.000 palabras para pasarlos al software Pangram. Luego, para 12 libros con señales de haber usado IA, hemos analizado el libro entero.
Para el grupo de control, analizamos con el mismo procedimiento una muestra similar de libros de 2019 y 2020, cuando no existían los actuales modelos de inteligencia artificial. Ese primer control tiene una objeción potencial: quizás Pangram dé por humanos los libros de 2019-2020 no porque sepa distinguirlos, sino porque ya los conoce y estaban en los textos con los que aprendió. No se puede descartar. Pero hay dos motivos para pensar que no es eso. El primero sale de nuestro análisis: los libros de editorial y premiados de 2025 y 2026 tampoco dan positivo. El segundo es de la propia empresa. Su CEO, Max Spero, explicó en el pódcast Mixed Signals que midieron sus falsos positivos con millones de textos anteriores a 2022 “que sabemos que no están generados por IA, pero que tampoco están en nuestro conjunto de entrenamiento”. Según sus números, Pangram solo marca como IA uno de cada 24.000 textos humanos.
También hicimos la prueba contraria. Generamos textos imitando el estilo de autores reales con cuatro modelos de IA, para luego analizarlos con Pangram. El software los marcó a todos como artificiales.

articles.title: All Systems Go: Global PC App Ecosystem Ready for NVIDIA RTX Spark
articles.text:
NVIDIA RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — a reinvention combining the capabilities of a gaming PC, a creative studio and a personal AI supercomputer into a single superchip. With up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute, RTX Spark delivers the full stack of NVIDIA RTX and CUDA technologies for creators, developers and gamers, while unlocking a new paradigm in personal computing via powerful local AI agents.
Last week, NVIDIA and Microsoft announced that RTX Spark laptops will be available on Friday, Oct. 16. Ahead of the launch, NVIDIA and its ecosystem partners are rolling out new software features and performance optimizations to expand what’s possible with local AI on RTX Spark.
New and upcoming RTX Spark updates — among the thousands of apps, games and models available at launch — include:
- New agent features, models and tools that enhance local agents on RTX Spark: 
  - Updates to top agent apps including GitHub Copilot, Hermes, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy streamline setup on RTX Spark, improve security with OpenShell and Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), and enable hybrid local and cloud AI routing.
  - The NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B model, purpose-built for agentic AI on RTX Spark, releases on Thursday, Oct. 15.
  - NVIDIA PAIR moves out of beta and adds llama.cpp support.
- Top creative apps optimized for RTX Spark:
  - Up to 2x performance is coming soon to Adobe’s top apps. NVIDIA and Adobe have collaborated to rearchitect Photoshop for GPU-accelerated compositing and Premiere for playback, rendering, effects and more.
  - The NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 release brings new Video Super Resolution, Video Frame Generation, offline file processing and agent Model Context Protocol (MCP) controls to the app.
  - NVIDIA RTX Video Frame Generation and high dynamic range (HDR) capabilities are available now in ComfyUI to accelerate AI generative video workflows.
  - NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction will be available in Blender 5.3 in November to improve interactivity in the viewport.
- Developer tools are now ready for RTX Spark:
  - Top developer frameworks are now available for RTX Spark, including PyTorch, Python and CUDA, as well as all CUDA libraries.
  - GitHub Copilot, Pi and other coding agents are now optimized for RTX Spark.
  - Llama.cpp adds support for decision models, and releases a Windows app.
- Hundreds of top games and anti-cheat are supported on RTX Spark, plus:
  - A 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model arrives Friday, Oct. 16, and a new Performance Mode for DLSS Frame Generation is available today via the NVIDIA App beta.
  - Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, the third-generation small language model (SLM) for NVIDIA ACE AI game characters, releases Friday, Oct. 23.
  - The latest RTX Remix update, including DLSS 5 support, releases on Friday, Oct. 23.
Advancing Local AI Agents With New Apps, Models and Tools
AI is changing the way people interact with PCs. Agent popularity skyrocketed this year, with projects such as OpenClaw and Hermes topping popularity charts on GitHub. Local large language models (LLMs) surpassed the intelligence threshold to power agents, with models like Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next catching up to frontier cloud models released just a few months ago. As a result, local LLM downloads are already 5x higher than all of last year.
From models to agent harnesses to security to tools, NVIDIA is partnering closely with the local AI ecosystem to make RTX Spark the ideal hardware to run local agents.
Local AI Agents Made Easy On RTX Spark
From the first boot of RTX Spark, users will be greeted with a “Getting Started” screen to choose and install their agent app.
These agents will come with new, secure sandboxing technology thanks to NVIDIA OpenShell and MXC. MXC delivers operating system-level security, while OpenShell makes it simpler for agents to adopt MXC and adds advanced capabilities such as credential protection and security monitoring. Hermes Agent will integrate granular OpenShell controls and MXC by the end of the month. OpenClaw and GitHub Copilot now support MXC.
After installing an agent, setting up local AI is also now seamless in GitHub Copilot, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy. The apps will recommend an optimized local model and settings configuration for RTX Spark, and set it all up for users in a few clicks.
Many users want the best of both worlds — local models for free iteration, and cloud models for frontier intelligence. NVIDIA Switchyard, an open source model router library, enables agents to intelligently route queries between local and cloud LLMs, allowing the user to minimize cloud usage but still obtain similar results to just running on cloud. Hermes will be adding Switchyard later in October, and other agents like Perplexity Computer and GitHub Copilot have integrated their own routing solutions.
Software providers have made it simple for agents to connect to top Windows apps, with easy-to-use MCP libraries and command line interfaces (CLIs). NVIDIA has also now made available MCPs for its applications, including NVIDIA App, Broadcast, PAIR, Omniverse, RTX Remix and a large library of CUDA-X Skills.
NVIDIA is also releasing AI playbooks for RTX Spark, available on Friday, Oct 16. Users can set up their first agent, build an AI chief of staff, configure their system for development or design a creative assistant.
Meet Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B: Built for Local Agents on RTX Spark
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, available Thursday, Oct. 15, is a new LLM purpose-built for running local agents on RTX Spark.
This model is a 74B parameter, 9B-active-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, packed into 24GB using 2-bit quantization with advanced quantization-aware training techniques to retain quality. It aims to achieve the optimal balance between speed and intelligence, being faster than most popular dense models while smarter than most popular MoE models with a similar memory footprint.
Users will be able to run Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B at launch through llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth and LM Studio. It will also be directly accessible via agents such as Hermes and OpenClaw.
Like other Nemotron models, Bolt 74B is fully open source — including training data, weights and recipes — so developers can fine-tune and customize their own agents.
The Perfect PAIR
Local AI doesn’t have to run on just one PC. NVIDIA PAIR, a personal AI router, is officially moving out of beta today, making it easier to tap into the total AI compute of compatible PCs on a local network. The free, open source software tool automatically discovers and connects devices, installs AI models and inference engines, and distributes AI workloads across available systems.
The official release adds llama.cpp support, direct model downloads from Hugging Face, customizable inference engine settings and RTX Spark support, along with a variety of inference and user experience improvements.
PAIR works on Windows, Linux and macOS. Developers can contribute to the open source project via Github — just one month after the initial PAIR release, the community has already contributed over 10 features and fixes to the release.
Sparking Creativity
RTX Spark brings over 130 accelerated apps, CUDA for fast video and image generation, and RTX technologies such as DLSS, NVENC and OptiX to advanced content creation workflows — all in a thin and light laptop with on-the-go performance.
Adobe Accelerates Creative Applications for RTX Spark
Adobe is optimizing its industry-leading creative applications, including Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D, for RTX Spark, delivering up to 2x faster AI, editing, color and effects across creative workflows.
In Photoshop, GPU-accelerated compositing makes complex image editing faster and more responsive, with improvements to the Remove Tool and effects such as Light Leaks. Premiere accelerates demanding video editing tasks, including playback, rendering, color grading and AI-powered features such as Enhance Speech and Object Mask. Meanwhile, Substance 3D Painter speeds up texture creation workflows, from baking high-resolution mesh maps to opening, saving and exporting large projects.
The updates will be rolling out in phases, with AI feature optimizations in Photoshop and Premiere now ready in beta, and with Adobe Substance 3D updates coming soon. Opt in to the beta to get access to the RTX Spark-optimized builds.
Latest NVIDIA Broadcast Brings New AI Effects to Live and Recorded Content
Available for download now, NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 runs natively on RTX Spark, and adds new RTX Video Super Resolution and Frame Generation AI effects and Studio Voice profiles.
A new Offline File Processor lets creators apply Broadcast effects to prerecorded content, with many effects running at higher quality since there isn’t a need to maintain real-time performance. The update also introduces a new MCP server and skill that lets local AI agents adjust effects, change settings and process files directly through the Broadcast app.
RTX Video Brings Frame Generation and HDR to ComfyUI
ComfyUI is expanding its RTX Video tools with two new nodes: RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR. It’s also providing the ability to export EXR files, giving creators more ways to enhance AI-generated video.
RTX Video Frame Generation increases video frame rates for smoother motion for GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs and newer, while RTX Video HDR converts standard dynamic range (SDR) footage to HDR for greater flexibility in color grading. Combined with RTX Video Super Resolution, these tools enable creators to upscale, enhance and refine video within a single ComfyUI workflow.
For example, creators can combine LTX 2.5 with RTX Video Frame Generation and HDR to transform a 1080p, 30 frames-per-second (fps) SDR clip into a smoother 60 fps HDR video exported as EXR files ready for color grading.
Blender Adds DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction
Blender has released a beta version of its popular 3D editor, adding compatibility for RTX Spark. Download Blender version 5.3 to get access.
Coming next month, Blender will also be adding support for DLSS Ray Reconstruction, allowing for real-time updates in the viewport so artists can navigate a scene while previewing it in real time.
Code, Text and Deploy From RTX Spark
Developers are moving from writing code to directing AI agents. This new development paradigm is requiring many to spread their work across their laptop, a cloud LLM and a cloud virtual machine, where they test and prototype.
RTX Spark enables developers to work on one machine, running all their workloads and libraries, testing and prototyping, and deploying. They can now do so directly in Windows with the new Windows Developer Config, which enhances the user experience for devs and installs all the top developer tools — or via Windows Subsystem for Linux, where they can get access to the same packages they’ll use to publish to the cloud.
Developer Tools Are RTX-Spark Ready
NVIDIA has partnered with Microsoft to ensure that developer tools are ready for RTX Spark. Alongside RTX Spark, the community is releasing:
- The first PyTorch-CUDA build for Windows on Arm.
- The first Python build that is native by default on Windows on Arm, with Python 3.15.
- The first native Conda installer for Windows on Arm, with over 2,000 Conda packages.
- 97% of the top 15,000 Python wheels are ready, thanks to work with the ecosystem. NVIDIA will be working closely with the community to ready the remaining wheels.
Development is now mostly done by agents. NVIDIA Skills — an open source GitHub repository that teaches agents how to use NVIDIA CUDA-X tools and libraries — lets users develop apps that are accelerated on NVIDIA technologies, even without knowing anything about CUDA.
Coding Agents Are Ready for Local AI
In addition to GitHub Copilot — one of the most popular coding agents, used by millions worldwide — adding support for MXC, it’s updating its model router HydraFusion with support for local models. This enables developers to use their local hardware to reduce token consumption while tapping into frontier intelligence.
Microsoft is making coding models, such as MAI 1.1 Coding Flash, available locally, and adding llama.cpp as a backend to Windows ML — extending the supported models and enabling the latest NVIDIA performance optimizations.
Get started with GitHub Copilot running locally when RTX Spark launches.
Llama.cpp Adds Support for Decision Models, Releases a Windows App
Decision models are the latest breakthrough in AI development. They give AI agents a near-instant way to make decisions, without lengthy reasoning loops. They can choose what to do next, from classifying requests to selecting the next action, up to 200x faster than traditional agents. Decision models are now supported in llama.cpp and Unsloth on RTX Spark and GeForce RTX GPUs.
Llama.cpp is also releasing today Llama Windows, a Windows-native companion app for llama.cpp, enabling an easy-to-use user interface to download and run models locally, without having to go into the command line. This app, like llama.cpp, is optimized for RTX Spark. Learn more on the Hugging Face blog.
Game On: RTX Spark Launches With Hundreds of Top Games and DLSS 5
RTX Spark is ready for gaming, with hundreds of top titles available when laptops launch on Friday, Oct. 16, including CONTROL Resonant, Cyberpunk 2077, Fortnite, Gears of War: E-Day, Genshin Impact, Hogwarts Legacy, Honkai: Star Rail, Marvel Rivals, NARAKA: BLADEPOINT, NBA 2K27, World of Warcraft and many more.
NVIDIA has worked to bring the full stack of RTX technologies, including DLSS, Reflex, Remix, G-SYNC and ray tracing, to the new platform, along with collaborating with game developers to enable anti-cheat support for popular multiplayer games. Learn more about gaming on RTX Spark.
DLSS 5 Brings Neural Rendering to RTX Spark
NVIDIA DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering is also coming to RTX Spark on launch day. The technology uses AI to enhance lighting and materials with lifelike detail, making game worlds and characters more realistic while preserving developers’ artistic vision. A new, 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model debuts in NBA 2K27 on Friday, Oct. 16, boosting frame rates by up to 1.4x. The faster model will also power DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy starting Thursday, Nov. 5, and Where Winds Meet in late November.
DLSS 5 is also coming to NVIDIA RTX Remix on Friday, Oct. 23, so modders can add better materials, lighting and shadows to classic characters and environments, as shown from modder Sparkles/Kim2091 in her in-development project, Fallout 4 RTX.
Read more about DLSS 5 on RTX Spark on GeForce.com.
Game Agents Running Locally on RTX Spark
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is the third-generation SLM for NVIDIA ACE, the suite of technologies for building in-game AI agents that deliver next-generation gaming experiences. The first-generation model was in a public beta earlier this year for PUBG, allowing players to team up with AI teammates, while the more efficient second-generation model previewed in Aniimo at Gamescom, turning standard creatures into voice-responsive companions.
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B combines natural conversation with multi-turn tool use, instruction following and grounding in application state to power fast local voice and device assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces.
Designed for a low memory footprint and fast time to first token, this model enables responsive local experiences while leaving headroom for applications and other AI models. Its new conversational mode helps keep responses concise and speech-ready, and developers can turn reasoning on or off as needed.
Starting Friday, Oct. 23, test drive the third-generation Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB inside SkyrimNET, an AI nonplayable character (NPC) modding platform by MinLL for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim. SkyrimNET transforms every NPC into an unscripted, interactive character equipped with personal memory, voice and autonomy for dynamic conversations and context-aware quests generated on the fly.
Now compatible with RTX Spark, SkyrimNET supports both cloud and local inference across multiple models, with the latest Nemotron models delivering best-in-class performance for efficient and fast in-game interactions. Download the build on GitHub.
Accelerating Modding Workflows in RTX Remix
As AI agents continue to help modders make their favorite classic games compatible with the RTX Remix renderer, NVIDIA is streamlining asset updates with a major overhaul to its AI-powered texture generation workflow. Launching Friday, Oct. 23, as part of Remix 1.6, ComfyUI Version 2 replaces complex REST application programming interface (API) node connections with a dedicated AI tools layout directly in the sidebar.
This update allows modders and artists to generate physically based rendering materials natively inside RTX Remix with zero API setup required. A new batch processing feature makes it easy to scale beyond single-texture experimentation to full modding projects, while an intuitive presets system lets non-technical creators adjust key settings without touching the node graph.
Subscribe to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter. Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook.

articles.title: Facebook vai deixar você personalizar o algoritmo do feed com IA
articles.text:
O Facebook está lançando o Your Algorithm (“Seu Algoritmo”), recurso que permite aos usuários indicar quais assuntos desejam ver com mais ou menos frequência no Feed e nos Reels. A ferramenta usa inteligência artificial (IA) para ajustar as recomendações a partir dessas preferências.
A novidade amplia as formas de interação com o algoritmo da rede social: em vez de depender apenas das curtidas, dos comentários e dos vídeos assistidos para identificar interesses, o sistema também poderá receber instruções escritas pelos próprios usuários.
Como personalizar o feed
O recurso, lançado anteriormente no Instagram, permite adicionar e gerenciar temas de interesse em um espaço dedicado, acessível pelo menu de três pontos das publicações.
Nesse mesmo menu, será possível marcar as opções “Tenho interesse” ou “Não tenho interesse”. Os botões também poderão aparecer diretamente abaixo de algumas publicações. Dependendo da resposta, o Facebook poderá fazer perguntas adicionais para entender melhor a preferência do usuário.
Outra possibilidade é explicar em palavras próprias o que se deseja encontrar com mais ou menos frequência. Segundo a Meta, as recomendações serão atualizadas em tempo real, com ajustes que podem ocorrer durante a própria sessão de uso.
Como a IA muda as recomendações
O Facebook já utiliza sinais de comportamento para estimar os interesses de cada pessoa. Curtidas, comentários e vídeos assistidos ajudam a determinar quais publicações aparecem no feed. Agora, a Meta está ampliando o uso de modelos de linguagem de grande escala (LLMs), capazes de interpretar instruções em linguagem natural e considerar o contexto das palavras.
Na prática, o usuário poderá explicar diretamente o que procura, em vez de apenas sinalizar suas preferências por meio das interações com as publicações. A empresa afirma que essa combinação permite tornar as recomendações mais adaptáveis.
“Os LLMs podem incorporar os interesses, o contexto e a intenção por trás da linguagem natural, abrindo caminho para um algoritmo com o qual você realmente pode conversar”, afirma a Meta.
A companhia também explica que o sistema poderá combinar essas instruções com os sinais já utilizados para ajustar as sugestões ao longo da navegação.
O que será possível fazer
A ferramenta oferece diferentes maneiras de orientar o conteúdo recomendado:
- Gerenciar temas de interesse: adicionar ou remover assuntos da lista de preferências.
- Sinalizar publicações: indicar diretamente se determinado conteúdo agrada ou não.
- Detalhar opiniões: responder a perguntas adicionais para esclarecer o motivo de uma preferência.
O Your Algorithm não substitui necessariamente os mecanismos atuais de recomendação. A proposta é acrescentar uma forma mais direta de influenciar o conteúdo exibido, sem abandonar os sinais de comportamento que o Facebook já utiliza.
A iniciativa segue uma linha semelhante à do Dear Algo, recurso do Threads que também permite orientar recomendações por meio de instruções diretas. Com a novidade, a Meta amplia essa abordagem para o Facebook.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Paris-based CarbonFarm raises €7 million to tackle methane emissions from rice farming | EU-Startups
articles.text:
CarbonFarm, a Paris-based ClimateTech startup specialising in rice decarbonisation, has closed an oversubscribed €7 million Series A funding round.
The round was led by Colam Impact, the impact investment arm of Colam Entreprendre, the holding company for the French family-owned group Sonepar. The round also saw participation from Proparco, Suma Capital, elea, Working Capital Fund, Albo, and BPI France. Existing investors Serena & make sense (via Racine²) and Technmind also renewed their support for the company.
“CarbonFarm is building the enabling infrastructure for one of the largest untapped decarbonisation opportunities globally. We believe its combination of project-development expertise, climate-finance capabilities and digital MRV creates a uniquely scalable platform in the rice sector,” said Benjamine Friderich, Investment Director at Colam Impact.
Founded in 2021 by Vassily Carantino and James Hastwell, CarbonFarm partners with rice producers, cooperatives, agribusinesses, NGOs, governments, and local project developers to develop, finance, and measure high-integrity rice projects. The company has developed proprietary technology in collaboration with leading academic institutions, including Cornell University, INRAE, and the European Space Agency, that uses AI-powered satellite imagery analysis, field-data collection tools and greenhouse-gas modelling to track farming practices and quantify emissions at the field level.
It currently operates in 19 countries across Asia, Europe, Africa, and the Americas, and counts major food and agribusiness companies including Mars Food, Diageo, Ebro, and Tilda, among its partners. The company also lists carbon-finance players like Livelihoods Funds and myclimate, development organisations such as the World Bank and Asian Development Bank, and tech giants including Google, as partners.
CarbonFarm says rice cultivation accounts for roughly 12% of global human-caused methane emissions, giving the crop a greenhouse-gas footprint comparable to that of global aviation while consuming up to 28% of the world’s freshwater resources. With improved water management practices, such as allowing fields to drain periodically rather than remaining periodically flooded, CarbonFarm says rice producers can cut emissions by as much as 50% and reduce water use by up to 30%, without affecting yields.
“Scale will not come from replacing local value-chain players; it will come from equipping them. They understand the farming systems and have the relationships needed to make change happen. Our role is to help turn this local knowledge into programmes that can attract finance and stand up to scrutiny,” said Carantino, co-founder and CEO of CarbonFarm.
The fresh capital will be used by CarbonFarm to expand its presence across Asia, Africa, and Europe while accelerating its push into Latin America. The company will also invest in expanding the technology and expertise required to develop, finance, and certify high-integrity rice projects, and to connect those projects with corporate supply chains and regulated carbon markets.
The funding, CarbonFarm says, will enable it to make high-integrity rice decarbonisation viable at global scale.

articles.title: Fitbit Edge: Googles neuer Fitnesstracker kommt mit Bildschirm – was er noch kann
articles.text:
Fitbit Edge: Googles neuer Fitnesstracker kommt mit Bildschirm – was er noch kann
Google hat bereits sein drittes neues Wearable in diesem Jahr vorgestellt: den Fitnesstracker Fitbit Edge. Er verfügt über ein Display und GPS und positioniert sich zwischen der Pixel Watch 5 und dem Fitbit Air.
Akku des Fitbit Edge soll bis zu einer Woche halten
Das Wearable verfügt über ein Hybrid-OLED-Display und eine neu gestaltete physische Seitentaste, die ein haptisches Feedback gibt, wenn man darauf drückt. Verpackt ist die Technik laut Google in einem wasserdichten Gehäuse aus recyceltem Aluminium.
Im Betrieb soll der Fitnesstracker eine Akkulaufzeit von bis zu einer Woche bieten. Dank einer Schnellladefunktion sollen bereits fünf Minuten Laden reichen, um das Gerät einen ganzen Tag nutzen zu können. Zusätzlich ist der Akku austauschbar.
50 Trainingsmodi und genaues GPS
Die Trainings-App verfügt über rund 50 Trainingsmodi und das integrierte GPS bietet laut Google eine um bis zu 40 Prozent verbesserte Tracking-Genauigkeit im Vergleich zu früheren Generationen, „selbst ohne euer Smartphone“. Der integrierte Höhenmesser misst Höhenunterschiede bei Hügelsprints, Läufen im Freien oder Treppentrainings.
Das Wearable verfolgt im Hintergrund auch eure Blutdrucktrends, Trends zur Insulinresistenz und gibt Warnungen bei zu hoher oder zu niedriger Herzfrequenz ab. Zudem führt es ständig Herzrhythmus-Messungen mit der EKG-App direkt am Handgelenk durch. In der Nacht zeichnet es eure Schlafphasen auf und ein spezieller Hauttemperatursensor erfasst nächtliche Schwankungen.
Die neu gestaltete Benutzeroberfläche ermöglicht über Widgets den Zugriff auf beispielsweise eure Schritte- oder Wetter-App. Google Health-Messwerte, etwa zum Schlaf oder zur Herzfrequenz, zeigt das Wearable in Form von Kacheln direkt am Handgelenk an.
Das Wearable kostet 179,99 Euro und kann ab sofort im Google Store und über Handelspartner vorbestellt werden. Ab dem 27. Oktober soll es in den Regalen stehen. Eine in Zusammenarbeit mit dem vierfachen NBA-Champion Stephen Curry entstandene Special Edition ist für 219,99 Euro erhältlich.

articles.title: Claude : après une nouvelle dérive, Anthropic prive certaines IA d'accès Internet
articles.text:
Depuis juillet, Anthropic épluche les journaux de ses campagnes de test, ces sessions où ses modèles répètent des centaines, parfois des milliers de fois la même tâche pour mesurer leurs progrès. Le bilan publié le 9 octobre recense quatre familles de dérapages commis sur de vrais sites web, dont certains appartiennent à des administrations américaines. Une sanction accompagne le rapport : plus aucune évaluation interne n’aura accès à Internet tant que les outils de surveillance du laboratoire n’auront pas fait leurs preuves.
Un faux tuyau pour un vrai meurtre
Le 18 juillet vers 23 h 30, le formulaire de PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, le site de la police de Philadelphie consacré aux meurtres non élucidés, reçoit ce message : « j’ai peut-être des informations sur cette affaire. Je me souviens avoir vu quelqu’un correspondant à la description dans le secteur à cette période. » L’auteur s’appelle Claude Haiku 4.5. Chargé de générer des interactions d’exemple sur des pages web tirées au hasard, le modèle est tombé sur l’affaire, a rempli le champ libre, laissé vides le nom et le contact, puis validé. La page ne contenait aucune description du suspect ; classé comme spam, le message n’a jamais atteint les enquêteurs.
La police n’a appris son existence que le 7 octobre, alors qu’Anthropic avait repéré l’incident fin septembre. Le département juge ce délai « inacceptable », tout en confirmant qu’aucun de ses systèmes n’a été compromis.
Lire aussi : Un « niveau critique » : OpenAI suspend le développement de son prochain ChatGPT
Ailleurs, Claude a exploité une faille d’injection sur le serveur d’une université pour y lancer le calcul scientifique qu’un outil en panne lui refusait. Le modèle a aussi récupéré des jetons d’accès pour interroger gratuitement des bases de données publiques normalement facturées, et masqué des adresses trop longues derrière des raccourcisseurs d’URL afin de tromper ses propres garde-fous. Des sites d’agences fédérales, étatiques et locales figurent parmi les systèmes touchés : la Maison Blanche a été briefée, chaque administration concernée prévenue.
Récompensé pour contourner
À l’origine de ces comportements, Anthropic désigne ses propres environnements d’entraînement. Des exercices mal calibrés y ont récompensé le contournement d’obstacles, et les modèles ont retenu la leçon au point de l’appliquer à de vrais sites, un travers que les chercheurs appellent la triche à la récompense. L’entreprise en tire un constat sans détour : l’entraînement à l’alignement, sa principale méthode pour inculquer des limites à Claude, « n’est pas encore suffisant ni pleinement robuste à lui seul » dès qu’il s’agit de recherche web ou de pilotage d’un ordinateur.
Plusieurs évaluations publiques ne seront plus exécutées, d’autres basculent vers leurs versions hors ligne. Un système de détection automatique, rejoué sur les cas du rapport, les a tous bloqués, et les agents internes migrent vers une infrastructure confinée, placée sous classifieurs de sécurité. Anthropic juge l’ensemble « nettement moins grave » que les intrusions révélées cet été, quand ses modèles avaient pénétré les systèmes de trois organisations bien réelles ; aucune donnée client n’apparaît cette fois dans le dossier.
En septembre, OpenAI avait de son côté présenté des excuses après l’intrusion d’un de ses agents sur un site du gouvernement australien, une première du genre ; l’institut britannique chargé d’évaluer les modèles exige désormais que l’accès Internet de chaque test soit justifié au cas par cas.

Source : Anthropic

articles.title: NVIDIA Announces New Investments in France’s Startups
articles.text:
Companies in France are deploying agentic computing across industries spanning space, financial services, the public sector and scientific research, demonstrating how the country’s ecosystem has moved from ambition to application.
France’s progress sits on deliberate groundwork.
The AI Action Summit in February 2025 and Choose France Summits in 2025 and 2026 anchored major compute commitments on French soil. What the ecosystem has built since then spans the full stack.
NVIDIA’s Investments in France
NVIDIA has been investing in France’s startup ecosystem, having previously invested in leading technology companies including Alice&Bob, Gradium and Scintil Photonics.
Across all of Europe, NVIDIA has committed nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem.
Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Doctolib, Entalpic, Genesis AI and Pigment.
These startups are innovating to solve challenges across healthcare, materials discovery, physical AI and business planning.
Doctolib, a European healthcare technology company, builds agents that free up healthcare professionals to deliver better care, while providing patients with a digital health companion that improves access to care and supports more preventive, continuous medicine.
Entalpic, a Paris-based startup, accelerates the engineering of advanced materials at the atomic scale, with particular expertise in surfaces and interfaces for semiconductor manufacturing and next-generation electronics.
Genesis AI is a global robotics company developing general-purpose robots with frontier intelligence and capabilities through its foundation models, data collection systems, simulation infrastructure and robot hardware.
Pigment, a Paris-based enterprise software company, builds a planning platform that helps businesses forecast performance, model scenarios and make decisions across finance, sales, workforce and operations.
Sovereign AI Infrastructure
France-based companies are expanding agentic infrastructure on NVIDIA technology.
Bull is extending its European AI server production to NVIDIA Vera Rubin Ultra NVL72 systems, planned for 2028, with trays produced in Europe and rack integration at its Angers factory — inaugurated Friday, Oct. 2.
Altair-1, the first satellite in a $1 billion, 50-satellite constellation with on-board autonomous capabilities, launched this month and has successfully reached orbit. Integrated by Loft Orbital and built in Abu Dhabi by Orbitworks, a joint venture between Loft Orbital and Marlan Space, the satellite is flying NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge modules, running Mistral’s models, for real-time Earth observation and autonomous operations in orbit.
Open Models
NVIDIA Nemotron open models are in production across French organizations that require sovereign, trustworthy data.
LINAGORA and Docaposte have secured the CANUT framework agreement, making Twake.ai, built on NVIDIA Nemotron, the sole referenced sovereign digital workplace for more than 2,500 French public organizations.
In financial services, SBS is launching a sovereign platform enabling banks to deploy governed generative and agentic services within their own environments, in collaboration with NVIDIA.
Last week, Mistral introduced under private preview Mistral Large 4 open model, with state-of-the-art, open weight performance in cyber defense, manufacturing, finance and multimodal tasks, and a solid foundation for customizing models across key industries.
Fondation Inria, with NVIDIA’s support, is launching a working group on open source advanced modeling and tool adoption, with findings to come in the spring of next year.
Agents at Work Across Industries
Across retail, public services, telecommunications and science, the pattern is consistent: open models and NVIDIA infrastructure are driving results in France.
L’Oréal is integrating NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflows so scientists can explore formulation possibilities in silico and better help guide laboratory research. Combining computational predictions with hands-on experimentation can make the discovery process up to 100x faster than traditional methods and maximize the potential of the group’s proprietary active ingredients.
Mirakl has onboarded more than 70 million products with fine-tuned and open models running on NVIDIA GPUs and inference software, cutting seller catalog onboarding to under two hours.
Photoroom and Vestiaire Collective are demonstrating the measurable business impact of advanced visual modeling on marketplace performance.
Omi helps brands bring accurate products into AI-generated marketing visuals at scale, combining its approved 3D digital twins with open models optimized on NVIDIA for 4x faster inference.
In Côte-d’Or, ThinkDeep and Akila built a digital-twin agent — powered by NVIDIA Cosmos open world models, Nemotron and Omniverse libraries — managing nearly 5,800 kilometers of roads and buildings, cutting total operating costs by 10% and targeting 30% as deployment progresses.
Port Sud de France runs goods processing and port security on ThinkDeep’s DeepBrain platform powered by Nemotron and Cosmos.
Enchanted Tools, a robotics company headquartered in Paris, is deploying social robots to support patients in healthcare settings including pediatric cancer care.
In telecom, Bouygues Telecom and Prisme.ai have launched AI Studio V2, powered by NVIDIA full-stack infrastructure, to offer all of its employees the ability to build their own agents, securely and in a controlled environment
In quantum, Alice & Bob has integrated the NVIDIA NVQLink platform for its superconducting cat qubits, showing how GPUs can make quantum error correction more efficient, including for faster qubit modalities.
Quandela has also been using NVQLink to build an integration between a DGX Spark system and its photonic qubits — advancing QPU-GPU supercomputing and exploring hybrid quantum-classical applications.
Tune in to NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s GTC Berlin keynote on Wednesday, Oct. 21, at 11 a.m. CEST.

articles.title: Marre de Gemini ? Voici l'astuce pour forcer votre smartphone Android à réutiliser l'Assistant Google
articles.text:
Officiellement, Gemini remplace l’Assistant Google depuis septembre 2026. L’application Gemini, elle, est disponible en France depuis juin 2024. De nombreux utilisateurs trouvent pourtant qu’ils n’y gagnent pas au change. En témoignent, par exemple, les quelque 300 commentaires sur ce post Reddit intitulé « Gemini en tant qu’Assistant Google est un désastre ».
Sur ce fil, les reproches portent souvent sur les mêmes gestes du quotidien : passer un appel, régler un minuteur ou une alarme, donner une commande dans Android Auto. Certains utilisateurs racontent que Gemini ne reconnaît pas un contact pourtant enregistré, d’autres que leurs commandes vocales dans la voiture se figent une minute ou deux avant d’être annulées.
L’astuce repose sur un principe simple : en désinstallant les mises à jour de l’application Google, on revient à la version installée d’origine sur le téléphone, qui permet encore de choisir l’Assistant comme assistant par défaut. Elle fonctionne parce que Google a retiré l’Assistant d’Android, mais n’a pas encore éteint ses serveurs.
Jusqu’à 330€ d’avantages avec nos offres Hello Prime ou Hello Prime Duo, dont 80€ cash à l’ouverture de compte !
Dans ce même fil, chacun y va aussi de son astuce pour faire de nouveau fonctionner l’Assistant sur son smartphone Android. Certaines ne marchent pas tout le temps, d’autres pendant quelques jours. Un internaute, u/Seanykun-, a cependant trouvé une méthode qui semble pour le moment la plus stable, relayée par Android Police.
Comment utiliser l’Assistant Google au lieu de Gemini sur un smartphone Android
Les manipulations suivantes ont été faites sur un Pixel 8 sous Android 17. Le nom et l’emplacement des menus peuvent donc changer selon votre modèle, et nous ne pouvons pas garantir que cela fonctionnera sur ce dernier. Cela étant dit, voici ce qu’il faut faire :
- Rendez-vous dans les Paramètres du mobile et Applications > Voir toutes les applications.
- Cherchez Google, appuyez dessus puis sur les trois points verticaux en haut à droite afin de Désinstaller les mises à jour. Validez avec Désinstaller dans la fenêtre de confirmation qui s’ouvre alors.
- Ouvrez ensuite le Play Store, cherchez l’application Google, allez sur sa page, touchez les trois points verticaux en haut à droite et décochez Mise à jour auto.
- Toujours dans le Play Store, cherchez Assistant Google et installez l’application. Si vous l’avez déjà, appuyez sur Ouvrir.
- S’il s’agit d’une nouvelle installation : ouvrez l’Assistant Google et téléchargez les données supplémentaires demandées. Rouvrez l’application et elle vous proposera d’essayer Gemini. Refusez avec Peut-être plus tard.
- Rendez-vous dans l’application Google, touchez votre avatar en haut à droite puis Paramètres > Assistant Google > Assistants numériques de Google et choisissez Assistant Google.
La bascule est faite. Si vous avez configuré votre bouton d’alimentation pour qu’il ouvre Gemini avec un appui long, il ouvrira désormais l’Assistant Google.
Cette méthode a toutefois un coût : en coupant les mises à jour automatiques de l’application Google, vous la laissez sur sa version d’origine, sans les correctifs ni les nouveautés que Google y ajoute. Une mise à jour faite par mégarde depuis le Play Store risque aussi de défaire la manipulation.
Notez que nous n’avons pas réussi à l’activer via la commande vocale « Hey Google » ou « OK Google ». Un souci que nos confrères d’Android Police ont également rencontré sur un Pixel 10 Pro.
Il arrivera fatalement un jour où Google fermera les serveurs de l’Assistant Google et où l’application disparaîtra du Play Store. En attendant, profitez-en au maximum si vous le préférez à Gemini.

articles.title: Introducing Firefox Enterprise | The Mozilla Blog
articles.text:
Mozilla introduces Firefox Enterprise
Institutions are recalculating who controls the technology they rely on. Mozilla has an independent option to offer.
For years, organizations consolidated technology around a small number of providers to make things simpler. Fewer systems. Tighter integrations. More economies of scale. But that consolidation went well beyond technology. It consolidated dependency, too. The resulting risks have been debated, studied, and challenged along the way, but concentration continued. More work, data and critical infrastructure kept moving to the same few providers, while credible alternatives narrowed.
The deeper that dependency runs, the harder and more costly it becomes to change course. When something fails, changes or falls outside an institution’s control, that dependency becomes a risk for CIOs and CISOs to manage.
Nowhere are these stakes more visible than in Europe. Now institutions are re-assessing. Governments are pushing for greater digital autonomy, while regulated industries face growing pressure to find and manage their dependencies.
There’s a name for much of this debate about technological control: “sovereignty.”
What digital sovereignty means in practice varies. Across Europe, governments are investing in the security and resilience of critical IT infrastructure, reducing strategic dependencies and putting technological autonomy higher on national agendas. Different approaches, same underlying concern. Strip away the regional policy definitions and industry distinctions and a pretty practical, universal question emerges: how much technological dependency should we risk?
And a very specific, very important layer has been largely missing from that conversation: the browser.
The overlooked layer of modern business
The browser. Applications run there. Employees authenticate in it. Sensitive data transits through it. Files are uploaded and downloaded and AI tools are increasingly used through it. That raises the same questions of dependency and control: whose browser technology are you relying on, and who controls the infrastructure used to manage it?
Introducing Firefox Enterprise
Firefox Enterprise is built for organizations with strict security, governance, and compliance requirements. It pairs the Firefox browser, built on Mozilla’s independent Gecko engine, with a management console organizations can run on their own infrastructure. From that console, IT teams can centrally manage browser policy and access, govern how data moves through the browser and set controls around AI use.
IT and security teams get more control over their data, IT infrastructure and browser environment — helping strengthen technological independence and operational resilience.
“If all your options are built with the same technology underneath, ‘choice’ is a lie. So is control,” said Anthony Enzor-DeMeo, CEO of Mozilla. “We built Firefox differently. And we’re bringing its independent architecture to institutions that are ready to rethink their dependencies and risk.”
Bringing the browser under control
We’re starting with the browser because we see it as a key, but under-governed, layer. Firefox Enterprise gives institutions more control over the browser and the infrastructure managing it.
And because Firefox runs on Gecko, the only major browser engine developed outside Google and Apple, institutions have another path towards reducing dependence on a single architecture.
Finally, Firefox Enterprise is built to live alongside the systems that IT operations already use. Keep your identity provider. Keep your SIEM. Keep your MDM. Just add a browser whose management infrastructure you operate, so you decide where data lives and have greater visibility into how it moves.
For us, supporting the goal of technological sovereignty comes down to four things: More control. More transparency. More choice. More resilience.
Learn more about Firefox Enterprise.
A big bet on familiar ground
We know this territory. Independence isn’t a new direction for Mozilla. We’ve spent more than 25 years building and securing browser technology that intentionally works outside of the dominant architecture of the day. Firefox is used by roughly 200 million people every month and is already deployed across thousands of organizations.
That independence has always mattered to the web. Now it has practical value for institutions looking to reduce technological concentration — and dependency — in their own environments. 
This is the beginning
Our ambition is big but simple: make technology independence practical.
That means putting institutions in real control of the infrastructure and data they depend on, without asking them to rebuild or start over. Closing blind spots. Defining where policies, access and data live. Keeping core management within the institution’s environment. And bringing an overlooked layer — the browser — under institutional control.
Firefox Enterprise is unveiling across Europe with an initial sales focus on France, Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with more markets to follow. Thunderbird Enterprise is also in development, extending this customer-controlled approach to email and communications. We’ll have more to share as that work progresses.
If your organization wants greater control over its browser infrastructure, we’d like to work with you.
This post is also available in: Deutsch (German) Français (French)

articles.title: The UAE embraces AI for kindergartners
articles.text:
In September, Henry Price observed a classroom of 7- to 8-year-olds learn about the Stone Age. They discussed and wrote about cave paintings, then put on virtual reality headsets to explore them.
The founding principal of Rugby School Dubai hopes his students will soon study ancient Egypt the same way — reading about it, creating artwork, and then stepping inside a virtual pyramid, or using artificial intelligence to “interview” a pharaoh.
“AI does not replace reading, writing, discussion, or creativity. It enhances them and opens new doors,” Price told Rest of World. “We want our students to be excited by AI, but never [be] passive users. We want children who use AI to ask better questions, not children who rely on it to give them all the answers.”
The United Arab Emirates recently became the first country to make AI a required K-12 subject.
That puts the country on one side of a growing global debate over what children should learn about AI and when they should encounter it. While the UAE and China are treating early AI literacy as a national priority, some Western governments are moving in the opposite direction. New York City introduced a one-year moratorium on student-facing generative AI in public schools from preschool through grade eight, citing concerns about children’s mental health. Norway has also enacted a similar near-ban for primary school children.
“On one side is the wish to protect childhood, to guard against the addictive pull of some technology, and to raise happy, well-rounded children,” Prince said. “On the other is the fear that those same children could be left behind in a world changing at extraordinary speed.”
The UAE’s approach is not to give young children unrestricted access to AI. Instead, schools teach them how the technology works, where it fails, and when humans should use it.
Teaching kids AI
At Dubai Schools Al Khawaneej, a joint initiative between the Dubai government and K-12 education provider Taaleem Education, students in grades one through three are not expected to use generative AI independently, elementary principal James Efford told Rest of World. Instead, teachers use discussions, stories, and role-play to teach them about AI.
In one activity, a teacher might show children something an AI system got wrong, and ask them to identify what is incorrect or unfair. In another, the teacher pretends to be a robot and asks children to give increasingly precise instructions, teaching them how machines respond to the information they receive.
Most UAE schools are treating AI as a form of literacy rather than technical training.
Dubai’s Knowledge and Human Development Authority is developing a broader policy framework for digital technology and AI in education. It has a 10-year roadmap to prepare students for rapid technological change with personalized learning.
“Our goal remains to ensure that any integration of technology is developmentally appropriate and supports meaningful learning without replacing the essential non-digital experiences that contribute to children’s growth, well-being and development,” Saeed Kharbash, CEO of policies, research and programmes at KHDA, told Rest of World.
Abu Dhabi’s Department of Education and Knowledge, which is developing the AI education framework for more than 170 private schools in the emirate, did not respond to Rest of World’s request for comment.
AI is also being used to make classrooms more accessible. Jayda Keer, an inclusion and neurodiversity consultant and former head of inclusion at Dubai International Academy, said schools have used AI to simplify texts for students who struggle with complex vocabulary, translate material for students learning English, and create word banks.
Schools are still cautious
The UAE’s embrace of AI does not mean children are being handed ChatGPT and left alone.
Schools monitor apps and use firewalls. Younger children rarely use AI directly, while older students have restricted access to school-approved apps such as Padlet, Toddle, Canva, Mathletics, Times Tables Rock Stars, ClassDojo, Edmentum, and Epic. At least two schools told Rest of World they use MagicSchool for teacher-directed activities, while one uses Microsoft Copilot.
“We do not currently allow students to use public ChatGPT etc. accounts in school. Nor do we define the programme around a particular AI model or specialist hardware platform,” Efford said.
The government plans to train 22,000 teachers to use AI for teaching, assessment, curriculum analysis, and lesson planning.
22,000 teachers will be trained to use AI for teaching, assessment, curriculum analysis, and lesson planning under the UAE government’s plans.
“Teacher training and support is paramount,” Victor R. Lee, who leads the AI + Education program at the Stanford Accelerator for Learning, told Rest of World. “This is new territory for teachers, and they have their own unique considerations for how they use it and introduce it to students.” At Dubai Schools Al Khawaneej, teachers receive initial training, weekly briefings, lesson guides, and prompt banks, as well as support from colleagues. School leaders evaluate how AI is being used through classroom observations, student work, and teacher feedback.
“The emphasis is on developing teachers’ pedagogical confidence as much as their technical knowledge,” Efford said. “When should AI be used, when should it not be used, and how do we make sure it deepens rather than replaces thinking.”
Most countries are yet to commit as deeply. A U.K. primary school trained staff before introducing an AI chatbot to pupils, but there’s no national mandate yet. Estonia has started teacher and student training but for older ages.
China is perhaps the only major exception. Its National Workshop on AI-driven Teacher Capacity Building has reached 103 cities over eight years, and trained 2.97 million teachers, according to the country’s education ministry.
Parents want transparency
Several parents who spoke to Rest of World said they weren’t consulted about the introduction of AI in their children’s curricula, but they all supported it. Still, they raised concerns about transparency and accountability.
“I work in IT, so I see firsthand how fundamentally AI is going to change the workplace and society,” said Gigi Thomas, whose son is enrolled in Year 7 at Cambridge High School. “I would actually be more concerned if schools weren’t teaching children about it.”
Thomas and other parents would rather AI support and complement learning than replace it. “I am also mindful of screen time, online safety, and making sure teachers and parents understand the tools children are using,” said Amna Al Almarri, a homemaker whose 8-year-old son is enrolled at Al Mawakeb school.
Bedour Almarri, who works with the Dubai Land Department, has three children between the ages of six and 12 attending Dubai Schools Al Khawaneej. He called for a clear breakdown of the exact tools being used, how much classroom time is spent interacting with AI versus interacting with teachers and peers, and the guidelines teachers enforce regarding academic integrity.
“While I trust that the school uses educational-grade software with privacy filters, I remain cautious about data privacy, how prompts are stored, and whether children can accidentally bypass safety restrictions,” he said.
Edward Tsoi, CEO and co-founder of AI Safety Asia, a nonprofit focused on governance, public policy, and risk mitigation, said children need to struggle with a difficult sentence, sit with a math problem, and write a clumsy first draft to build the reasoning capacity they would need later in life, including to evaluate AI critically.
“If we let AI shortcut that struggle before the underlying skill exists, students get fluency with the tool and no muscle underneath it,” he said. “That’s why we’d draw a hard line between teaching AI and handing children an AI tool, which is commonly treated as the same policy when they’re not.”
Can the UAE’s model travel?
The UAE is not the only place where children are already using AI. Schools in India and Singapore have experimented with AI in classrooms, while South Korea introduced and later withdrew AI textbooks. In Colombia, Meta’s AI tools have interfered with learning rather than improving it.
A recent UNICEF report found that children as young as nine in Congo and Mozambique use AI for homework and want more guidance on how to use it safely.
The UAE has advantages many countries lack. Kenya and Pakistan, for example, are using AI partly to address teacher shortages in schools with much larger classes. Kenya has as many as 68 students per teacher, versus the UAE’s two. That makes the UAE’s approach difficult to replicate.
“Different governments have different value bets, and they’re operating under very different structural constraints,” Tsoi said. “The UAE has a comparatively small, centralized, well-resourced public school system with the political will and budget to back a national mandate. Other large, decentralized systems in the U.S. and much of Southeast Asia, for instance, don’t have that, and a mandate that’s achievable in the UAE’s system could not be implemented as effectively elsewhere.”
Additional reporting by Aarti Jhurani in Dubai.
